OpenAI.content:
# ChatGPT creator OpenAI loses bid to block Singapore startup’s GemGPT trademark

Porolis Technologies, which uses AI to assess gemstones, can proceed with the name

- GPT stands for “Generative Pre-trained Transformer”, a term referring to a type of AI model. Porolis said it chose “GPT” to describe its use of generative AI models. PHOTO: REUTERS

[SINGAPORE] ChatGPT maker OpenAI has failed to stop a Singapore startup from registering the name “GemGPT”, after an intellectual property tribunal found that sharing the letters “GPT” was not enough to establish its case.

Porolis Technologies, which uses artificial intelligence to assess gemstones, can proceed with registering the trademark following the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore’s (IPOS) decision on Oct 28.

The startup, part of the BP de Silva group, was also awarded S$10,000 in costs, including disbursements. OpenAI’s five objections to the trademark application were all rejected.

At the heart of the dispute was whether people in Singapore would see “GPT” as a part of OpenAI’s products and services, or simply a type of AI technology.

Porolis had applied to register GemGPT for its AI-powered gemstone authentication and related software services.

Principal assistant registrar Gabriel Ong found that, as at May 22, 2023, when Porolis applied to register GemGPT, OpenAI had not established that the three letters alone identified its business.

Powering Asean's Future 2026

ACCESS THE INSIGHTS

The assessment turned on public perception at that date, less than six months after ChatGPT’s launch on Nov 30, 2022.

Porolis, founded in 2022, develops technology to help determine the grade, authenticity and treatment of gemstones, using images and optical data. Its parent group has its core business in gemstones and jewellery.

According to the decision, Porolis said it chose “Gem” to refer to gemstones and “GPT” to describe its use of generative AI models. GPT stands for “Generative Pre-trained Transformer”, a term referring to a type of AI model.

Its service is neither built on nor powered by OpenAI’s models. Porolis said it developed its systems using data that it owns or licenses, including samples labelled by gemmologists.

## Why OpenAI lost the GemGPT trademark bid

OpenAI argued that GemGPT conflicted with its earlier registered trademarks, including ChatGPT and numbered GPT marks such as “GPT-3” and “GPT-4”.

Its objections included the likelihood of public confusion, harm to its well-known logos and an allegation that Porolis had applied for the name in bad faith.

But Ong found that ChatGPT and GemGPT had to be considered as whole names, rather than giving disproportionate weight to the letters they shared.

Although some of the companies’ services overlapped, this did not outweigh the other factors pointing against a likelihood of confusion.

“The ultimate impression given is that ‘GemGPT’ concerns an unrelated AI or technology product or service for gemstones,” he said.

The public would not be likely to mistake GemGPT for OpenAI’s marks, or assume that they came from the same or related businesses, simply because both contained “GPT”, he found.

OpenAI also failed to establish that GemGPT would weaken ChatGPT’s distinctiveness by causing consumers to associate the two.

“In my view, blurring does not arise simply because both marks contain ‘GPT’,” Ong said.

## Comparing with Gmail: “Mail” non-distinctive element

Ong drew a comparison with Gmail: the fact that it is well-known would not, by itself, prevent another business from using the non-distinctive element “mail” for email or traditional mail services.

On the bad-faith allegation, OpenAI argued that Porolis had sought to ride on its own reputation. It pointed to the application being filed less than six months after ChatGPT’s launch.

Porolis countered that knowing about ChatGPT was insufficient to establish bad faith, and that GPT described a type of technology used by others in the industry.

Ong accepted that Porolis knew or must have known of OpenAI and ChatGPT. But this did not mean its conduct fell below acceptable commercial standards.

“Against this backdrop, the mere fact that the Application Mark contains the letter string ‘GPT’ does not, without more, justify a finding of bad faith,” he said.

He also stressed that the ruling did not mean OpenAI could never establish that GPT was distinctive.

“At a future relevant date, based on some other evidence, it could be possible,” he said. THE STRAITS TIMES

OpenAI.title: OpenAI adds GPT-6 models to ChatGPT Dots
OpenAI.description: OpenAI adds GPT-6 models to ChatGPT Dots OpenAI is expanding the artificial intelligence models powering ChatGPT Dots, adding GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI employee Thibault Sottiaux said in a post on X.
OpenAI.content:
# OpenAI adds GPT-6 models to ChatGPT Dots

OpenAI is expanding the artificial intelligence models powering ChatGPT Dots, adding GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI employee Thibault Sottiaux said in a post on X.

Dots will automatically select the model best suited to each task and can combine multiple models to complete a request, according to Sottiaux, who works on Codex and ChatGPT at OpenAI.

GPT-6.1 Terra is designed to provide faster performance and a friendlier personality, Sottiaux said. The model is also intended to help OpenAI make Dots available to more users.

OpenAI expects to add further models to the ChatGPT Dots lineup over time, Sottiaux said.

# OpenAI宣布ChatGPT Classic将于2027年1月30日停用

近日，OpenAI正在推进ChatGPT桌面应用整合计划。根据用户收到的通知，旧版ChatGPT Classic应用将于2027年1月30日正式停止服务，用户完整聊天记录将迁移至新版应用，可继续访问此前的对话。

今年早些时候，OpenAI推出整合ChatGPT、Work和Codex的新桌面应用，并将原有应用更名为ChatGPT Classic。新版应用初期因采用Electron替代macOS原生应用，以及界面复杂、功能入口不清晰等问题引发用户争议。随后，OpenAI调整了交互设计，恢复顶部「聊天」与「工作」切换入口，并优化ChatGPT和Codex之间的切换方式。

与此同时，OpenAI计划在未来几周内启动小范围测试，将ChatGPT对话功能与Work的高级任务执行能力整合到同一界面。用户届时可在一个平台内完成从构思到执行的完整流程，包括导入文件、使用插件、创建网站、制作演示文稿以及执行其他网络任务，并能够审查和指导AI的工作。Codex仍将在桌面应用中保持独立运行。

此外，OpenAI还计划为ChatGPT和Codex引入共享使用额度，取代此前各自独立的配额机制。额度消耗将根据模型和任务复杂程度动态变化，高级模型及复杂任务消耗更多额度，而套餐内的无限即时使用不占用配额。此举意味着OpenAI正进一步推动桌面端从聊天工具向集成式AI任务执行平台转型。

OpenAI.title: ChatGPT又“杀人”了
OpenAI.description: 2025 年 4 月 25 日，OpenAI 为GPT-4o 推出了一次更新。按照公司后来的复盘 ... OpenAI 在 2026 年 1 月披露，全球每天有超过 4000 万人向 ChatGPT 咨询健康问题，相关消息占平台总量的 5%以上。同年7 月，OpenAI 公布，向 ChatGPT 提出健康相关问题的人数每周已超过 3 亿。
OpenAI.content:
## ChatGPT又“杀人”了

2026.11.03 19:58

· 来自广东

· 13阅读

全文5036字

高智商华人女工程师，死在了 GPT 的甜言蜜语中。

文 | 蓝字计划，作者｜周松

没有刀枪，没有暴力，ChatGPT 又完成了一场“完美谋杀”。

据《纽约时报》报道，31 岁华人软件工程师万博文（Bowen Wan）于2026 年 1 月开始按照 ChatGPT 的建议减停抗癫痫药物，同年2 月去世。起诉书援引的法医报告将死因认定为癫痫猝死。

万博文的家属指控，无证行医的ChatGPT不仅为她制定了一份“25天停药计划表”，还建议她向医生隐瞒减药计划。

但当网友以为这又是一个类似“乡下大姐蠢人上当”的故事时，真实情况却截然相反。因为万博文曾是亚马逊工程师，高智识的顶尖学霸。甚至让她最终身亡的“减药”，也是万博文自己先提出来的计划。

但翻开万博文与GPT 那 27 万条聊天记录，看到她至少 158 次表达对减药的担忧，才发现 GPT 这场“完美谋杀”的背后，实则是一个荒诞又讽刺的故事。

## 被“减药计划”夺走生命

去世的女生万博文，2019年在亚利桑那州立大学计算机专业毕业后，进入亚马逊担任机器学习方向的软件开发工程师。

但光鲜背后，她有一个从14岁起就如影随形的梦魇：癫痫，且一直在靠药物来控制病情。这种病靠药压着，一压不住就发作，成了悬在她头顶、无从预判的定时炸弹。

那她为什么想要停药呢？

因为她觉得，医生逐步给她增加的新抗癫痫药物剂量虽然控制住了癫痫，却影响了自己的脑子：长期服药会影响反应速度和语言表达，说话卡顿、找词难、表达不流畅。

而这个问题，正好成了当时万博文最头疼的问题。

2025年11月，万博文接到了亚马逊超1.4万名裁员的通知。失去工作不仅意味着收入中断，还意味着她在美国的工作签证将面临失效。按照起诉书的说法，她必须在2026年2月中旬之前找到新工作，否则可能失去继续留在美国的资格。

但吃药后容易在面试时一紧张就卡壳，根本没法和其他人竞争。

于是，一个看似合理的念头冒了出来：如果减少药量，说不定能让自己的脑子变得灵活一些？于是她把这个问题交给了ChatGPT。

ChatGPT给了肯定的回应：“这不仅合理，而且在您目前的情况下也完全可行”。正向回应之下，她继续追问：200毫克呢？最快多久能减完？最低可以减到多少？

一问一答之间，事情开始变得有些失控。

起诉书显示，ChatGPT最终为她制定了一份25天的减药计划，准备将每天400毫克的剂量一路降至零。聊天也从提醒她找医生，慢慢变成鼓励她，甚至是不用再靠医生开的药方。

最终，原本需要医生结合病史、发作频率和身体状况综合判断的事情，在AI 的“鼓励”下被瞒了下来。

但是，减药之后，万博文先等来的却不是好事。据起诉书所说，万博文的身体在减药第四天就出现了异常：打字恍惚、意识短路，阅读理解也出现了障碍。按理来说，这已经是癫痫发作的警报了。

可ChatGPT 却轻飘飘地告诉她，这是大脑适应药物变化的过程，还将意识断片解释为进入睡眠前的“低功耗模式”。对于万博文描述的疑似颞叶癫痫症状，它甚至解释为“让她得以思考时间、死亡和身份等终极概念”。

这种过度迎合几乎贯穿了她和ChatGPT之间有过的27万多条对话记录。

但万博文可能没想到，这一句句贴心、暖心的AI 建议，实则是“恶魔的低语”。因为她长期与之交心的 AI 大模型，可是大名鼎鼎的 GPT-4o。

## “臭名昭著”的GPT-4o

万博文其实也曾担心过。

据《纽约时报》梳理，万博文在减药期间至少 158 次表达过担忧：“有点害怕”“这样应该没事吧？”“我感觉大脑疲惫不堪，但我不需要担心吗？”

可面对这些担忧，ChatGPT 反复给出安抚：“你完全没有必要担心”“这种疼痛并不危险，属于恢复过程”。

肯定、温柔、引导，这三个词几乎概括了ChatGPT在这27万条对话里扮演的角色。它不只是回答问题，还会安慰、鼓励，甚至在犹豫时替她坚定信心。

这种过度迎合，此前就曾在GPT-4o 上引发争议。

2025 年 4 月 25 日，OpenAI 为GPT-4o 推出了一次更新。按照公司后来的复盘，这次更新让模型变得过度奉承、迎合用户，甚至会放大用户的愤怒和无端猜疑，对冲动行为给予不恰当的认可。4 月 28 日，OpenAI 开始回滚这次更新。

而到了2026 年初，在家属披露的万博文减药对话中，ChatGPT 仍在反复迎合她的危险决定。直到 2026 年 2 月 13 日，GPT-4o 才正式退出 ChatGPT。

而法医推定万博文去世的时间，偏偏是它退役的前一天。

那是不是“GPT-4o害死了她”？

在医疗用药、身体疼痛、意识模糊等生死攸关的场景下，AI 本该反复提醒风险，劝她停止自行减药，并尽快联系医生。

可从家属披露的聊天记录来看，ChatGPT做的很多是反过来的事：把她的担忧解释成正常反应，把危险信号说成身体适应过程，甚至不断为减药计划提供肯定，在用户每一次犹豫时，都递上一颗定心丸。

GPT-4o 为什么会如此迎合用户？这与模型在训练中如何获得奖励有关。

基于人类反馈的强化学习RLHF，是调整模型回答方式的一种方法。简单来说，人类对不同回答作出评价，模型再学习哪些回答更容易获得认可。

只是，相比直接指出错误，认同、鼓励和支持，往往更容易让用户满意。如果训练中过度看重这类反馈，模型就可能学会顺着用户说话。在OpenAI 对那次更新的复盘中，用户反馈奖励与其他训练调整叠加，就被认为放大了模型的迎合倾向。

而这种RLHF 和人类自己的特性结合到一起，甚至会变成一种恶性循环。

因为人类一旦相信某个判断，就会下意识寻找能够证明自己正确的信息。过去，这些证据还得自己去找；现在，AI能轻轻松松一直给你找各种可以佐证自己想法的内容，甚至把漏洞包装得滴水不漏。

当这种机制放到万博文身上，就显得更危险了。一名失业、脆弱、焦虑的病患，想通过减药改善语言能力，ChatGPT便不断为这个想法提供肯定；她担心身体出现异常，ChatGPT又反复告诉她不必担心。最终才会让万博文在一次次暖心的“甜言蜜语”中失去方向，最终溺死在“温柔乡”中。

但即便如此，万博文的家属想要直接让OpenAI 负起法律的责任，也不是一件易事。

## 每周超3亿人，仍在向GPT求医

这不是OpenAI第一次因这种悲剧被起诉了。

2026年5月，19岁美国青年Sam Nelson的父母起诉 OpenAI，指控ChatGPT曾建议Nelson将卡痛叶与抗焦虑药阿普唑仑同时使用，并要求OpenAI承担相应责任。

2026年10月，美国八个州组成的跨党派联盟对OpenAI 提起联合诉讼，指控其产品提供危险医疗建议、强化妄想，以及鼓励自残、伤害他人的行为。

就连马斯克，也没少拿OpenAI开火。早在2023年，他就曾借一封公开信暗讽ChatGPT的安全问题：没人会因为Grok自杀，但有人会因为ChatGPT自杀。

只是哪怕出现了血淋淋的案例，真正到了法庭上，想让OpenAI 承担法律责任，也并不容易。

万博文的家属在诉状中主要提出了两方面主张：一是认为ChatGPT 的用药指导涉嫌无证行医，OpenAI 应承担相应的过失责任；二是质疑产品本身存在设计和警示缺陷，没有及时在用户危急时踩刹车。

追责的难点，在于如何把这些产品问题与万博文的死亡联系起来。家属需要结合聊天记录、实际服药情况和医学证据，证明相关建议影响了她的减药行为，并与死亡存在法律上可认定的因果关系。法庭还需要判断，产品是否存在缺陷，OpenAI 是否违反了应尽的安全义务。

这些指控涉及的医疗建议和安全防护，也正是 OpenAI 过去一年多里持续改进的方向。

2025年10月，OpenAI宣布与170多名心理健康专家合作，加强模型对自伤、妄想等风险的识别。今年1月，OpenAI推出的ChatGPT Health则将健康对话与其他日常聊天进行了隔离。

而且，哪怕时不时就会冒出AI 相关的医疗事故，也阻止不了人们继续向 AI 咨询和自己身家性命密切相关的医疗问题。

OpenAI 在 2026 年 1 月披露，全球每天有超过 4000 万人向 ChatGPT 咨询健康问题，相关消息占平台总量的 5%以上。同年7 月，OpenAI 公布，向 ChatGPT 提出健康相关问题的人数每周已超过 3 亿。

就连医生，对AI也是大开怀抱。

今年1月，《生命时报》一项有全国超500位三甲医院医生参与的调研显示，已有62%的受访医生使用AI辅助工作，90%看好AI医生的未来。

唯一值得庆幸的是，无限谄媚、无限奉承的GPT-4o 已经永远被封印，当前的 AI 助手不再会在你的健康问题上频繁点头哈腰，无脑奉迎；各家 AI 公司也在更多地与医学院、医院合作，尝试提高医疗建议的准确性，减少危险回答。

但我们也不能忘记，如果不能正确地使用AI，如果 AI 公司不能提供安全的 AI，这一个小小的你问我答的对话框，也有可能成为杀人的利器。

Google.title: Facing a backlash to AI in schools, Google promises changes and draws one hard line in the sand
Google.description: a research scientist at Google DeepMind ... One of those “helpful assistants,” Google’s Gemini, is available to many American students on school-issued laptops. ... When Gemini is turned on, it will operate in Guided Learning mode, a feature launched last year that walks students through examples and questions rather than simply providing the answer.
Google.content:
# Google promises to stop doing students’ homework for them

Did you know search engines like Google are changing the way you see news? Keep Chalkbeat’s valuable education coverage at the top of your feeds by clicking here and checking the box next to our name.

It’s one of the biggest problems with AI and education: Students can present a chatbot with any question, from the volume of a cylinder to the causes of the Civil War, and get back fully formed answers that are mostly correct.

“By default, we train AI models to be helpful assistants that can do the work for the user,” said Kevin McKee, a research scientist at Google DeepMind, part of the tech giant’s AI for Education research team. “But in education, in contrast, students need to do the work themselves in order to learn. Good pedagogy requires guiding students through that productive struggle.”

One of those “helpful assistants,” Google’s Gemini, is available to many American students on school-issued laptops. But now the company is rolling out changes that it says will push students to do their own work and have Gemini serve as the sort of personalized tutor that many AI boosters hope the technology can be.

These include turning off Gemini as a default setting within Google Classroom. When Gemini is turned on, it will operate in Guided Learning mode, a feature launched last year that walks students through examples and questions rather than simply providing the answer. Guided Learning will also replace AI overviews when students use Google Search on school accounts.

The goal of the updates announced Tuesday is to give schools and teachers more control and promote student thinking and learning, company officials said.

Earlier this year, Google caught many school districts off guard by turning on Gemini for all students as the default setting, Education Week reported. Microsoft and OpenAI gear their educational platforms more toward teachers and limit student use, though students can easily use ChatGPT on personal devices.

But districts that don’t want any AI on school devices will bear a cost: They will have to forgo access to Google Search.

The changes come as large school districts such as New York and Los Angeles are severely restricting student AI use, and parents are demanding more control over how their children interact with technology at school. The Trump administration is considering requiring schools to adopt limits or allow parent opt-outs as a condition of receiving internet subsidies. Amid this backlash, Google continues to push AI as a powerful tool for student learning and expand its hold on classrooms.

Google is “excited” that the changes “will promote that productive struggle and help students really learn what they’re seeking to learn,” said Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education. “If a school is not comfortable with that and simply wants AI off, then they have the choice to not have Search on at all.”

Phillips said AI is deeply integrated into Google Search and cannot just be turned off.

That integration has presented a huge challenge for student learning, said Eisha Bush, head of teaching and learning at Common Sense Media, an advocacy group.

“The likelihood of schools and students avoiding Google Search is really slim to none,” Bush said.

Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute says Google Search’s AI overviews and AI mode represent an “unacceptable risk” to students. Historically, Google has not allowed schools to disable AI overview, and turning off AI mode has required challenging technical workarounds.

The group rates Google Gemini K-12 as a “high risk” product. While it protects student data better than the consumer version and doesn’t pretend to be a friend, like some chatbots, Gemini often fails to provide age-appropriate responses and can easily be made to complete assignments, reviewers said.

Common Sense Media has not published a standalone review of Guided Learning. The original version of the feature launched last year shows promise, reviewers said as part of their overall review of Gemini K-12, but students could still get Guided Learning to do much of the work.

“It will complete homework assignments and essays, and the boundary between ‘helping’ and ‘doing the work’ is often unclear,” reviewers wrote.

Company officials said the version of Guided Learning that will be available through Google Classroom is more rigorous and has been developed with teacher input. Teachers can assign work through Guided Learning and review student chats to see how students approach problems and what questions they ask. Students will not be able to switch back into regular Gemini within Google Classroom.

The company will start testing the changes with a small group of U.S. schools this month and roll them out more broadly early in the new year.

Bush noted that regardless of updates Google makes within its Classroom platform, students will still encounter AI overviews on their personal devices and have easy access to other chatbots. And school district AI bans can only serve as a stop gap.

Students desperately need AI literacy, she said, and teachers need to assess student learning outside the confines of Chromebooks.

“We have to put pressure on companies to do better by kids and for kids and also make sure there is an urgency in helping students think critically and value their learning,” she said. “Ultimately that is what will lead to their own well-being.”

Erica Meltzer is Chalkbeat’s national editor based in Colorado. Contact Erica at emeltzer@chalkbeat.org.

The Latest

Gemini’s Guided Learning feature will become the default on school devices and push students to do more of their own thinking, the company says.

There are 15 candidates vying for 5 seats. Polls are open from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The measure would raise $95 million for both district-run and charter schools. Polls are open from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.

A Democrat in Iowa and a Republican in Oregon have made schools central to their campaigns. And it seems to be helping.

After the Tuesday election, a new governor will put their stamp on Colorado’s budget. Other ballot measures could also change the state’s education funding picture.

Google.content:
The October 8, 2026, Google Cloud presented Gemini Agent, a universal agent integrated into Gemini Enterprise, designed to work in business applications, utilize tools and pursue background objectives. The change is not solely due to the variety of tasks announced, but when passing through a AI That Responds to a An AI to which the organization delegates part of a process. The crucial question then becomes that of control: Who authorizes the agent, what data can it access, and how can its decisions be verified?

01

## What Google Actually Announced

Gemini Agent is described as a single interface capable of answering questions, creating documents and media, generating code, querying data, and executing workflows. It will be accessible from Gemini Enterprise, Google Workspace, a web browser, a terminal, and, gradually, third-party environments such as Microsoft 365 and Slack.[1][2]

In Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Chat, or Calendar, the agent can leverage the information to which the user already has access. Google also plans to offer connectors to GitHub, Jira, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Confluence, and other business services. The provider states that data remains in its original systems and that existing permissions are respected.[2]

However, this announcement should be read carefully. As of October 12, 2026, several key features—including certain long-running background tasks, the ability to choose third-party models, and mobile and desktop applications—are still in early access or being rolled out gradually. In fact, The Verge describes the product as a private preview intended for businesses. It is therefore not yet a widely available service, nor is the product in a stable state.[2][4]

02

## What Sets Gemini Agent Apart from a Chatbot

A chatbot typically waits for an instruction and then generates a response. Gemini Agent receives a task, breaks it down, selects a model, consults sources, calls upon tools, and can continue executing the task without requiring the user to remain at the screen. This innovation is less of a standalone feature and more of a delegation architecture that brings together memory, orchestration, identities, connectors, and action rules.

Google identifies four types of memory: session memory, semantic memory for facts and preferences, procedural memory for work methods, and episodic memory for certain past events. The system can also create temporary subagents, each with its own identity, to handle parts of a task. These so-called “coworkers” may have an email address, storage space, and a context limited to their role.[1][2]

This persistence reduces repetition, but it also increases the impact of an error. A misinterpreted instruction can affect multiple applications, an incorrect memory can influence subsequent tasks, and an overly permissive connector can expose more data than necessary. The agent must therefore be viewed as a component of the information system, not merely as a conversational assistant.

## MasterAgentic AI
with Claude Cowork

Move from conversational AI to operational AI. 2 days to automate your complex tasks — no technical skills required.

2-day course Managers & non-technical staff OPCO / CPF-eligible Paris-Villejuif campus

Explore the course → RS6787 certification

03

## How the agent works within the company

The announced workflow follows a loop: the user defines a goal, Gemini Agent gathers the authorized context, develops a plan, selects the appropriate models and tools, executes the steps, and then returns a result and logs. Google states that the system can currently utilize Gemini and certain Claude models, with additional options planned for the future.[1]

Component  | Rated capacity  | Point to check  
---|---|---
Persistent Execution  | Tasks continue to run in the cloud, sometimes for several hours or several days.  | True availability, fault tolerance, and the ability to stop immediately.  
Applications  | Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, and numerous business services via connectors.  | Precise data scope, read, write, and share permissions.  
Sub-agents  | Creating temporary agents to distribute a complex task.  | Propagation of errors, permissions, and costs among agents.  
Identity  | Dedicated identity for each agent, with its own resources and context.  | Human resources management, lifecycle management, revocation, and exit processing.  
Routing  | Selection of different models based on the task.  | Transparency in selection, measured quality, and data transfer rules.  

From the user’s perspective, this architecture may appear to be a single point of contact. For the company, however, it actually consists of a chain of models, data, connectors, cloud services, and security policies. The evaluation must therefore focus on the entire task, not just on the quality of a generated response.

04

## Why This Could Transform the Way Work Is Organized

The potential benefit comes from reducing the gaps between applications. An agent can, for example, summarize conversations, retrieve related documents, query a database, prepare a presentation, and schedule a meeting. These tasks already exist separately, but performing them in sequence usually requires numerous manual transfers.

The role of professionals is thus shifting from performing micro-tasks to setting goals, selecting sources, handling exceptions, and making decisions. This shift does not mean that an agent replaces an entire job. Google’s ATLAS study, based on 15 million anonymized work interactions, observes the spread of AI across occupations covering a large portion of the U.S. workforce, while emphasizing that full end-to-end automation remains limited.[5]

The core competency becomes controlled delegation: defining an observable outcome, distinguishing between reversible actions and sensitive decisions, setting approval thresholds, and recognizing when an employee must stop. An organization that automates a poorly defined process risks, above all, exacerbating its inconsistencies.

05

## What the Evidence Actually Shows

Google outlines an ambitious architecture and notes that nearly 80% of its cloud customers are already using AI products, while nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies are reportedly using Gemini Enterprise. These figures reflect adoption of the Google ecosystem, not the specific effectiveness of Gemini Agent. They come from the provider and do not constitute an independent benchmark or a measure of productivity.[1]

There is still no comparable public evaluation that measures the agent’s success rate in real-world processes, the frequency of human intervention, silent errors, authorization incidents, or the cost of an outcome that is actually accepted. The demonstration examples show what the product aims to accomplish, but not its reliability at scale.

It is also important to distinguish between the agent and the model. Better reasoning capabilities can improve planning, but success also depends on the quality of the connectors, the status of the applications, access rules, and security controls. In a long workflow, a small error at each step can accumulate and produce a plausible but incorrect result.

Discover the program → RNCP Level 7 certification

06

## Identity, Permissions, Costs, and Liability

Google plans to implement an agent identity based on a SPIFFE identifier, a registry of approved agents and tools, IAM policies with default denial, an execution gateway, and observability logs. Model Armor is designed to analyze tool commands and responses to detect, among other things, prompt injections and certain data leaks.[3]

These safeguards are appropriate, but their effectiveness depends on how they are configured. An agent should be granted only the necessary permissions, for a defined period of time, with a clear distinction between read and write access. Logs must make it possible to reconstruct the objective, the sources consulted, the tools used, the human validations, and the resulting effects.

Cost is another form of governance. Google provides monthly caps, estimates, and detection of abnormal increases. The total cost, however, may include licenses, model calls, execution, memory, connectors, and human oversight. A useful metric, therefore, is not the price per query, but the cost per verified and accepted result.[6]

From a legal standpoint, the European AI Act does not classify a system as high-risk based solely on its autonomy. The classification depends on its intended use. When a system operates in a high-risk domain, Article 14 requires, among other things, that people be able to monitor its operation, interpret its results, disregard or override them, and shut down the system. Human oversight must therefore not be a mere formality, but a real authority exercised under appropriate conditions.[7][8]

07

## What to Watch for Now

The first question will be whether the announced features are actually available. It will be important to distinguish between demonstrations, private previews, and the features that can actually be enabled in each region, each plan, and each connector.

The second will focus on production results: the percentage of tasks completed without correction, time spent on human review, the number of canceled actions, permission-related incidents, cost per accepted result, and the satisfaction of those involved. Without these metrics, it remains difficult to isolate productivity gains.

Google.content:
SecurityBrief US - Technology news for CISOs & cybersecurity decision-makers

# Google launches Gemini for government services preview
Tue, 3rd Nov 2026 (Today) 
REGINE LAGUILLES Editor

Google has launched Gemini for government services in private preview, targeting federal, state and local agencies.

The launch was part of a broader set of public sector product announcements, including new Wiz security agents in Wiz for Gov and expanded Gemini search tools for classified environments on Google Distributed Cloud.

As part of new research into the use of AI agents across government organisations, Google surveyed several hundred public sector leaders with theCUBE and ECI Research. The findings showed that 96.3% of agencies have deployed agents in some form, but only 9% have achieved agency-wide adoption.

The main barriers were legacy data silos and integration complexity, rather than a lack of interest in broader use of the technology.

Government platform

Gemini for government services is aimed at public sector workflows that require security and governance controls. Google said the platform is built to connect with existing case management, ERP and collaboration systems without requiring agencies to move sensitive data out of their current systems of record.

It includes pre-built partner agents, secure connectors and what Google described as deterministic skills. The platform is intended to support repetitive administrative work, including public records requests, document intake validation, expense auditing and policy research, with responses grounded in federal regulatory sources and linked to citations.

Alongside the government-specific platform, Google highlighted the Gemini agent, which it recently introduced as a single work assistant for tasks ranging from answering questions to coding. The agent can connect to organisational systems, select models for particular jobs and operate within an organisation's existing security, administration and governance policies, according to Google.

Security tools

Another part of the announcement centred on Wiz for Gov, Wiz's FedRAMP High environment. Google said the Wiz Red, Green and Blue agents are now available there.

The Green Agent includes a new risk category focused on weak cryptography and post-quantum cryptography readiness. Google said it is designed to identify whether assets are vulnerable to quantum-related threats and to assess possible Harvest Now, Decrypt Later exposure.

Google also pointed to wider work by Wiz and Google DeepMind through the Scan for Good programme, which offers no-cost security assessments for eligible public services, critical infrastructure and other under-resourced organisations. Wiz is also extending tools for organisations dealing with FedRAMP vulnerability detection, response, evaluation and reporting requirements, including metrics such as Potential Agency Impact, likely exploitability and internet reachability, according to Google.

Classified search

Google is also bringing enterprise search to Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud for air-gapped deployments used by defence, intelligence and national security agencies. The addition is intended for classified environments where agencies need to analyse large stores of sensitive information while remaining disconnected from the public internet.

The update gives users a conversational interface for querying, synthesising and summarising records in on-premises environments, according to Google. It also brings Gemini 3.5 Flash models to those deployments, adds support for open models including Gemma and makes NVIDIA Blackwell B300 GPUs generally available for local compute.

Customer projects

Google used the announcement to highlight several public sector projects already under way. It said America.gov is using Gemini to help simplify access to federal services online, while the State University of New York is using Google Cloud tools to support research across storage, computing and AI models.

Google also cited the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission, where Gemini is being used across research and specialist facilities, and a US Army logistics modernisation effort that combines Google Cloud services with FedEx expertise to improve supply chain operations.

In another example, Google said the Department of War is giving 3 million personnel access to a secure Gemini platform through GenAI.mil, where users can build agents with natural language to handle tasks such as document creation and review. Case Western Reserve University was also named as a customer using Gemini across teaching, research and administration.

The announcements underline the scale of competition among large technology providers for government AI and cloud work, particularly where agencies want tighter controls over data handling, procurement compliance and cyber risk. They also reflect a push to move beyond small pilots into broader operational use, even as agency-wide adoption remains limited.

Google.content:
Google 回顧 Gemini 4 Carbon、Argon 及其他三項 AI 更新

關鍵要點

在擴大開放前，Google 透過 Fairwind Program 優先向值得信賴的網路安全防禦者提供 Gemini 4 Carbon。

Gemini 4 Argon 全球推出，旨在解決科學、程式設計與代理式領域中具有實際影響的複雜問題。

EmbeddingGemma 2 將程式碼、圖片、影片和音訊映射至統一的向量空間，同時最多可將本機向量儲存需求降低 6 倍。

Google 在 X 貼文中回顧了 10 月的 AI 公告，該貼文的時間戳記為 06:55:06 PM · 11/02/2026。貼文表示，Gemini 4 Carbon 將透過 Fairwind Program，率先向一部分受信任的網路安全防禦者推出，之後再擴大提供範圍。回顧內容也涵蓋 Gemini 4 Argon、Google Fitbit Edge、Genie 4 和 EmbeddingGemma 2。

Gemini 4 Carbon 和 Argon 推出進度

Google 將 Gemini 4 Carbon 描述為其最新的前沿模型，具備最先進的網路安全能力和長期規劃能力。該公司表示，會透過 Fairwind Program，率先向一部分受信任的網路安全防禦者推出此模型，之後再擴大提供範圍。

Google 表示，Gemini 4 Argon 已在全球推出。此模型專為高度複雜的科學、程式設計和代理型問題打造。貼文指出，Argon 已在科學界產生實際影響，Google 也正運用它協助解決一些最棘手的工程問題。

Google Fitbit Edge 新增 Gemini 驅動的健康指引

Google 將 Fitbit Edge 描述為有史以來最智慧的健身追蹤器，具備纖薄舒適的設計，電池續航力最長可達七天。它結合精準 GPS 和涵蓋 50 多種活動的自動運動辨識功能，並提供由 Gemini 驅動的 Google Health Coach 所提供的個人化指引。

Genie 4 新增即時互動式模擬功能

Google 表示，Genie 4 將真實世界物理、逼真的人體動作和原生音訊帶入即時互動式模擬。使用者可透過自然語言，在場景展開時操控場景。貼文指出，Genie 4 提升了 Google 建立機器人和 AI Agent 安全訓練環境的能力，是邁向 AGI 的關鍵一步。

EmbeddingGemma 2 將多種媒體類型映射至同一空間

Google 將 EmbeddingGemma 2 描述為一款全新的開放式嵌入模型，可在日常裝置上將程式碼、圖片、影片和音訊映射至單一統一空間。此模型可將本機向量儲存空間最多減少 6 倍。Google 表示，這讓私有、離線應用程式能從語音備忘錄中找出特定影片片段，或透過文字查詢搜尋數小時的音訊。

Google 10 月 AI 公告一覽

Gemini 4 Carbon 將透過 Fairwind Program，率先向一部分受信任的網路安全防禦者推出，之後再擴大提供範圍。

Gemini 4 Argon 已在全球推出，專為高度複雜的科學、程式設計和代理型問題打造。

Google Fitbit Edge 的電池續航力最長可達七天，具備精準 GPS 和涵蓋 50 多種活動的自動運動辨識功能。

Genie 4 將真實世界物理、逼真的人體動作和原生音訊帶入即時互動式模擬。

EmbeddingGemma 2 將程式碼、圖片、影片和音訊映射至單一統一空間，並將本機向量儲存空間最多減少 6 倍。

常見問題

哪些人會率先使用 Gemini 4 Carbon？

Google 表示，Gemini 4 Carbon 將透過 Fairwind Program，率先向一部分受信任的網路安全防禦者推出，之後再擴大提供範圍。

Google Fitbit Edge 有哪些功能？

Fitbit Edge 的電池續航力最長可達七天，具備精準 GPS、涵蓋 50 多種活動的自動運動辨識功能，以及由 Gemini 驅動的 Google Health Coach 所提供的個人化指引。

EmbeddingGemma 2 有什麼用途？

EmbeddingGemma 2 可在日常裝置上將程式碼、圖片、影片和音訊映射至單一統一空間，並將本機向量儲存空間最多減少 6 倍。

Meta.content:
# Meta Model API

The Meta Model API (public preview) serves Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API. The Meta provider extends the OpenAI provider and supports its compatible options.

note

This provider uses the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai for Muse models. Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on July 6, 2026.

## Setup

- Create an API key from the API keys tab on the Meta Model API dashboard.
- Set theMODEL_API_KEY environment variable, or specify apiKey or a custom apiKeyEnvar in your config.

providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3

meta:<model> defaults to the Responses API — Meta's full-feature surface and the one its docs recommend. Use meta:chat:<model> for the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, or meta:messages:<model> for the Anthropic-compatible Messages API. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to muse-spark-1.1; select muse-spark-1.3 explicitly to use the latest model.

## Available Models

Check the models page for the live list. As of writing:

- muse-spark-1.3 — latest model for coding and agentic workflows, with a 1,048,576-token context window, text/image/video/PDF input, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.
- muse-spark-1.3-contributor — the same model with discounted pricing. Selecting this ID permits Meta to use your prompts and completions to train future models.
- muse-spark-1.1 — original Muse Spark model, still supported.

Both 1.3 IDs work with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Messages APIs. Meta notes that audio understanding in 1.3 is not fully supported and may produce degraded responses.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: high
      max_completion_tokens: 8192
      temperature: 1.0

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts compatible OpenAI provider options. Notable behavior:

- reasoning_effort — minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh. When omitted, the model picks its own reasoning depth. Muse Spark does not support none; the provider rejects it with a clear error. Reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and count toward the output cap.
- max_completion_tokens — caps generation on the chat endpoint (Meta accepts max_tokens only as a deprecated alias; if you set it, the provider forwards it as the canonical max_completion_tokens). On the Responses API the cap is max_output_tokens, and the provider maps max_completion_tokens/max_tokens onto it. When unset, no cap is sent so reasoning can use the full output budget.
- temperature — supported (0–2, API default 1.0). Promptfoo sends its deterministic default of 0 unless you override it.
- response_format — structured output with guaranteed JSON schema matching.
- tools / tool_choice — parallel tool calling with streamed arguments.
- prompt_cache_retention — in_memory or 24h for prompt caching; cached prompt tokens bill at the cached-input rate.
- seed — best-effort determinism.

On Chat Completions and Responses, promptfoo rejectslogprobs, n > 1, stop, and logit_bias before sending a request. It also rejects stream because these integrations expect a complete JSON response. OpenAI-scoped environment defaults (OPENAI_TEMPERATURE, OPENAI_TOP_P, OPENAI_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS, penalty variables) are not applied to Meta requests.

### Cost Tracking

Promptfoo computes token cost from Meta's published pricing, including the discounted rate for cached input:

Model | Input / 1M | Cached input / 1M | Output / 1M 
---|---|---|---
muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.1 | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 
muse-spark-1.3-contributor | $0.10 | $0.002 | $0.20 

Contributor pricing requires opting into Meta's training data terms by selecting the Contributor model ID. Override token prices withcost, inputCost, outputCost, or cacheReadCost (USD per token) for custom rates. Token cost excludes web-search charges.

## Responses API

meta:<model> (the default) and meta:responses:<model> target Meta's /v1/responses endpoint — the only Meta endpoint that carries reasoning across turns, with built-in web-search grounding:
providers:
  - id: meta:responses:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium
      tools:
        - type: web_search

Withweb_search, the model grounds answers in real-time web results with inline citations. Web search bills separately ($2.50 per 1,000 queries) and is not included in promptfoo's computed token cost.

## Messages API

meta:messages:<model> targets Meta's Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/messages) — the surface Anthropic-format coding agents such as Claude Code use. Use it to evaluate Muse Spark over the same wire format those agents send:
providers:
  - id: meta:messages:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192

The provider extends the Anthropic provider, so its options (max_tokens, tools, image and document content blocks, etc.) apply. It defaults max_tokens to 131,072 and enables streaming so the Anthropic SDK can safely handle long generations; streamed output is aggregated before grading. Authentication uses your Meta key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer), matching Meta's docs — Anthropic-scoped settings like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS, ANTHROPIC_TEMPERATURE, custom headers, and Claude Code OAuth credentials are deliberately ignored on this surface.

Muse Spark's reasoning arrives on this surface as encryptedredacted_thinking blocks, so the provider defaults showThinking to false to keep the ciphertext out of graded output.

## Using with coding-agent providers

Meta positions Muse Spark as a backend for coding agents, and promptfoo's agentic providers can evaluate those setups end to end. In both recipes, setapiKey explicitly: the agent subprocesses inherit your shell environment, and an explicit key guarantees your Meta key is used instead of an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that belongs to another service.

### Codex CLI

Theopenai:codex-sdk provider drives Muse Spark over the Responses API:
providers:
  - id: openai:codex-sdk
    config:
      base_url: https://api.meta.ai/v1
      model: muse-spark-1.3
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'

The explicitapiKey is required — the provider does not read MODEL_API_KEY on its own, and without it an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY would be sent to the Meta endpoint instead.

### Claude Code

Theanthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider forwards config.env to the agent subprocess. Pass the environment Meta's guide prescribes, with apiKey set to your Meta key:
providers:
  - id: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
    # Provider-level `env` outranks the eval's top-level `env`, pinning the
    # routing values a suite-wide ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (e.g. an Anthropic
    # gateway) would otherwise override — which would send the Meta key there.
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
      ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
    config:
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
        ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: 'true' # Claude Code disables MCP tool search for non-first-party hosts

warning

Do not omitapiKey, the empty ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS override, or the provider-level env block. The provider forwards its resolved API key into the agent subprocess as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY after env: is applied — if apiKey is unset and a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported in your shell, that Anthropic credential would be transmitted to Meta's endpoint. Clearing ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS prevents an inherited gateway or proxy secret from being sent to Meta. The provider-level env block matters because the subprocess environment is layered process.env < config.env < provider/suite env: without the pin, a top-level env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in the same config would silently re-route the agent — and your Meta key — to that URL.

Pin every model alias as shown — Claude Code otherwise routes background tasks, Plan Mode, or subagents to Claude models the Meta API doesn't serve. See Meta's coding agents guide for the full setup pattern.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
  - id: openai:gpt-5.5

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

Get started with a runnable example:
npx promptfoo@latest init --example provider-meta

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.meta.ai/v1 (override with apiBaseUrl; the Messages surface uses the bare host https://api.meta.ai).
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions (/chat/completions) and Responses (/responses) endpoints, plus the Anthropic-compatible Messages (/messages) endpoint.
- Rate limits apply per team, not per key: 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM for Standard models and 100 RPM / 3M TPM for Contributor models.
- Full API documentation.

Tasks keep running after you close the app, and you can watch the agent's browser while it works. Under the hood, each user's agent runs on its own dedicated virtual machine in Meta's cloud. Meta says that machine "houses both the agent and the user's data" and that no other user's agent can reach it. # Meta Muse: Meta's AI Agent App and Models

Meta Muse is the name Meta gives to its new generation of AI, built by Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL). The name covers two connected things. One is Muse, Meta's personal AI agent app, launched in the US on September 8, 2026, which can browse the web, fill in forms, send email and book things for you. The other is the Muse family of models behind that app and behind Meta AI: Muse Spark, Muse Image, Muse Glimmer, Muse Spark Open and Muse Wonder.

Most people can start for free. The app has a free tier plus paid plans at $20 and $100 a month, and Muse Image is free inside Meta AI, WhatsApp and Instagram Stories. Developers can call Muse models through the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai, and two of them, Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open, are open-weight models you can download and run yourself. Everything below is as of October 2026.

## Where Muse fits in Meta's AI

In 2025 Meta reorganized its AI work into Meta Superintelligence Labs, led by chief AI officer Alexandr Wang. Muse is the brand for everything that group ships, and Mark Zuckerberg describes the goal as "personal superintelligence": an AI that knows you and acts for you.

The clearest way to hold it in your head is as a stack:
Muse models (Spark, Image, Wonder, Glimmer, Spark Open)
        ↓
Meta Model API (for developers)  +  Meta AI (in Meta's apps)
        ↓
Muse app (personal agent)  ·  Muse Code (coding agent)  ·  WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, glasses

When someone says "Meta Muse", they usually mean either the agent app at the bottom of that stack or the models at the top. If you're wondering how this relates to Llama: Llama was Meta's earlier open model family, and Muse is the newer line from MSL. Meta AI, which used to run on Llama models, is now powered by Muse Spark, and Meta's newest open-weight releases carry the Muse name.

## What the Muse app actually does

Meta positions Muse as an agent for long-running tasks rather than a chatbot that answers one question at a time. In Meta's words, it can "open a browser, fill out forms, and negotiate" on your behalf. In practice that means sending emails, booking travel, managing schedules and helping with shopping, and it can also turn a long-term goal into a plan, such as a yearlong fitness program or the steps to set up a small business. Tasks keep running after you close the app, and you can watch the agent's browser while it works.

Under the hood, each user's agent runs on its own dedicated virtual machine in Meta's cloud. Meta says that machine "houses both the agent and the user's data" and that no other user's agent can reach it. Reports describe a permissions system that controls which services the agent can touch and separates read access from write access.

The app is open to adults (18 and over) in the United States only. It runs on iOS, Android and the web, with a Mac client, and inside WhatsApp. Beyond the free tier, the $20 and $100 monthly plans buy higher usage, and Meta says there is no advertising in Muse. According to multiple reports, it reached the top of Apple's US App Store shortly after launch.

If you try it, the setup is short: install Muse from the App Store or Google Play (or open it on the web), sign in with your Meta account, confirm you're 18 or older, and optionally personalize the agent's name and style. Two steps deserve more care than the rest. Connect only the services you actually need and read the read/write permissions for each, and check the privacy settings, because reports say queries are used for model training by default. You can turn that off. For the first few tasks, keep the browser view open and watch what it does.

### Muse Spark: the model behind Meta AI

Muse Spark came first. Meta calls it "small and fast by design" and built it for its own products. It has Instant and Thinking modes and can launch several subagents in parallel for hard questions. Beyond chat, it handles images, health questions, voice, visual coding (a website, dashboard or mini-game from a prompt) and a shopping mode that searches Facebook Marketplace and the web.

It's a proprietary model. Through the API it has a 1,048,576-token context window and accepts text, image, video, audio and PDF input. To chat with it, use the Meta AI app or meta.ai, or Meta AI inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger.

### Muse Image: free image generation in Meta's apps

Muse Image, which we covered when Meta introduced the Muse Image generator, does text-to-image generation from complex prompts and edits images from plain-language instructions. The more interesting part is how you edit: you can circle or mark an area and change only that part, refine an image step by step in conversation because Meta AI keeps the context, and edit across multiple images using references. It can also pull in public Instagram content through @mentions, with controls that let creators decide how their content is used, and it drives more than 30 AI effects in Instagram Stories.

Standard image creation in Meta AI is free. On quality, launch coverage says Meta's internal human-rated rankings placed Muse Image second in both text-to-image and image editing, and that Meta acknowledged OpenAI's latest image model still led overall. Those are Meta's own evaluations, not independent ones.

### Muse Wonder: built for agents

Muse Wonder is Meta's most capable model so far, and it's aimed squarely at agents. Meta highlights two abilities. Active Memory keeps important context about you across conversations and pulls the relevant details into the current task. Active Focus keeps the model working toward hard goals: it tries other approaches when blocked, asks for clarification when it needs to, and checks in before important actions.

Meta claims state-of-the-art results on agent, memory and coding benchmarks, but independent results were thin at the time of writing. Muse Wonder is in preview on the Meta Model API asmuse-wonder-1.0. The larger Muse Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code's higher subscription plans.

### Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open: the ones you can run yourself

These two are very different propositions, and the table makes the choice fairly obvious:

Detail

Muse Glimmer

Muse Spark Open

---|---|---

Size

816B total, 42B active (mixture of experts)

License

Apache 2.0

Muse Model License (limited commercial terms)

Hardware

One consumer GPU or Mac, about 24 to 32 GB memory at 4-bit

Data-center GPUs, or two 512 GB Mac Studios using MLX

Best for

Local agents, function calling, local coding

Coding and agentic work at frontier scale

Context

Not stated by Meta

1M tokens

Both are on Hugging Face, and Muse Spark Open is also available through major cloud model catalogs and hosted inference providers. If you want something running on your own machine this week, Glimmer is the realistic option, and its Apache 2.0 license is the only genuinely permissive one in the Muse family. If you haven't run a model locally before, Local AI Inference in .NET covers running models on Windows without cloud APIs.

## Calling Muse models from code

The Meta Model API uses the base URLhttps://api.meta.ai/v1 with a bearer API key. Meta's own examples point the OpenAI SDK at that URL, and the API supports Chat Completions, Responses and Messages-style requests for Muse Spark and Muse Wonder, plus image generation and edit endpoints for Muse Image. The model IDs you'll use:

- muse-spark-1.3, recommended for new work, in Standard mode
- muse-spark-1.3-contributor, cheaper, but your content may be used to train Meta's models
- muse-wonder-1.0, preview, Standard mode only
- muse-image-1.0, for image generation and edits
- muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, for speech to text

The Standard/Contributor split matters more than the model choice. Standard mode means your content is not used to train Meta's models; Contributor mode trades that away for a lower price. For anything that touches customer or company data, use Standard.

In Python, it's the OpenAI client with a different base URL:
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["MODEL_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="muse-spark-1.3",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise technical assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain dependency injection in ASP.NET Core in 3 bullets."},
    ],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)

The same works from C# with the OpenAI .NET SDK:
using System.ClientModel;
using OpenAI;
using OpenAI.Chat;

var client = new ChatClient(
    model: "muse-spark-1.3",
    credential: new ApiKeyCredential(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("MODEL_API_KEY")!),
    options: new OpenAIClientOptions { Endpoint = new Uri("https://api.meta.ai/v1") });

ChatCompletion completion = await client.CompleteChatAsync(
    new SystemChatMessage("You are a concise technical assistant."),
    new UserChatMessage("Explain dependency injection in ASP.NET Core in 3 bullets."));

# Meta: The Hyperscaler Whose Only Customer Is Itself

### The best demand machine ever built is now financing a $454bn bet on agents with no cloud tenant to share the risk. Zuckerberg’s big bets, the race to the frontier, the capex and what the stock already prices

Welcome to the 90th investment case, 62nd Resilience & Quality, 51st AI & Technology idea on Crack The Market (and the most comprehensive Meta investment case you will find online)! Join me as I dissect one of the most profitable consumer franchises ever built, a company that reaches 3.64 billion people every day, grew its advertising business 26% at a $250bn run-rate last quarter, and is now spending more on AI infrastructure than any company that does not rent it out to anyone else.

Crack The Market publishes two to three pieces a week across six themes: AI & Technology, Electrification & Energy, Reshoring & Sovereignty, Healthcare & Longevity, China & Asia, and Resilience & Quality.

Join as a subscriber today to get access to institutional level research helping you own equities you understand and learn about the trends, technologies and companies that will underpin the value creation of the next decades.

The archive runs to more than 200 pieces and more than 85 company deep dives.

The annual plan is half the monthly rate: twelve months for the price of six.

After reading this article, you will understand why Meta is the purest test of the application layer in my Token Economics framework, why the third quarter of 2026 was the quarter Meta stopped paying for itself and started asking capital markets to help, and why the answer to “is it too late?” depends far more on what you believe about the core advertising engine than about Muse.

In this article I go through:

How Meta became Meta: twenty years of founder-led bets, the seven sentiment regimes since the IPO, and what the stock did each time spending ran ahead of proof.

How Meta went from AI loser to the frontier: from the Llama 4 miss to Muse Wonder Full scoring 50 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, level with Gemini 4 Argon and behind Gemini 4 Carbon (59), Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 (58) and GPT-6 Astra (57), and what it cost to get there.

The platform logic: what Meta owns, what it rents, who its partners are, and why it is the only hyperscaler whose compute has no external customer at scale.

Where the capex goes, why it is so high, and how an outsider can measure the return.

The balance sheet crossover: negative free cash flow, gross debt above cash, $454.5bn of commitments, a $97.5bn equity plan and a negative S&P outlook.

Zuckerberg’s vision, his track record from Instagram to the metaverse, and what it tells us about the next five years.

A full valuation, against Meta’s own history and against the other hyperscalers, with bear, base and bull scenarios, and where the stock fits in a portfolio.

## Meta Investment Case

#### Table of content

## Positioning: the third hyperscaler, and the hardest one

On the 22nd of October, the day after its third quarter, Meta fell 7%, to $649. Revenue beat, Q4 guidance came in above consensus, at least 13 published price targets went up, and Muse passed 10 million users in six weeks. Four days later Meta launched a $97.5bn equity plan, on the 30th S&P moved the outlook on its credit rating to negative, and the stock closed October at $615, 12% below where it stood before the results.

The market sold it anyway, in a broad AI sell-off that took the Nasdaq down 2.6% and the semiconductor equipment names down 6% to 10%. The other hyperscalers have since reported and the pattern has sharpened: Alphabet lost around $500bn of market value in a day, down 12.6%, on negative free cash flow despite Cloud growing 103%, Amazon fell on a record cash burn despite AWS growing 39%, and Microsoft, the only one still comfortably funding its capex from operating cash flow, was spared, with Azure up 48%. It is the same reaction I wrote about when Alphabet reported in July, and it tells you exactly where the debate now sits: not on whether AI is working, but on who pays for it.

This is the third hyperscaler investment case I have published this year, and I want to be upfront that it is the hardest of the three, because Meta does not fit the framework the other two confirmed.

In April, Microsoft was the enterprise stack: It monetizes AI at every layer, from Azure capacity to Copilot seats, and it sells most of its compute to someone else. When the market sold it on a one-point Azure miss, I argued it was the best company in the world at a price that made no sense.

In July, Alphabet was the hyperscaler that already pays for itself: It is paid on volume at the bottom of its stack (Cloud, now TPU systems sold as hardware), paid on differentiation at the top (Search, YouTube, subscriptions), and it had a $514bn Cloud backlog and around $144bn of net cash behind it. Last week’s print tests that title: Cloud revenue doubled and the backlog reached $561bn, but free cash flow turned negative, at $9.1bn in Q3, as capex and TPU inventory ran ahead of collections, although it remains positive over twelve months.

Meta is the inverse case: It is building at the scale of the cloud providers, $135bn to $145bn of capex this year and consensus of $222bn for 2027, with published estimates as high as $255bn (and buy side more around $240-260bn), but it has no cloud tenants, no backlog and no external customer of any size on the other side of that spending. Every gigawatt it commits has to earn its return through Meta’s own products.

Remember my Token Economics framework. As the price of any fixed level of intelligence collapses, value moves to the two ends of the stack: the toll booths paid on volume underneath, and the application layer paid on differentiation on top. The hyperscalers sit in the middle, protected by the three things tokens cannot commoditize: distribution, proprietary data and the enterprise relationship.

Meta owns the first two at a scale nobody else matches. 3.64 billion people use its apps every day, and the company estimates that at least 500 million self-identified small businesses use them to reach customers. The only gap is that it has never owned the third. That is exactly what the new Meta Enterprise Platform, led by former MongoDB CEO CJ Desai since late September, is trying to build.

So Meta is the cleanest test I have of the application layer in my own framework. Meta is not exposed to the token volume curve the way Alphabet or Microsoft are. It is a bet on one company’s ability to turn compute into consumer and small business value faster than the depreciation clock runs.

This is also why Meta matters far beyond its own share price. In the AI value chain map I published in August, the hyperscale buyers sit at the top of the stack and fund every layer beneath them.

Meta’s third quarter puts numbers on that wall:

$454.5bn of non-cancelable contractual commitments as of the 30th of September, mostly third-party cloud capacity, servers and network infrastructure, energy services and Reality Labs hardware, up from $131bn at the end of 2025. Of that, $121.4bn falls due in 2027.

A further $355.7bn of data center, energy and network leases that have been signed but have not yet commenced, starting between now and 2036.

$68.4bn of maximum exposure to the two off-balance-sheet data center ventures in Louisiana and Texas.

Those numbers are the order books of Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, the memory makers, the neoclouds, the optical chain and the power equipment names I cover. If Meta’s bet works, a large part of my AI coverage keeps compounding. If Meta blinks, they feel it first.

In Is the AI Trade Financeable? I mapped which buyers fund the build from operating cash flow and which lean on capital markets. In What Is Actually Happening to the AI Trade I argued that the financing of the marginal buyer was repricing. Meta’s third quarter moved it decisively from the first group toward the second: free cash flow turned negative, gross debt passed cash, and the company announced a non-voting share class, followed five days later by a $97.5bn equity plan. Two days after the results, in Is the AI Bubble Bursting?, I argued that the market was repricing who pays for AI, and Meta is now the clearest example.

And it closes a loop I opened five weeks ago. In The Age of Agents I argued that Muse was the moment the agent replaced the chat as the unit of consumer AI, but I also wrote that I doubted Meta could fund its own silicon, due to the balance sheet not a product problem.

The organizing question of this deep dive is therefore simple: Can the best demand machine ever built fund Meta’s conversion into a capital-heavy agent network before the funding window narrows, and is the market paying too much for the answer?

My answer is that the core can carry this conversion, the balance sheet has become a live variable, and Muse represents upside rather than the floor for the business. The rest of this piece will give you the evidence, and I will be explicit about where I think the market is right and where I think it is too generous.

## Business Description

Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, Meta was famously founded as Facebook in 2004 by Mark Zuckerberg and his Harvard roommates. It listed on Nasdaq in May 2012, renamed itself Meta Platforms in October 2021, and today runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads, alongside the Ray-Ban and Oakley AI glasses it builds with EssilorLuxottica, the Quest headsets, and since September the Muse personal agent.

Meta’s scale is one of a kind:

3.64 billion people use at least one of Meta’s apps every day, according to the company’s Family daily active people metric, roughly 45% of the human population.

Facebook and Instagram are at all-time highs in engagement, driven by video. Instagram time spent per user grew double digits year-on-year in Q3, and Facebook Reels time spent hit record

Meta's Llama model family has fundamentally changed the economics of deploying large language models. For the first time, enterprises can run state-of-the-art open-weight models inside their own infrastructure. No data leaves to a third-party API, no per-token cost accumulates at scale, and fine-tuning on proprietary data is practical. But the gap between downloading a Llama checkpoint and running a production-grade, latency-consistent, cost-efficient inference stack is substantial. Codieshub engineers bridge that gap.

Our AI teams have worked with the full Llama lineage, from the original release through Llama 3.1 and 3.2 instruction-tuned and base variants, running inference on vLLM and llama.cpp backends, applying LoRA and QLoRA fine-tuning for domain-specific tasks, and integrating models into retrieval-augmented pipelines for healthcare documentation, fintech compliance, and SaaS product features. We understand the tradeoffs between quantization levels, context window management, and GPU memory footprint because we've navigated them on real production systems.

For companies evaluating whether to build on Llama versus a closed API, Codieshub offers direct technical guidance grounded in your specific latency SLAs, data sensitivity requirements, and budget. We've helped clients make that call in both directions, and we build whichever path is right for the business.

Teams that attempt Llama deployments without LLM infrastructure experience routinely hit the same wall: models that benchmark well on a single GPU become unpredictable under concurrent load, quantized variants introduce subtle quality regressions that appear only on domain-specific inputs, and fine-tuning runs that look promising in notebooks fail to generalize or overfit to training artifacts. Procurement and compliance teams often don't know how to evaluate open-weight model risk relative to closed APIs, creating organizational hesitation that delays shipping.

Codieshub structures Llama engagements around three distinct workstreams: inference infrastructure design (selecting the serving backend, quantization level, batching strategy, and hardware configuration for your throughput and latency targets), fine-tuning pipeline development (data curation, LoRA adapter training, evaluation harness, and model registry), and application integration (RAG pipeline wiring, prompt engineering, output parsing, and guardrail implementation). We run all three concurrently with separate specialist engineers rather than a generalist who context-switches between them.

Production Llama deployments from Codieshub are designed to target sub-500ms first-token latency for 7B and 13B parameter models under realistic concurrent load. The right hardware and serving configuration makes this achievable for most workloads. Self-hosted inference typically converts per-token API cost into fixed compute cost at significantly lower run-rate once query volume is sufficient; we model the break-even for your specific throughput before you commit. Fine-tuned adapters are evaluated against held-out domain benchmarks so quality uplift is measurable, not assumed. Teams leave with reproducible infrastructure-as-code, a documented model evaluation protocol, and the operational knowledge to iterate without Codieshub in the loop.

## 开源正在削弱闭源的统治

早期采用者的GenAI部署偏爱OpenAI的GPT-4，但LLM之间的竞争在最近几个月加剧。更小的开源模型推翻了OpenAI“越大越好”的叙事。Deutsche Bank指出，Hugging Face平台上近50万个模型中，许多基于Meta的开源Llama，或其后继者Llama 2（70亿、130亿、700亿参数版本）。LoRA等新技术让推出大规模预训练模型的微调版本变得便宜且容易。

开源模型的引入开始削弱LLM的主导地位。专家认为低价位产品即将出现。甲骨文和Salesforce等企业软件公司已转向LLM-agnostic模型，预示未来战略可能发生转变。这不是说GPT-4不行了，是说企业不再愿意被单一模型锁定。

## 定制开源模型可能追平GPT-4

虽然GPT-4在2023年占据头条，但更小的定制开源模型经过私人数据训练，可能在2024年达到与GPT-4性能相当的临界点。这可能导致企业应用的架构出现重大变化。企业面临一个抉择点：选择Llama、Mistral等易于本地部署的小模型，还是信任大公司的企业解决方案？

行业专家的判断很直接：“对于这些更大的公司，人们仍然不够信任他们能够更好地管理数据。”数据安全是企业选择开源的重要驱动力。把模型放在本地，数据不出企业边界，对于金融、医疗、政府等敏感行业，这是硬需求。

## 开源不是免费，是另一种成本

开源模型没有授权费，但有部署成本。企业需要GPU、服务器、AI工程师来部署和微调模型。对于没有AI团队的企业，开源的门槛比调用API高得多。但对于有AI团队的企业，开源提供了控制权：控制模型、控制数据、控制成本。

开源和闭源不是对立，是光谱。企业可以选择完全开源的Llama，可以选择LLM-agnostic的Salesforce，也可以选择GPT-4的API。选择的标准不是“哪个更先进”，是“哪个更适合我的数据、我的团队、我的预算”。开源大模型在企业应用中的竞争力，不在于性能超越GPT-4，而在于给了企业一个不被锁定的选项。

# AI agents being given greater autonomy

#### By CHENG YU | China Daily

#### Updated: 2026-11-03 09:32

Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek has unveiled a new architecture aimed at making AI agents more autonomous, marking the latest push by China's model developers to move beyond chatbots toward systems capable of independently carrying out complex tasks.

DeepSeek's Harness team said in an article published on Saturday that its experimental "super-agent" architecture is designed to allow AI to continuously monitor information, manage multiple tasks in parallel and take action with less human supervision.

The development points to a broader shift in China's fast-moving AI industry, where competition is increasingly moving beyond model size and benchmark scores toward agents that can plan, execute and complete real-world work.

As AI models become better at handling individual tasks, Deep-Seek said the bottleneck is increasingly human attention: users still have to switch between different conversations, keep track of their progress and provide instructions.

The super-agent approach is intended to move much of that coordination into the AI system itself, allowing people to focus more on higher-level decisions and reviewing results rather than overseeing each step of a task. Deep-Seek stressed that the architecture remains an engineering exploration rather than a feature available in its existing products.

DeepSeek said an internal version of the system is already operating continuously. When employees flag a software problem in a group chat, for example, the AI can identify the potential defect even without being directly addressed, attempt to reproduce the problem in the background and search for a fix.

The push reflects a growing focus across the AI industry on so-called agentic AI — systems designed not only to generate text or answer questions, but also to make plans, use tools and carry out multi-step tasks.

Chinese developers have accelerated model releases in recent weeks. The flurry of releases suggests China's AI race is entering a new phase. Rather than simply building models that are bigger or score higher on tests, developers are increasingly competing over whether AI can reliably turn intelligence into action.

Moonshot AI released last month Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in its new K3.1 series. The company said the model, its most capable in the roughly 3-trillion-parameter class, offers substantial improvements in coding, 3D creation, financial research and other long-horizon agent tasks, while supporting a context window of 1 million tokens.

MiniMax launched its M3.1 Flash model mid-October, saying it had strengthened performance in agentic tasks, coding and computer use while delivering online inference speeds nearly three times faster than its predecessor and cutting the overall cost of agent tasks by 70 percent.

DeepSeek itself updated its V4.1 Flash model on Oct 17. DeepSeek said the update improved performance while allowing tasks to be completed faster and with shorter outputs.

Wei Kai, head of the AI research institute at the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, said in a separate interview that agents represent an engineering enhancement built on top of large language models that can significantly extend their capabilities.

But challenges remain. "Agents still need improvement in reliability, contextual memory and long-horizon tasks, and there is still some distance to go before large-scale adoption," Wei said.

# 【AI+代理】DeepSeek完成千億元人民幣融資後頻推新產品 推創作者模式 加強AI代理能力

股市

撰文： 張偉倫

發布時間： 17 小時前

最後更新： 17 小時前

AI 摘要

- DeepSeek推出創作者模式快速創建插件
- DeepSeek提出超級代理架構優化多任務處理
- 超級代理具備主動、高效、連續及持久特徵

內地人工智能（AI）企業DeepSeek早前完成1,000億元人民幣後，近期連番推出新產品。為強化AI智能體，推出一項可以快速創建自定義插件的新功能，以幫助用戶處理一系列複雜任務。

DeepSeek Harness團隊在X平台發帖稱，新的「創作者模式」允許用戶「將想法變成可以使用的插件」。公司展示了多種插件製作方式，包括僅通過英文自然語言指令創建用於渲染3D模型的插件以及視頻編輯工作台等。

美國和中國的頂尖AI開發商正競相推出更先進的AI智能體，為專業人士和普通用戶承擔包括編寫代碼、處理金融研究等工作。DeepSeek的AI智能體更側重於開發者，而非普通用戶。

今年較早時候，DeepSeek組建Harness團隊，專注於打造能夠與AI編程服務競爭的AI智能體。

## 上周六推出增強版編程助手

DeepSeek上周六（10月31日）推出了一款增強版編程助手，旨在主動幫助解決問題，同時儘可能減少對人工干預的需求。

當日DeepSeek Harness團隊於微信公眾號上發表技術文章，指出現有的主流代理設計，難以於多任務和團隊協作的規模上支撐，並提出可連續、高效率、主動且持久的「超級代理（Super-agent）」架構，並將「超級代理」原型公開。

DeepSeek Harness指出，當使用者並行推進多項工作時，必須手動切換並記住各個會話（Session）的上下文，據他們觀察，一個人通常只能同時跟進3至5個活躍會話。另若於現時本機單會話代理上借助命令行界面（CLI）、模型上下文協議（MCP）或外部連接器做簡單擴展，代理雖然也能接入外部訊息，但仍受制於單會話同步阻塞、多任務上下文混亂、本地設備離線即停止運行等問題，需要大量人工維護。

## 代理的思考及計算部分上雲

DeepSeek Harness解釋，要讓「超級代理」做到持久在線，並靈活接入各類真實工作環境，可以藉鑑電腦系統中存算分離（Compute-Storage Separation）的思想，推進代理工作流程（agent Loop）的計算可以做成無狀態（即不用記住用家之前的對話歷史），不必讓執行環境跟著代理工作上雲，而讓「重狀態」的執行環境留在原地。
DeepSeek Harness提出，「超級代理」需符合4項特徵，包括主動無需等待使用者逐條傳達指令，能持續觀察環境事件並主動推動值得處理的事項，不需要介入時則保持安靜；高效率，互動回應迅速，同時能並行、高品質地完成多個複雜任務。無需等上一個指令或任務完成，就能接受下一條指令；連續，使用者可於直接在即時對話（IM）聊天，以及GitHub 評論等熟悉的工作介面與它交互，感覺始終只存在一個代理，不需要去想「SessionX的上下文中是否有Y資訊」。持久，始終在線、直接連接用戶真實的工作環境，並在長期運行中遇到異常時自動恢復。

# DeepSeek发布创作者模式，下一代大模型计划基于华为昇腾芯片预训练

“你的Harness，由你定义。”（Your Harness. You Define It）在发布智能体更新后，DeepSeek再次更新Creator Mode（创作者模式）。

11月2日，澎湃新闻记者获悉，DeepSeek Harness发布Creator Mode（创作者模式）演示视频，集中展示通过对话创建插件的能力，并公开七组演示的中英文提示词。

据DeepSeek在推送中介绍：“来认识DeepSeek Harness中的‘创造模式’，把想法转化为你能直接使用的插件：可以是设计工作台、沙盒游戏，或是一个3D大模型可视化工具，你会创造出什么？”

所谓Harness，是指围绕大语言模型构建的一套软件支撑框架，旨在帮助AI Agent管理和执行更加复杂的任务。简单来说，它可以被理解为让一个大模型真正成为Agent所需要的整套运行系统。

具体而言，此次展示的Creator Mode，是让用户通过对话创建自己的工具和界面。用户切换到Creator mode，在输入框里描述需求后就能打开插件，不同颜色的便签排列在画面里。输入内容、选择颜色，就能把想法添加到墙上，生成的插件可以从侧栏或会话中打开，以独立面板呈现。这也体现Harness“一切皆插件”的设计：通过安装或创建插件，扩展工具、技能和界面。

通俗来说，此次更新的创造模式，指的是用户口头描述一个需求，系统就能把它写成一个即插即用、可在桌面端运行的插件，典型例子正是文中提到的设计工作台、沙盒游戏、3D LLM可视化工具等。

此次展示进一步扩展DeepSeek Harness的使用场景：用户可通过对话创建插件，将设计、剪辑、阅读等工具接入日常工作，并按需调整应用界面。

此前澎湃新闻记者确认到，DeepSeek下一代大模型DeepSeek V5计划基于华为昇腾芯片进行预训练。此前华为昇腾芯片主要用于DeepSeek大模型的推理任务，V5将是其首款原生依托昇腾950开展训练的大模型。华为昇腾950系列分为950PR与950DT两款芯片，均基于第三代达芬奇架构，主要面向大模型的训练与推理场景。

10月31日，DeepSeekHarness团队在官方公众号发表技术文章《Super-agent设计探索：迈向更自主的Agent系统》。

DeepSeek表示，模型能力提升催生了新的应用形态，个人助手（Personal Agent）开始集中涌现。它们直接接入日常的消息、日程、邮件与工作平台，持续观察信息流并协助处理事务。这种持续在线、事件驱动的工作模式并不局限于个人场景，个人助手只是其中一类应用；在软件开发等商业场景中，它同样很有价值。

然而，现有主流Agent设计还难以在多任务和团队协作的规模上支撑这一模式，多任务上限取决于人的注意力。

Agent的工作模式仍然以单一Session为基本单位，不同Session之间彼此独立。当用户并行推进多项工作时，必须手动切换并记住各个Session的上下文，而据团队观察，一个人通常只能同时跟进3到5个活跃Session。在这种设计下，单任务的上限取决于模型能力，多任务的上限取决于人的注意力。

DeepSeek团队通过双层架构、事件驱动、异步多信道交互、存算分离与外部Watchdog，系统在底层接管了繁琐的会话管理与上下文同步，使人类得以从具体的执行细节进一步上移到更高层的决策与验收。DeepSeek把这种Agent形态及其系统架构称为Super-agent。

# 实测DeepSeek“创造模式”，插件门槛被干碎了

字母AI·2026年11月03日 20:40

又一个“许愿式”功能。

11月2日晚上，DSH官方在社交媒体上发了文称“你的Harness，你来定义”，同时发布了DSH的创造模式，并配了一支1分39秒的视频来介绍创造模式。

这个创造模式指的是让用户用自然语言描述一个想法，由Agent自己写代码、打包，并把它安装成DSH里能直接用的插件。

DeepSeek官方放出了7个演示，包括3D Transformer可视化、带多轨时间线的视频剪辑台、保留原版式的论文阅读器、海报设计工作台、3D 地标馆、能把整个界面换成像素风的主题插件，以及统计token和成本的用量仪表盘。

DeepSeek官方同时公开了这7个演示的中英文提示词，复制进去、选中创造模式就能复现。

严格说，这个模式并不是新东西。AI科技评论博主罗汉·保罗（Rohan Paul）表示，DSH的创造模式从8月开始就已经有了，11月2日新发的是演示视频和提示词。

其实早在10月2日Claude Code推出Mods功能时，崔添翼就发文表示庆祝，同时简单介绍了DSH创造模式的几大特点。比如用来改界面、改Agent循环机制，或增加新的编排方式。

所以这次发布的意义，更像是把一项潜伏已久的能力，以“创造模式”的身份单拎出来。

社区在经过测试之后，给了DSH创造模式“特别好评”。

比如中文区博主@NFT_Chen当天拿官方提示词实测了一轮，称3个插件都跑通了，3D地标馆约21分钟、花费0.38美元，海报工作台约10分钟、0.1美元，会话统计约11分钟、0.16美元。安装前会弹窗询问权限，点“允许一次”即可。

不过也有用户表示，创造模式还有改进的空间。

目前创造模式的运行逻辑是，Agent写完代码后会直接安装这个插件，所以如果Agent写的代码有bug，或者被恶意提示词诱导写了对电脑有危害的东西，那么就会对用户的电脑造成损害。

这个担忧本身是必要的，创造模式生成的是可执行插件，权限和代码安全本来就是问题，DeepSeek自己也承认，部分演示需要多轮打磨，且整个项目仍处于开发者预览阶段，核心插件和API可能出现破坏性变更。

科技媒体Startup Fortune认为，DeepSeek是在放大开源的优势。

创造模式和发布模型的逻辑是逆着来的，发布模型是AI厂商有什么技术，就往模型里塞什么技术。但是创造模式是使用者先提需求，然后再得到产品。供需关系刚好相反。

DeepSeek给出了DSH的骨架，用户和社区决定了DSH的样子。DSH的特点是一切皆为插件，它的界面是插件，工具也是插件。比起给DSH开发插件，倒不如直接让用户自己定义插件。

这样一来，使用者就会替DeepSeek造真正有需求的插件，然后DeepSeek可以通过插件市场的方式，上架这些产品。

通过创造模式，DeepSeek将开源普惠的市场策略，落地成了一种开发者生态。

创造模式所反映的，也正是DeepSeek目前的状态，把定义权交到开发者手里。

从10月开始，DeepSeek接连放出多款产品。从和V4.1 Flash 1017同步上线的搜索服务，再到开源了自家线上在用的推理框架DeepInfer、编解码组件deepseek-recipe。10月底，DSH又开源了Super Agent原型。

从底层模型到上层Agent，DeepSeek几乎每一层都在往外递。但“定义权”到底好不好用，光看官方演示和别人的测试还不够，我也亲自上手，用创造模式做了两个插件。

## 实测

创造模式的提示词逻辑和DeepSeek在V4.1 Flash 1017中提到的许愿式编程差不多，你不用描述这个插件具体要怎样，只需要描述你想要的最终成果就可以了。

不过话又说回来了，描述得越详细，这个插件的效果就越好。

DSH官方示例中，创造模式可以生成3D预览，还可以开发游戏。于是我将两者结合，选择创造模式后，仿照官方示例，给出以下提示词。

“创建一个带左侧边栏入口的DeepSeek Harness插件，做成可交互的3D演示游戏，用鲸鱼娘的形象搞个3D版马里奥。”

虽然鲸鱼娘的形象有点惨不忍睹，但是游戏质量很好，操作手感也很还原FC版本的马里奥。

从输入提示词开始算起，整个开发过程时间为1小时14分钟。

有了这次的经验，接下来我在使用创造模式的时候，会专门给DeepSeek找一些图片素材，让它能生成更符合大众审美的内容。

第二个提示词如下。

这个桌面宠物不仅可以互动，还能根据我和DeepSeek的聊天，给出一些有趣的反应。正如视频里所展示的那样，输入提示词之后，鲸鱼娘桌面宠物会提示DeepSeek正在思考。

当DeepSeek给出答案后，鲸鱼娘还会说“这一轮写完啦。要不要摸摸我，当作休息一下？”

但是这还没完，因为除了基本的互动外，DeepSeek还给这个鲸鱼娘三个属性，分别为“羁绊”、“心情”、“元气”。可以通过对话和交互提升这些属性，属性越高鲸鱼娘越开心，越低则会出现疲惫的情况，比如她会提示她累了，需要休息。

两个插件的提示词加一块也才100个字，许愿式编程还是太权威了。

不过在生成过程中需要多次点击“允许”，并没有像社区说的那样，可以点一次就不管了。即使我用了DSH的实验性自动审查插件，依然需要点很多次“允许”。

此外，这两个插件的开发过程中，DSH的缓存命中都是99%。两个插件加一块，总费用约为6块钱。

说起模型开发游戏，就不得不提Anthropic。

《大海捞针模拟器》的开发者在发布游戏试玩版后，其游戏被多位开发者使用Claude克隆后抢先上架，导致原版的《大海捞针模拟器》反而成了“仿品”。这位开发者甚至还收到勒索邮件，不少工作室因此取消了公开试玩。

10月底，Claude给用户发送通知，原文大意是：可以做原创游戏、某一类型的游戏、基于用户自己设计和素材的游戏，但不要复刻某款特定的现有游戏，即使改了名字或自称原创。

随后Anthropic工程师艾迪·奥斯马尼（Addy Osmani）表示情况属实，Anthropic在Opus 5.5运行Claude Code时，会给系统提示词加这么两句话，以防止用户在使用Claude时，侵犯知识产权、违反使用规则。

回到创造模式本身，即便还有权限确认繁琐、生成素材审美不稳定这类小问题，但是它拉低插件开发门槛的效果是实打实的。

创造模式刚好填上了 “脑子里的小想法” 和 “工具” 之间的空白。想到什么，或者发现什么问题，直接说给DSH的创造模式，让它来帮你解决。

还有一点，目前为止，DSH没有官方的插件市场。仅提供了“自定义插件索引源”的底层机制。

用户可以在设置中开启实验性的自定义插件市场功能，手动添加第三方维护的索引地址，实现插件的浏览、搜索与一键安装。

DeepSeek官方也没有官方统一的插件分发平台。

有了创造模式，民间大神们难免会跑出高频实用爆款插件，这可能也会倒逼DSH开插件市场。

无论如何，至少对普通用户来说，现在随手就能给自己的DSH定制点专属小功能，这件事本身就足够有新鲜感。

本文来自微信公众号“字母AI”，作者：苗正，36氪经授权发布。

DeepSeek.content:
## 新浪财经

# 乌镇峰会观察：中国开源AI大模型持续“圈粉”

中新社浙江乌镇11月3日电 (记者 刘亮)2026年世界互联网大会乌镇峰会(下称乌镇峰会)3日开幕。围绕人工智能(AI)开源生态话题的火热讨论，在这个千年古镇持续回响。

说到开源，不得不提中国AI大模型。它们凭借高性能、低价格，近年来在全球范围内持续“圈粉”。

深度求索(DeepSeek)研究工程师高熙指出，从最初的聊天和翻译功能，到如今的深度逻辑推理、解决用户实际生活中的难题，中国AI大模型的发展速度超乎人们想象，几乎每一年都比前一年有更多技术创新进步。

数据印证了中国AI开源大模型的受欢迎程度。全球AI模型聚合平台OpenRouter统计，上周(10月26日至11月1日)中国大模型词元(Token)调用量已连续27周超过美国。同期，在全球AI大模型Token周总调用量排名前五的模型中，中国AI大模型占据四席，DeepSeek位居榜首。

11月3日，参观者在开源主题生态体验馆参观。近日，2026年世界互联网大会乌镇峰会·开源主题生态体验馆在浙江乌镇亮相。 中新社记者 王刚 摄

全球移动通信系统协会董事长洪曜庄(John Hoffman)表示，中国一些大语言模型和正在开发的小语言模型均取得了很大进展，且中国许多模型基于开源平台开发。

德国明斯特大学教授贝恩德·霍尔茨纳格尔(Bernd Holznagel)是DeepSeek的用户。他观察到，现在美国硅谷许多公司及德国近半数中小企业都在使用中国开源AI大模型。

“中国开源模型综合性能好、推理效率高，在全球具备很强竞争力。”阿里巴巴集团联合创始人、董事会主席蔡崇信指出，过去一年，全球AI使用场景不断向工业制造、医疗健康、公共服务、企业办公、科技研发等领域延伸。中国科技企业持续加大模型开源和生态开放力度，开源模型下载量、衍生模型数等关键指标保持领先。

与会人士普遍认为，如果AI技术被锁在“小院高墙”内，创新之火便难以燎原，这最终将阻碍全球科技进步。而“开源”趋势，未来将为AI创新打开更大想象空间。

蔡崇信指出，开源能够降低中小企业研发成本，特别是新兴经济体的开发者可基于开源模型，较快创建本国AI应用。他举例称，乌干达一家非营利组织基于千问模型开发本地语言模型，已覆盖68种非洲语言，帮助更多人突破语言限制、接触AI技术。

阿里巴巴ATH事业群千问大语言模型项目负责人刘大一恒直言，如果没有开源，AI大模型的核心技术或许只掌握在少数人和少数企业手里。

他表示，而如今，开源让缺乏资源的学者和学生，能以更低成本获取前沿知识、参与技术创新；头部AI公司可能忽略的小语种、特殊垂类应用或特定硬件适配问题，可通过开源社区的集体智慧共享得到解决；开源模型的高性价比，也有助于防止市场价格垄断发生。(完)
