# 2026年阿里云双十一活动入口、政策：通义千问 Qwen3.8-Flash 优惠折扣与选型方案解析

2026-11-03 3

简介： Qwen3.8-Flash作为通义千问高性价比主力模型，在本次双十一给出了分层优惠方案，兼顾临时测试、轻量开发、企业批量处理多种场景。理清按量节省计划、Token Plan订阅、夜间折扣、缓存折扣四套福利的生效范围，把离线批量推理任务调度到夜间执行，提前做好用量预估，就可以最大化利用双十一优惠，用更低的成本搭建RAG知识库、轻量智能体、代码辅助应用。

Qwen3.8-Flash是通义千问3.8系列主打高吞吐、高性价比的MoE模型，支持最高百万Token超长上下文窗口，兼顾推理速度与成本优势，适合RAG知识库、轻量智能体、批量文档处理、日常代码辅助等场景，也是本次2026阿里云双十一百炼平台主推的性价比款模型。和定位深度复杂推理的Qwen3.8-Max不同，Qwen3.8-Flash的原生单价更低，同时同步开放按量节省计划、Token Plan订阅抵扣、Night Plan夜间4折、上下文缓存折扣、新用户免费额度多重优惠，两套计费通道相互独立，优惠规则不能互通混用，很多开发者容易混淆两套体系的消耗倍率、折扣生效条件。本文围绕双十一活动周期、两套计费模式优惠细则、缓存优惠、夜间折扣叠加限制、场景选型、用量监控方法完整解析，搭配可直接运行的CLI查询命令，方便独立开发者、开发小组、中小企业评估调用成本，合理规划Qwen3.8-Flash的使用方案。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

本次Qwen3.8-Flash相关优惠周期和云上双十一大促保持一致，从预热阶段开启，持续至11月30日，所有折扣、节省计划新购、Token Plan订阅特惠、免费额度申领都需要在活动周期内操作。优惠入口集中在百炼Model Studio双十一会场，登录阿里云控制台，通过首页双十一banner跳转AI专场，即可找到Qwen3.8-Flash体验与优惠专区；新实名账号进入页面可以直接领取专属免费Token额度，先测试模型吞吐能力、评估Credits消耗速度，再选择按量付费或者Token Plan订阅方案，降低试错成本。该模型支持思考模式与普通问答模式，思考模式会产生额外推理Token，预估用量的时候需要把这部分消耗纳入预算。

### 2026年阿里云双十一活动入口：

2026年阿里云双十一活动入口 | 核心功能 | 适配人群  
---|---|---
阿里云双十一活动主会场入口 https://t.aliyun.com/U/hNZNGM | 阿里云轻量应用服务器、阿里云ECS云服务器、阿里云GPU云服务器、阿里云百炼大模型服务平台特惠机型一键选购 | 新客首购、免费试用、秒杀抢购  
云服务器活动主会场入口 https://t.aliyun.com/U/tj0Y6d | 阿里云大模型服务平台、阿里云轻量应用服务器、阿里云ECS云服务器、阿里云GPU云服务器特惠机型一键选购 | 新客首购、免费试用、秒杀抢购  
综合权益中心入口 https://t.aliyun.com/U/Qu7Kql | AI权益+云产品权益双轨并行，Token Plan、千问办公、万小智AI建站等一网打尽 | 新老用户均可，尤其适合AI应用探索者  
99计划专场入口 https://t.aliyun.com/U/qISm14 | 99元e实例与199元u1实例新购续费同价，锁价至2030年 | 个人开发者、中小企业长期持有  

Qwen3.8-Flash分为原生按量付费、Token Plan统一Credits订阅两套独立计费通道，双十一优惠分开执行，额度互不通用。

第一套：原生按量付费模式，适合调用量波动大、不想包月订阅的用户。Qwen3.8-Flash原生定价本身具备优势，输入每百万Token 0.8元，输出每百万Token 2.7元，同时自带上下文缓存折扣，缓存命中之后输入Token计费大幅降低，非常适合RAG、多轮对话这类重复加载上下文的业务场景。双十一期间上线AI通用节省计划，这份节省计划支持包含Qwen3.8-Flash在内的150多款百炼平台模型，包季档位最低至4.5折，购买之后自动抵扣按量调用账单，不需要额外配置，每次调用优先消耗节省计划额度，额度耗尽之后恢复原价计费。缓存折扣和节省计划可以叠加，进一步压低长文档、知识库场景的开销。

第二套：Token Plan订阅抵扣模式，也是本次双十一主推方案，包月统一Credits额度，Qwen3.8-Flash调用按照固定倍率扣减Credits，和按量付费体系相互独立。双十一Token Plan套餐本身有新客首购5折福利，Lite、Essential、Standard、Pro四档套餐都可以调用Qwen3.8-Flash，档位越高月度Credits额度越多，支持的Agent并发数量越高。其中Essential及以上套餐自带Harness工具权限，搭配Qwen3.8-Flash可以直接使用联网检索、代码解释器、文件解析等扩展能力，非常适合Hermes Agent、OpenClaw、轻量RAG项目开发。抵扣顺序为优先消耗当月套餐Credits，额度耗尽之后自动抵扣提前购买的补充用量包；套餐和用量包全部耗尽，调用直接暂停，不会自动切换按量付费产生意外账单；当月剩余Credits不会结转，订阅周期结束自动清零。

本次Qwen3.8-Flash一大亮点就是纳入Night Plan夜间限时4折优惠，北京时间每晚22:00至次日早上8:00期间调用该模型，Token Plan体系下Credits消耗直接打4折，仅消耗白天六成额度，和Qwen3.8-Max共享同一个夜间优惠时段。该权益不需要手动开通，订阅Token Plan之后到点自动生效，适合批量文档摘要、代码仓库扫描、知识库向量化整理、素材批量生成这类不需要实时响应的离线任务，把大批量任务调度到夜间执行，可以显著降低月度AI开销。需要重点区分：夜间4折只在Token Plan订阅体系内生效，原生按量付费通道调用Qwen3.8-Flash不享受夜间折扣，只能使用节省计划+缓存折扣来降本。

除折扣之外，新用户福利规则清晰：首次体验Qwen3.8-Flash的实名账号，可以领取免费体验额度，有效期90天，免费额度仅支持原生按量通道，不能在Token Plan订阅里面使用，额度用完之后自动转为正常计费。免费额度适合简单验证模型吞吐、调试Prompt、测试API连通性，不适合长期高频调用。

下面梳理优惠叠加的限制规则，也是高频踩坑点。首先，夜间4折仅作用于Token Plan的Credits消耗，按量节省计划和夜间折扣不能叠加；其次，Token Plan套餐折扣和按量节省计划相互独立，账单互不抵扣；代金券可以用于Token Plan订阅订单或者节省计划采购订单，单笔订单仅能使用一张满减券；套餐升配即时生效，差额按照订阅剩余天数折算扣费，降配要等到当前订阅周期结束之后才生效；Token Plan订阅订单不支持无理由退款，下单前一定要先用免费额度实测Qwen3.8-Flash的Credits消耗速度，避免档位选择过高造成额度浪费。另外，Qwen3.8-Flash虽然性价比高，但复杂数学推理、深度多步骤逻辑任务的效果弱于Qwen3.8-Max，选型的时候需要区分业务场景，不要盲目用Flash替代Max。

场景选型建议清晰易懂。独立开发者、偶尔调用、任务量不稳定，优先原生按量付费，搭配4.5折AI节省计划，随用随付，没有包月压力；搭建RAG知识库、轻量Agent、高频代码辅助，每天稳定调用，优先选购Token Plan套餐，搭配夜间4折调度批量任务，成本可控；小团队内部业务、批量数据处理，优先Token Plan团队版席位，支持成员权限隔离、独立API Key分配、用量看板统计；短期Demo验证、方案测试，直接使用新用户免费额度，不需要付费；高并发在线问答、客服对话，结合缓存折扣，优先按量模式搭配节省计划。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

开发者可以使用阿里云CLI命令，查询订阅信息、Qwen3.8-Flash调用用量、API Key、优惠券，用来做自动化监控、账单预估，下面命令可以直接复制执行。
查看账号内百炼订阅、Token Plan套餐信息：
aliyun bailian ListSubscriptions --Output json

查询指定周期Qwen3.8-Flash的调用消耗明细，评估Credits消耗速度：
aliyun bailian ListUsageRecords --StartTime "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z" --EndTime "2026-11-30T23:59:59Z" --ModelId qwen3.8-flash --Output json

查询账号可用代金券，确认是否可以用于订阅或者节省计划采购：
aliyun bssopenapi QueryCouponList --Output json

获取百炼平台API Key，用于本地Agent、代码项目接入Qwen3.8-Flash：
aliyun bailian GetApiKey --Output json

最后总结几个实操避坑要点。第一，两套计费通道相互隔离，按量节省计划和Token Plan额度互不通用；第二，夜间4折仅限Token Plan体系，按量调用没有该权益；第三，开启思考模式之后Token消耗明显上涨，批量任务预估额度时必须预留余量；第四，上下文缓存折扣仅在按量通道生效，Token Plan内缓存命中只会间接减少Credits消耗，没有单独标注缓存折扣；第五，Qwen3.8-Flash主打性价比吞吐，复杂深度推理任务建议切换Qwen3.8-Max；第六，补充用量包不能单独购买，必须绑定一份有效Token Plan主套餐。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

Qwen3.8-Flash作为通义千问高性价比主力模型，在本次双十一给出了分层优惠方案，兼顾临时测试、轻量开发、企业批量处理多种场景。理清按量节省计划、Token Plan订阅、夜间折扣、缓存折扣四套福利的生效范围，把离线批量推理任务调度到夜间执行，提前做好用量预估，就可以最大化利用双十一优惠，用更低的成本搭建RAG知识库、轻量智能体、代码辅助应用。

Qwen.content:
# Alibaba Cloud (Qwen)

Alibaba Cloud's DashScope API provides OpenAI-compatible access to Qwen language models. Use OpenAI provider options supported by your chosen model.

## Setup

To use Alibaba Cloud's API, set theDASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file:
export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

## Configuration

The provider uses OpenAI provider options; support varies by model. Example:
providers:
  - alibaba:qwen3.8-max # Simple usage
  - id: alibaba:qwen3.7-plus # Aliases: alicloud:, aliyun:, dashscope:
    config:
      temperature: 0.7
      apiKey: your_api_key_here # Alternative to DASHSCOPE_API_KEY environment variable
      apiBaseUrl: https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 # Optional: Override default API base URL

note

The equivalent provider prefixes arealicloud:, aliyun:, and dashscope:. For new configurations, Alibaba recommends qwen3.7-plus for balanced use, qwen3.8-flash for lower cost, or qwen3.8-max for stronger reasoning. Check the model catalog for your region; model availability differs by region.

If you're using the Alibaba Cloud Beijing region console, switch the base URL tohttps://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 instead of the international endpoint.

## Supported Models

The built-in Alibaba provider implements OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and text embeddings. The catalog below also lists separate realtime, speech recognition, and image generation services. Listing a model here does not add those endpoints to this provider. Choose a model supported by your selected endpoint and region.

### Qwen 3 Flagship

- qwen3.8-max / qwen3.8-max-0902 - Current flagship with text, image, and video input and a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.8-flash - Faster Qwen3.8 model with a 1M-token context window
- qwen3.7-plus / qwen3.7-plus-2026-05-26 - General-purpose model with thinking, vision, and tool calling
- qwen3.7-flash / qwen3.7-flash-2026-07-15 - Lower-cost Qwen3.7 model
- qwen3.7-max / qwen3.7-max-2026-06-08 - Previous flagship
- qwen3.6-plus / qwen3.6-flash and qwen3.5-plus / qwen3.5-flash - Previous model families
- qwen3-max - Supports reasoning and tool calling
- qwen3-max-preview - Preview version with thinking mode support
- qwen3-max-2025-09-23 - September 2025 snapshot
- qwen-max - 32K context (30,720 in, 8,192 out)
- qwen-max-latest - Always updated to latest version
- qwen-max-2025-01-25 - January 2025 snapshot
- qwen-plus / qwen-plus-latest - 128K-1M context (thinking & non-thinking modes)
- qwen-plus-2025-09-11, qwen-plus-2025-07-28, qwen-plus-2025-07-14, qwen-plus-2025-04-28, qwen-plus-2025-01-25 - Dated snapshots
- qwen-flash / qwen-flash-2025-07-28 - Latency-optimized general model
- qwen-turbo / qwen-turbo-latest / qwen-turbo-2025-04-28 / qwen-turbo-2024-11-01 - Earlier low-latency model; see qwen-flash
- qwen-long-latest / qwen-long-2025-01-25 - 10M context for long-text analysis, summarization, and extraction

### Qwen 3 Omni & Realtime

- qwen3.8-omni-flash - Text output from text, image, audio, and video input through Chat Completions; use the separate realtime API for qwen3.8-omni-flash-realtime
- qwen3-omni-flash / qwen3-omni-flash-2025-09-15 - Supports speech and vision in thinking and non-thinking modes
- qwen3-omni-flash-realtime / qwen3-omni-flash-realtime-2025-09-15 - Streaming realtime with audio stream input and VAD
- qwen3-omni-30b-a3b-captioner - Dedicated audio captioning model (speech, ambient sounds, music)
- qwen2.5-omni-7b - Qwen2.5-based multimodal model with text, image, speech, and video inputs

### Reasoning & Research

- qwq-plus - Alibaba's reasoning model (commercial)
- qwq-32b - Open-source QwQ reasoning model trained on Qwen2.5
- qwq-32b-preview - Experimental QwQ research model (2024)
- qwen-deep-research - Long-form research assistant with web search
- qvq-max / qvq-max-latest / qvq-max-2025-03-25 - Visual reasoning models (commercial)
- qvq-72b-preview - Experimental visual reasoning research model
- DeepSeek models (hosted by Alibaba Cloud):
- deepseek-v4.1-flash / deepseek-v4-pro-0813 - Current hosted Flash and Pro models; these IDs differ from the direct DeepSeek API
- deepseek-v3.2-exp / deepseek-v3.1 / deepseek-v3 - DeepSeek V3 models
- deepseek-r1 / deepseek-r1-0528 - DeepSeek reasoning models
- deepseek-r1-distill-qwen-{1.5b,7b,14b,32b} - Distilled on Qwen2.5
- deepseek-r1-distill-llama-{8b,70b} - Distilled on Llama

### Vision & Multimodal

Commercial:

- qwen3-vl-plus / qwen3-vl-plus-2025-09-23 - High-res image support with long context (thinking & non-thinking modes)
- qwen3-vl-flash / qwen3-vl-flash-2025-10-15 - Fast vision model with thinking mode support
- qwen-vl-max - 7.5K context, 1,280 tokens/image
- qwen-vl-plus - High-res image support
- qwen-vl-ocr - OCR-optimized for documents, tables, handwriting (30+ languages)

Open-source:

- qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-thinking / qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct - 235B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen3-vl-32b-thinking / qwen3-vl-32b-instruct - 32B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen3-vl-30b-a3b-thinking / qwen3-vl-30b-a3b-instruct - 30B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen3-vl-8b-thinking / qwen3-vl-8b-instruct - 8B parameter Qwen3-VL
- qwen2.5-vl-{72b,7b,3b}-instruct - Qwen 2.5 VL series

### Audio & Speech

- qwen3-asr-flash / qwen3-asr-flash-2025-09-08 - Multilingual speech recognition (11 languages, Chinese dialects)
- qwen3-asr-flash-realtime / qwen3-asr-flash-realtime-2025-10-27 - Real-time speech recognition with automatic language detection
- qwen3-omni-flash-realtime - Supports speech streaming with VAD

### Coding & Math

Commercial:

- qwen3-coder-plus / qwen3-coder-plus-2025-09-23 / qwen3-coder-plus-2025-07-22 - Coding agents with tool calling
- qwen3-coder-flash / qwen3-coder-flash-2025-07-28 - Fast code generation
- qwen-math-plus / qwen-math-plus-latest / qwen-math-plus-2024-09-19 / qwen-math-plus-2024-08-16 - Math problem solving
- qwen-math-turbo / qwen-math-turbo-latest / qwen-math-turbo-2024-09-19 - Fast math reasoning
- qwen-mt-{plus,turbo} - Machine translation (92 languages)
- qwen-doc-turbo - Document mining and structured extraction

Open-source:

- qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct / qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct - Open-source Qwen3 coder models
- qwen2.5-math-{72b,7b,1.5b}-instruct - Math-focused models with CoT/PoT/TIR reasoning

### Qwen 2.5 Series

All support 131K context (129,024 in, 8,192 out)

- qwen2.5-{72b,32b,14b,7b}-instruct
- qwen2.5-{7b,14b}-instruct-1m

### Qwen 2 Series

- qwen2-72b-instruct - 131K context
- qwen2-57b-a14b-instruct - 65K context
- qwen2-7b-instruct - 131K context

### Qwen 1.5 Series

8K context (6K in, 2K out)

- qwen1.5-{110b,72b,32b,14b,7b}-chat

### Qwen 3 Open-source Models

Open-source Qwen3 models with thinking mode support:

- qwen3-next-80b-a3b-thinking / qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct - Next-gen 80B (September 2025)
- qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507 / qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507 - 235B July 2025 versions
- qwen3-30b-a3b-thinking-2507 / qwen3-30b-a3b-instruct-2507 - 30B July 2025 versions
- qwen3-235b-a22b - 235B with dual-mode support (thinking/non-thinking)
- qwen3-32b - 32B dual-mode model
- qwen3-30b-a3b - 30B dual-mode model
- qwen3-14b, qwen3-8b, qwen3-4b - Smaller dual-mode models
- qwen3-1.7b, qwen3-0.6b - Edge/mobile models

### Third-party Models

Kimi (Moonshot AI):

- kimi-k3 - Current Kimi model
- kimi-k2.6 - Previous Kimi model with a 256K context window
- moonshot-kimi-k2-instruct - First open-source trillion-parameter MoE model in China (activates 32B parameters)

Z.AI (GLM):ZHIPU/GLM-5.3 and glm-5.2. Check the regional model catalog for access and endpoint requirements.

### Embeddings

Usealibaba:embedding:<model> for embeddings. The alibaba:<model> shorthand sends chat requests.

- text-embedding-v3 - 1,024d vectors, 8,192 token limit, 50+ languages
- text-embedding-v4 - Latest Qwen3-Embedding with flexible dimensions (64-2048d), 100+ languages
- qwen3.7-text-embedding - Newer Qwen3.7 text embeddings; availability depends on the region

defaultTest:
  options:
    provider:
      embedding:
        id: alibaba:embedding:text-embedding-v4

### Image Generation

Thealibaba provider does not call image-generation endpoints. To use models such as qwen-image-plus, configure the HTTP provider for Alibaba's image API.

See the DashScope model catalog for availability.

## Additional Configuration

Put DashScope-specific request fields underconfig.passthrough. For example, enable_thinking controls thinking mode on Qwen3.8 and Qwen3.7 chat models:
providers:
  - id: alibaba:qwen3.8-max
    config:
      passthrough:
        enable_thinking: true

Standard OpenAI parameters (temperature, max_tokens) are supported. Base URL:https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 (or https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 for the Beijing region).

For API usage details, see Alibaba Cloud documentation.

Qwen.content:
# Alibaba has finally secured the deal with Apple

未来之地2026-11-03 07:39

A new Alibaba with a 2-trillion valuation is emerging.

After two years of twists and turns, Alibaba has finally secured the long-coveted partnership with Apple!

On October 31, Apple and Alibaba announced a cooperation agreement to integrate Qwen into Apple Intelligence.

When Tim Cook finally gave the nod to allow Qwen's code to run on the China-market iPhone models, this is far more than the conclusion of a business partnership, but rather a metaphor for an era.

In smartphones, the most intimate terminal for human beings, China's large model has finally obtained a ticket to the future.

But on the back of this ticket lies a footnote that few people dare to face directly: the road to Artificial Super Intelligence (ASI) is a one-way tunnel paved with trillions of capital and massive computing power.

Over a month ago, Wu Yongming proposed the "20GW" figure at the Yunqi Conference; Zhang Yiming made unrestrained, cost-agnostic bets within ByteDance; Liang Wenfeng was advancing silently at full speed behind DeepSeek. They seem to be telling different stories, but in essence, they are all heading for the same destiny.

This is not only a battle of faith around the Scaling Law, but also a brutal capital war.

When the former king of e-commerce tries to forge a new king in the silicon-based wasteland, a new Alibaba with a 2-trillion-yuan scale is gradually taking shape in this high-stakes gamble.

1、

Qwen's integration into Apple has been officially confirmed. Starting from November 4, these features will be open for testing with the latest iOS developer Beta version, and will be launched for Chinese users when the official iOS 27.3 is released in December.

At that time, Chinese users can directly call Qwen's capabilities including text and image understanding, content generation in Siri, writing tools and visual intelligence.

After a full year of anxiety at the application layer, this is probably the most exciting moment for Alibaba's AI business this year. It means that Alibaba's intelligence has finally truly entered the pockets of countless people.

Why Qwen? In this two-year-long "eight-select-one" selection process, Apple had many alternatives, including DeepSeek, Doubao, Baidu, Kimi... and finally, Apple chose Alibaba.

What Apple values far more than Qwen's ranking on the benchmark leaderboards is the unfathomable hidden card behind it — the full-stack AI infrastructure that integrates large models, chips and cloud computing as a whole.

The open-source family of Qwen large models has accumulated billions of downloads, growing into one of the world's largest open-source communities. The team is advancing recursive self-improvement, with the parameter scale expanding to 5 trillion to 10 trillion.

T-Head released its AI chip Zhenwu V900 in September, whose computing power is three times that of the previous generation. It will go into mass production in the first quarter of 2027, and the cumulative shipment of the Zhenwu series has reached 470,000 units. Deutsche Bank estimates that its material cost is about 40% lower than that of NVIDIA H20.

What connects all these parts is cloud computing. At the Yunqi Conference on September 22, Wu Yongming announced that by 2032, the total computing power of data centers operated by Alibaba Cloud will exceed 20 gigawatts, equivalent to a quarter of the total global computing power today. According to Gartner's statistics, Alibaba Cloud has already captured 32.8% of China's cloud market share, ranking first.

However, amid the hustle and bustle since the beginning of this year, Alibaba's AI seems to have been relatively low-key. While ByteDance's Doubao has set off wave after wave of popularity on short video and social platforms, and native AI companies such as Kimi have updated their large models time and again, Alibaba rarely competes for attention in the C-end traffic field.

The implementation of the cooperation between Apple and Qwen has finally let the market see Alibaba's strength. Wu Yongming's "20 gigawatts" figure further declares Alibaba's ambition: to move towards ASI.

20GW is equivalent to the power generation capacity of 10 Three Gorges Dams, or a super brain that can support the computing power demand at the level of human civilization.

Among the players pursuing ASI (Artificial Super Intelligence), Alibaba, ByteDance and DeepSeek, the three most determined players, have almost unanimously chosen the same path: fully committed to the Scaling Law.

Zhang Yiming has long calculated the accounts clearly inside ByteDance. The Seed team does not need to explain ROI to business departments. ByteDance's annual 200-billion-yuan investment in computing power is buying the ticket to "recursive self-improvement".

Liang Wenfeng and DeepSeek have pushed all their chips to the deep water zone at the bottom of the model. The 105.5 billion yuan of financing is not spent on PPTs, but on real parameters and computing power clusters.

These three paths all lead to the same destination: heavy assets.

There are no shortcuts in this logic. It means 5 to 10 years of continuous operation and maintenance in the future, which is a trillion-yuan level long march.

They are all betting that the Scaling Law curve will not break suddenly at a certain inflection point, and that when the computing power reaches the critical point, intelligence will gush out from the crevices of the rocks by itself, just like water.

2、

On the other side of this story, it is also a capital war that no one can quit. What it competes for is not whose PPT is more attractive, but who has thicker cash flow and more sophisticated capital operation capabilities.

Alibaba is obviously the most well-equipped heavy armored knight in this war.

Many people have forgotten that Alibaba is first and foremost a money printing machine.

Even in today's fiercely competitive e-commerce industry, Alibaba can still generate hundreds of billions of yuan in free cash flow every year.

This is the confidence for it to dare to write the 20GW target into its strategic plan. When others are still running around for the next round of financing, Alibaba can directly draw funds from its e-commerce profit pool to nourish the roots of AI.

But profits alone are not enough, the capital market needs to see determination. That's why we saw the HKD 80 billion share placement. Alibaba's largest capital operation in seven years!

This is not a simple loan, it is a signal flare jointly sent to the market by Joseph Tsai and Wu Yongming.

They are telling everyone: we are willing to dilute our current equity in exchange for a ticket to the future.

What is more subtle is that while Joseph Tsai and Wu Yongming carried out the share placement, they also made real-money increases in their holdings on the secondary market.

The implication of this combination of moves is crystal clear: we are determined to win this war.

In comparison, although DeepSeek has the financing capability supported by national-level platforms, policy backing and long-term capital, it is more like a special forces soldier carrying out targeted blasting on a specific highland.

Alibaba, on the other hand, aims to fight a full-scale war, advancing simultaneously on all battlefields of e-commerce, cloud, AI, logistics and local life services.

This is extremely difficult.

From the king of e-commerce to the standard-bearer of AI, there is huge organizational inertia, countless people's doubts, and the risk that the technical route may collapse at any time.

But Wu Yongming and Joseph Tsai seem to be fully prepared.

They are well aware that the road to ASI is destined to be lonely. At this stage, there are no applauses, only the roaring noise of servers; there are no flowers, only the constantly jumping electricity bills.

But they still move forward without hesitation.

Because in that 20GW blueprint, there hides another new Alibaba with a trillion-yuan scale.

3、

From the king of e-commerce to the heavyweight AI asset giant, Alibaba is undergoing a fateful transformation. The old Alibaba with trillion-yuan revenue is still there, and another new Alibaba with trillion-yuan revenue is growing up.

In March this year, Wu Yongming revealed at the earnings call that in the next five years, the commercial revenue of cloud and AI including MaaS will exceed 100 billion US dollars.

If the 20GW computing power is fully put into operation, according to the current pricing and call volume of MaaS (Model as a Service), it will be able to generate trillions of yuan in external commercial revenue.

When this 1-trillion-yuan AI increment is superimposed on Alibaba's originally stable trillion-yuan e-commerce basic market, a super species with annual revenue exceeding 2 trillion yuan will have a clear outline.

In China's current technology landscape, no company has yet crossed the threshold of 2 trillion yuan in annual revenue.

Even ByteDance, which is extremely prominent at the moment, recorded total annual revenue of about 1.3 trillion to 1.4 trillion yuan in 2025; the three giants of JD, Alibaba and Tencent have annual revenue of 1.3 trillion yuan, 1 trillion yuan and 750 billion yuan respectively; as for rising stars such as Meituan and Pinduoduo, they are still fighting in the 300 billion to 400 billion yuan range.

On the global stage, there are only three or four technology companies with annual revenue exceeding 2 trillion yuan, including Amazon, Apple, Google, and Microsoft has just crossed the line.

In the past, Alibaba relied on GMV to support its trillion-yuan market value, and defined itself as the king of e-commerce with a transaction volume of 8 trillion yuan. That was the glory of the last era.

But now, Alibaba is trying to use computing power, models and intelligence to build another trillion-yuan skeleton in the silicon-based world.

Qwen.title: 把通义千问接进工单系统：三个版本够用，但有两个坑没人提前告诉我
Qwen.description: 把通义千问接进工单系统：三个版本够用 ... 通义千问的接口（Qwen API）是 OpenAI 兼容的，这一点省了非常多事。我们不需要为每个版本写一套客户端，只改model 这个字符串。
Qwen.content:
# 把通义千问接进工单系统：三个版本够用，但有两个坑没人提前告诉我

我们公司的工单系统跑了六年，去年年底加了一个 AI 助手：客服把用户的话粘进去，自动判断该派给哪个组、紧急程度几级、要不要拉人。

一开始很朴素——所有请求都丢给同一个模型。跑了两周，账单下来了，我盯着那个数字看了很久，然后决定重做。

不是模型不好。是我们把一个需要"想得很深"的活和一个只需要"归个类"的活，交给了同一个脑子。

## 一、先看一个很土但很有用的分法

工单系统的 AI 请求，拆开看其实只有三类：

类型 | 占请求量 | 特点 
---|---|---
分类打标 | 71% | 输出只有几个字段，不需要推理 
摘要改写 | 22% | 中等长度输入，输出 100 字左右 
疑难判断 | 7% | 长上下文，需要跨多轮记录找线索 

这三类的成本不该一样。但当时我们是一个价。

改完之后，71% 的请求走通义千问里最小的那个版本，22% 走中间档，只有 7% 走大版本。月度 token 花费从 4,180 元降到 1,590 元，降了 62%。

而工单分类的准确率——从 91.2% 涨到 93.7%。是的，涨了。因为小模型在"输入很短、任务很明确"的分类上，反而更少自作聪明。

这一点当时挺意外，后来想通了：大模型的问题不是不够聪明，是有时候太聪明，会给你一个"更合理但不是你要的"答案。

## 二、接法：一份代码，三个模型名

通义千问的接口（Qwen API）是 OpenAI 兼容的，这一点省了非常多事。我们不需要为每个版本写一套客户端，只改model 这个字符串。
python 代码解读复制代码import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://api.tokenfreeai.com/v1",   # OpenAI 兼容，换服务只改这一行
)

ROUTE = {
    "classify": "qwen-turbo",     # 分类打标，71%
    "summarize": "qwen-plus",     # 摘要改写，22%
    "reason":    "qwen-max",      # 疑难判断，7%
}

def ask(task: str, prompt: str, **kw):
    return client.chat.completions.create(
        model=ROUTE[task],
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        **kw,
    )

调用方传的不是模型名，是任务名。这个抽象很重要——它意味着以后换模型，改的是这张表，不是散落在四十几个文件里的字符串。

上线三个月，这张表改过五次。如果没有这层，那五次就会变成四十个文件的 diff。

## 三、坑一：长文本不是"上下文更长"，是"计价方式不一样"

这个是真正让我吃了一次亏的地方。

工单里有不少"疑难判断"要读历史记录，一条对话可能几万字。我一开始想得很简单——找个支持长上下文的版本，把整段丢进去不就行了。

于是我把 7% 的疑难工单全切到长文本版本，跑了三天，成本没降反升，而且升得很多。

原因在计价结构上：长文本模型的输入单价和你按普通模型算出来的完全不是一回事。 我原来按"普通模型贵一点"估的，实际结算是另一套折算，超出的部分比我想的狠。

后来改成两步：先用普通版本对历史记录做一次压缩，把 3 万字的对话压成 800 字的摘要，再交给长文本版本判断。成本回到预期，判断质量几乎没掉——因为对"该派给谁"这个问题，原始对话里 95% 的内容是噪音。

一个通用结论：上下文长度是能力，不是免费的容量。  能用摘要解决的事，别用长上下文硬扛。

这也是我用 token 计费这件事上最实在的一课：单价表看起来简单，但输入长度、输出长度、缓存命中，每一项都在改最终数字。RFC 里没写的那部分，得自己跑一个月账单才看得见。

## 四、坑二：结构化输出的 strict 模式，不是所有版本都一致

工单分类的输出必须是机器能吃的。我们用的是结构化输出，JSON Schema 写死字段：group、urgency、need_escalate。

问题出在小版本上。同一份 Schema，大版本老老实实按字段返回，小版本偶尔会：

- 把urgency 从整数变成 "3" 字符串
- 在 JSON 外面包一层 ```json 代码块
- 字段顺序乱掉（这个其实不影响，但我们的老解析器按位置取的）

第三个是我们的问题，前两个是真实的兼容性差异。

解决方式很土：在代码里做一次归一化，不指望模型。 字符串数字转整数，剥掉代码块包裹，按 key 取值不用位置。二十行代码，比换模型便宜得多。

教训：不要假设"同一个接口"等于"同一个行为"。  版本间的差异往往不在能力上，在边界情况的处理上。

## 五、限流和并发：这件事比模型选择更影响体验

我们做过一次线上观测：真正让客服抱怨"这个 AI 好慢"的请求里，只有三成是真的模型慢，另外七成是在队列里等。

原因是并发开太大。我们把并发从 32 调到 12，同时加了两个东西：

一是超时降档——超过 2.5 秒没拿到首字，换一个小版本先回一个"正在分析"，后台继续跑。用户看到的是有反应，不是转圈。

二是按任务分级排队——分类打标这类短请求走快队列，疑难判断走慢队列，互不占坑。以前一个疑难工单会把后面二十个分类请求全堵住。

改完之后，端到端 P95 从 6.8 秒降到 2.1 秒。这个 2.1 秒里，首字延迟占 1.3 秒左右，剩下的是网络和渲染。

代码里的地址和密钥是一个入口一套，账单按子密钥分了"工单分类"和"疑难判断"两个账本，月底对账不用再拿 Excel 拆。我这边用的是词元云（tokenfreeai.com），几个版本在同一个密钥下面，做这种按任务的成本拆分省了不少事；用各家官方后台也能做，就是得开几个账号对着看。

## 六、三个版本各自适合干什么（跑了一年之后的结论）

小版本：分类、打标、简短改写、意图识别。输入短、输出结构固定、要求快。这类任务上它和大版本的差距小到可以忽略，价格却差一个数量级。

中间版本：摘要、多轮改写、带一点推理的判断。这是最"万金油"的一档，我个人用得最多。

大版本：跨多份材料的比对、需要按步骤推理的疑难、写出来要直接给人看的长文。真用它的时候，你会发现它值那个价——但如果你发现自己 30% 的请求都在用大版本，先别调价，先看看是不是任务没分好。

技术选型里最贵的一课，从来不是选错了模型，是根本没分。 一个模型走天下，最后一定是大材小用和小材大用同时发生——这也是我们在选大模型 API 时最该先想清楚的一件事。

Qwen.content:
## 蔡崇信：開源為AI普惠關鍵 阿里千問成全球最大開源模型矩陣

責任編輯：程向明 2026-11-03 10:58:30原創 來源：香港商报网

2026世界互聯網大會烏鎮峰會于今日（3日）舉行，阿里巴巴集團主席蔡崇信發表主題發言，強調開源是AI普及與普惠發展的核心。他指出，業界開源共創模式突破單一主體局限，既能推動智能技術普及，也可保障企業數據部署安全，助力打造可持續普惠智能時代。

千問開源成果亮眼 形成全球最大模型矩陣

蔡崇信介紹，阿里三年前布局AI開源戰略，旗下千問（Qwen）已累計開源超470款模型，全球下載量突破40億、衍生模型超33萬款，為全球規模最大開源模型矩陣，有效降低中小企業AI研發門檻，惠及多個發展中地區。

魔塔社區鏈接全球 開源方案落地海外多地

阿里魔塔社區已匯聚239個國家及地區共3300萬用戶，全球開發者共建共享，落地多個海外場景。烏干達機構依托千問研發適配68種非洲語言的AI模型，印證開源技術的普惠價值。

直面AI治理挑戰 持續推動全球開放共建

蔡崇信表示，AI發展仍需解決紅利分配、倫理治理等議題，阿里將持續堅持開源開放，與全球合作方共建普惠智能生態。（記者 蔡寧 王學東）

Europe's Biggest Tech Startup Cuts AI Coding Costs by 90% Using Chinese Model

# Europe's Biggest Tech Startup Cuts AI Coding Costs by 90% Using Chinese Model

"Self-hosting GLM brings our blended cost of tokens to 30 cents per million. Our invoice is now one-tenth of what we were spending on Anthropic and OpenAI,” said David Abitbol, who leads AI operation

Published Updated

## Key takeaways

- Revolut has reduced AI coding costs to one-tenth of previous expenses by self-hosting the GLM model from Z.ai.
- The deployment of the GLM model improved engineering lead times by 70% and coding time by 60% for 2,000 engineers.
- Revolut's valuation increased significantly, positioning it as Europe's most valuable private technology company.
- The company started self-hosting open-source models in April 2026 to mitigate high commercial AI costs.

5 min

British fintech giant Revolut has reduced its inference costs for AI coding tasks to roughly one-tenth of its previous spending on Anthropic and OpenAI.

The company achieved this by self-hosting the open-weight GLM model from the Chinese AI lab Z.ai on dedicated NVIDIA GPUs.

The European digital bank said the deployment has also improved engineering lead times by 70% and coding time by 60% across a sample of 2,000 engineers.

David Abitbol, who leads AI operations at Revolut, revealed this at a technical session at the AI Engineering conference.

"Self-hosting GLM brings our blended cost of tokens to 30 cents per million. Our invoice is now one-tenth of what we were spending on Anthropic and OpenAI,” he said.

Revolut was valued at $115 billion in a secondary share sale in July, up from $75 billion last November and $45 billion in 2024.

The transaction reinforced its position as Europe's most valuable private technology company.

The company began experimenting with AI tools in January 2025, initially introducing Gemini for internal data access before testing Anthropic's Claude Code.

Concerned about commercial AI costs, with some engineers spending $1,000–$10,000 monthly without clear ROI, Revolut imposed strict usage budgets.

Abitbol said the company then began looking for ways to give engineers unrestricted access to AI coding tools without incurring comparable commercial inference costs.

In April 2026, Revolut began self-hosting open-source models, settling on the GLM family for coding workloads.

Abitbol said Revolut downloads model weights and runs inference on US-based infrastructure rather than sending requests to Chinese-hosted inference endpoints.

Revolut found that removing token constraints also let engineers spend less time on activities such as searching documentation, managing inboxes and coordinating development tasks.

The infrastructure supporting the deployment consists of 56 NVIDIA B200 GPUs serving approximately 2,000 engineers running GLM-5.3.

Revolut targets a time to first token below three seconds, with Abitbol saying latency exceeding five seconds causes engineers to complain.

The company serves interactive workloads at around 200 tokens per second, although engineers can access throughput of up to 800 tokens per second after 5 pm, when GPU demand is lower.

“Open source is now a priority at Revolut. The economics are favourable, the billing is flat, and we don't have any bill shock at the end of the month,” he said.

The company also improved inference performance without adding GPUs.

Between April and August, requests per second increased from approximately three to more than seven, while time to first token fell from over 10 seconds to around 1.6 seconds.

This represented an 88% performance improvement despite a 76% increase in demand.

Abitbol attributed the gains to inference optimisation rather than simply adding computing capacity.

Revolut has not entirely replaced commercial models. It still uses frontier tools such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini for specialised workloads, including image recognition. Its internally hosted GLM models handle most coding tasks.

In October, CEO Nik Storonsky said Revolut was developing proprietary AI models trained on customer transaction data.

He cited the company's 30 million to 40 million daily transactions as a source of training data.

GLM.content:
Run GLM models from Z.ai in Guild agents under policy

Call Z.ai’s GLM models from Guild agents through AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, or Fireworks AI, with model policies on every workspace and agent.

Integrations · Z.ai

Guild agents call Z.ai’s GLM models through task.llm, using a credential for AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, or Fireworks AI. Guild holds the credential server-side, checks your model policies on every call, and attributes spend to the workspace, agent, and user that made it.

GLM models reach Guild only through third-party inference providers. glm-5.3 is on Bedrock in all four supported US regions and on Fireworks AI, which adds glm-5.3-flash and glm-5.2. The default, glm-5, is on Bedrock outside us-west-1. OpenRouter serves its z-ai/ namespace.

Agents never hold the key. Guild stores the credential server-side and shows only a masked value, so you can rotate it without touching agent code or the model policies bound to it. Policies are an allowlist: a workspace, agent, or installed agent can call a GLM model only if a rule allows it. Set a daily token limit to cap spend, and see each call by workspace, agent, and user in Usage.A raw API key in an agent’s environment reaches every model the key can. A policy reaches only the models you name.

Guild prices and recognizes these Z.ai model IDs. A policy or preference can also name any other model your credential can reach. Third-party providers route more models than this list, and their catalogs change; see each provider’s page for what it serves.

Guild has no managed key for Z.ai. To use Z.ai models, add a credential for a provider that serves them. Adding your first credential switches the whole account to bring your own key (BYOK).

1

Open Models & providers

Click Access & setup in the left nav, then Models & providers. In an organization, only admins can open it.

2

Add a credential

Click Add API key and choose an inference provider from the table above.

3

Enter the provider's secret

Give the credential a Name and paste your provider’s API key. AWS Bedrock asks for an IAM role and region instead.

4

Choose Z.ai

Under Models, check Z.ai. Keep glm-5 as its default model or enter another from the list above. Then click Add Key. On Fireworks AI, pick a model from its list, because the pre-filled default isn’t available there.

To control which workspaces and agents can use Z.ai models, add a model policy for the credential. For example, --models "glm-*" limits a policy to matching models:

The first entry asks for glm-4.7-flash. The second falls back to the default model of the matching policy. Preferences are strict: if no credential or policy allows any of them, the call fails rather than using another publisher. See LLM preferences.

The "zai" provider value needs @guildai/agents-sdk 0.7.6 or later.

# Why Chinese AI stars like Z.ai, MiniMax struggle to match Anthropic’s profit margin

The US giant’s massive revenue advantage highlights the struggle Chinese AI developers face despite technical gains

3-MIN READ3-MIN

0

US artificial intelligence giant Anthropic’s initial public offering prospectus has exposed a vast profitability gap between it and rivals Z.ai and MiniMax, highlighting the challenges facing China’s AI model developers in turning technological advances into sustainable businesses.

The Claude developer’s filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) last week revealed a significant financial advantage over its most direct Chinese counterparts, despite the latter’s continued advances in model capabilities, analysts said.

Anthropic reported a gross profit margin of 85.4 per cent in the first half of 2026, compared with 26.4 per cent for Z.ai, also known as Zhipu AI, and 17.9 per cent for MiniMax, according to Anthropic’s S-1 prospectus and the two Hong Kong-listed companies’ latest financial disclosures.

Anthropic generated US$16.3 billion in revenue during the first six months of the year, compared with US$141 million for Z.ai and US$116.6 million for MiniMax.

The gap was also evident in the companies’ ability to monetise computing resources, a major expense for developers training and running advanced AI models, HSBC analysts Ritchie Sun, Charlene Liu and Wang Peishan wrote in a research note published on October 27.

For every US dollar spent on computing resources, Anthropic generated US$2.08 in revenue in the second quarter, compared with 46 US cents for Z.ai.

The HSBC analysts linked Anthropic’s stronger returns on computing investment partly to its progress in recursive self-improvement, in which AI models increasingly help build more powerful versions of themselves, while noting that Z.ai had also begun to see similar gains.

Z.ai’s revenue generated per dollar of compute increased 23-fold from the first half of 2025, compared with a 4.2-fold increase for Anthropic over the same period.

“Z.ai also mentioned that GLM started to support inference engine optimisation and training of [the] next generation of GLM,” the analysts wrote, rating its stock a “Hold” with a target price of HK$1,375.

Z.ai and MiniMax have seen their Hong Kong shares slide around 13 per cent and 2 per cent, respectively, since Anthropic’s prospectus filing.

Poe Zhao, a Beijing-based tech analyst and founder of Hello China Tech, said the financial disparity between Anthropic and the two Chinese AI model companies reflected differences in pricing and scale.

“The simplest test is whether gross profit can pay for research,” said Zhao. “In the first half of 2026, Anthropic’s gross profit covered its R&D spending about 1.4 times. Zhipu’s covered about one-eighth, and MiniMax’s about one-fourteenth.”

Zhao said gross margins were largely determined by pricing, while the ability to cover research and development costs depended more heavily on scale.

“All three companies must pay to stay near the frontier, and only Anthropic has the revenue to spread that cost,” he said.

Chinese AI developers have increasingly competed on price to attract users, but Zhao questioned whether that strategy could sustain the enormous investment required to develop frontier models.

“Low prices can win usage, but at today’s margins they cannot fund research,” he said. “For now, the capital market pays for the gap.”

He added that technological improvements for Chinese AI companies did not necessarily translate into greater pricing power, given fierce competition both at home and abroad.

“The test is whether a Chinese lab can launch its next top model at a higher price, and whether customers pay it,” he said.

Unlike Anthropic, which committed to computing capacity 12 to 18 months in advance, the Chinese developers relied more heavily on purchasing computing resources as a service, leaving them with less profit to reinvest, he added.

While Anthropic also pays external providers for computing power, its longer-term commitments help keep costs predictable, and its much larger revenue allows it to absorb those expenses more easily. Meanwhile, Chinese AI developers such as Z.ai and MiniMax face tighter profit margins as they pay cloud providers to run their models.

Nevertheless, Anthropic also faces significant financial pressures despite its greater scale and pricing power, based on its performance in the latest quarter.

In an amended IPO filing submitted to the SEC on Monday, the Claude developer reported about US$17 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 47 per cent from the previous three months.

However, it recorded an operating loss of US$567 million, reversing a US$974 million operating profit in the preceding quarter, as rising computing expenses and slowing revenue growth weighed on its bottom line.

Preparing for what could be the largest IPO in history, the company faces mounting scrutiny over its balance sheet and heavy spending, with investors questioning whether rapid AI growth could justify its staggering capital demands.

Institutional investors were urging Anthropic to target an IPO valuation of US$1.5 trillion to US$1.6 trillion, down from the US$2 trillion the start-up had previously reportedly sought, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

Previously, he was an AI reporter for Business Insider's Singapore bureau, and began his journalism career at CNA Digital in Singapore. He is a fellow at the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism.

# Financial technology unicorn Revolut turns to Zhipu GLM, programming bills reduced to about one-tenth

2026-11-03 18:39:01

The European highest-valued fintech unicorn Revolut has set the GLM of the AI company Zhipu as the default AI programming model for approximately 2,000 engineers, with tools like Claude Code and Codex relegated to alternatives, mainly reserved for complex tasks. David Abitbol, the head of AI operations at Revolut, revealed that the company previously set a limit of $300 per person per month for Claude Code, but it provided limited help to overall efficiency.

In April this year, the company began to deploy GLM independently and opened unlimited Tokens to engineers. Currently, Revolut uses about 56 NVIDIA B200s to run GLM 5.3, with a comprehensive cost of approximately $0.30 per million Tokens, and the related bill is only one-tenth of what was previously spent on Anthropic and OpenAI.

According to internal company statistics, the coding time metrics for engineers improved by about 60%, and the cycle metrics from task handover to delivery improved by about 70%. In the past, with limited Tokens, engineers tended to reserve their quotas for complex tasks; now that there are no usage restrictions, they have begun to extensively use AI to search internal documents, handle Jira tickets, and find requirement specifications in Slack.

# Revolut Cuts A.I. Coding Costs 90% With a Chinese Open-Weight Model

Unlimited tokens instead of spending caps, at a tenth of the price: The neobank Revolut has moved its roughly 2,000 software engineers from Claude Code and Codex to a self-hosted open-weight model from China. Instead of the coding agents from Anthropic and OpenAI, Revolut’s default is now GLM, a model from the Chinese A.I. lab Z.ai. According to Revolut, its bill is now about a tenth of what the fintech used to pay Anthropic and OpenAI.

David Abitbol, who oversees A.I. operations and infrastructure at Revolut, shared the details in his talk “Shipping like a startup, regulated like a bank” at the AI Engineer conference in New York. With more than 80 million customers in 45 markets and a recent valuation of about $115 billion (about €103 billion), Revolut is one of Europe’s most valuable start-ups. For its eventual I.P.O., the company is aiming for as much as $200 billion (about €180 billion).

## From Gemini to Claude Code to GLM

Revolut got there step by step. It first rolled out Google’s Gemini across the company, which cut coding time by 20 percent and lead time, from picking up a task to merging it, by 10 percent, according to Mr. Abitbol. Claude Code came next, but with strict per-engineer budget limits. The benefit was small at first, he said, while the costs were high.

Since the spring, GLM has been running on Revolut’s own infrastructure, and the numbers look very different. In a sample of about 2,000 engineers, coding time fell 60 percent and lead time 70 percent. For Mr. Abitbol, the fact that lead time dropped more than coding time is telling: “The bottleneck for engineering is not necessarily coding,” he said. Engineers spend a lot of time searching inboxes, Jira and Confluence.

The biggest change for engineers is that token limits are gone. They no longer have to ration usage, for example near the end of a quarter or on particularly demanding tasks.

## 56 GPUs for 2,000 Engineers

The technical setup is surprisingly modest. Revolut runs GLM, a model with about 800 billion parameters, on roughly 56 Nvidia B200 chips. The cost comes to about 30 cents per million tokens, Mr. Abitbol said, and a flat bill has replaced unpredictable month-end invoices.

- Tuning: Out of the box, inference was “terrible,” Mr. Abitbol said. After optimization, time to first token fell from more than 10 seconds to 1.6 seconds, even as demand rose 76 percent. Above five seconds, he said, “my Slack inbox starts to blow up.”
- Context: The context window is capped at 256,000 tokens. “Long context is a scam,” Mr. Abitbol said.
- Images: GLM handles only text. A router sends image tasks to Gemini.
- Exceptions: Claude Code and Codex remain available. The latest models from Anthropic and OpenAI are excellent, he said, but are now used sparingly as the exception.

## Chinese Weights, Western Servers

For a regulated bank, the model’s origin is sensitive. “There’s been a lot of stigma in using Chinese open source model,” Mr. Abitbol acknowledged. Revolut therefore uses only the openly available model weights and runs them on infrastructure in the United States, rather than through the developer’s inference endpoint in China. Data is meant to be processed only in jurisdictions with equivalent data protection, such as the United States, the European Union, Britain and Israel, and providers must have zero data retention by default.

Revolut also tells regulators that its coding agents do not act autonomously. They run in a sandbox with approval rules that determine which commands are allowed. “They’re always with a human in the loop,” Mr. Abitbol said.

Revolut is not alone. Open models from China such as GLM, DeepSeek and Kimi have been catching up in benchmarks, and European developers like Mistral are also betting on open weights with Mistral Large 4.

## What the Bill Leaves Out

Whether the approach carries over to other companies is an open question. According to an analysis by StartupHub.ai, the 90 percent savings exclude the costs of cloud, staff and monitoring. The results also depend on 56 B200 chips, ongoing tuning and Revolut’s ability to shape the load through sandbox rules and working hours. Smaller teams could face high bills or slow response times.

Then there is the hardware. Mr. Abitbol did not say whether Revolut bought its 56 B200 chips or rents them. Buying them would mean an investment in the millions: When Nvidia introduced the B200, Jensen Huang, its chief executive, put the price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip, which would add up to about $1.7 million to $2.2 million (about €1.5 million to €2 million) for 56 chips. Complete servers with eight B200s each cost about $450,000 to $500,000, according to industry estimates. Seven such systems would come to $3.2 million to $3.5 million (about €2.9 million to €3.1 million), not counting power and data center costs.

And the chips have an expiration date. Nvidia now releases a new chip generation every year, and Rubin, the successor to Blackwell, is already on its way. Data center operators such as Nscale depreciate their GPUs over five to six years, but they acknowledge that this useful life could prove too long if technology changes quickly. Critics such as the investor Michael Burry consider two to three years more realistic.

Kimi.description: Moonshot (Kimi) Moonshot AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API for its Kimi models — the Kimi K3 and K2 thinking models and the Moonshot v1 generation models. ... - Kimi K3 — flagship thinking model, 1M context ... - Kimi K2 — thinking models, 256k context...
Kimi.content:
# Moonshot (Kimi)

Moonshot AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API for its Kimi models — the Kimi K3 and K2 thinking models and the Moonshot v1 generation models. The Moonshot provider extends the OpenAI provider, so all of its options are supported.

## Setup

- Get an API key from the Kimi (Moonshot) platform.
- Set theMOONSHOT_API_KEY environment variable or specify apiKey in your config.

Kimi K3 requires a successful account top-up of at least $1; see the access requirements.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3

Bothmoonshot:<model> and moonshot:chat:<model> resolve to the chat completions endpoint. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to kimi-k3.

## Available Models

Moonshot's lineup rotates over time — call the list models API (GET https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/models) for the live set. As of writing:

- Kimi K3 — flagship thinking model, 1M context:kimi-k3 (released July 2026). Always-on reasoning, native image and video understanding, and a top-level reasoning_effort control (see below).
- Kimi K2 — thinking models, 256k context:kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed. These reason before answering and emit a separate reasoning stream (see below).
- Moonshot v1 — legacy generation models:moonshot-v1-8k, moonshot-v1-32k, moonshot-v1-128k (context-length variants) and the vision variants moonshot-v1-8k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-32k-vision-preview / moonshot-v1-128k-vision-preview; existing accounts may also see the auto-router moonshot-v1-auto in the list-models API. The moonshot-v1 series and kimi-k2.5 are closed to newly registered users and sunset platform-wide on August 31, 2026.

The olderkimi-k2-0711-preview, kimi-k2-0905-preview, kimi-k2-turbo-preview, kimi-k2-thinking, kimi-k2-thinking-turbo, and kimi-latest ids were discontinued in 2026 — Moonshot recommends migrating to kimi-k3.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3 # flagship thinking model — leave sampling params unset
  - id: moonshot:moonshot-v1-8k # legacy generation model — accepts arbitrary sampling
    config:
      temperature: 0.2
      max_tokens: 1024

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts every option the OpenAI provider supports. Commonly used:

- temperature, max_tokens, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty
- stream
- response_format (JSON mode), tools / tool_choice (function calling)
- showThinking — set to false to drop a thinking model's reasoning from the graded output (default true)
- cost, inputCost, outputCost, cacheReadCost — Moonshot ships no built-in price table, so set these to track cost. Every override is in USD per token. Moonshot's official pricing page publishes rates in USD per 1 million tokens, so divide each published rate by 1,000,000 before configuring it. inputCost/outputCost take precedence over the flat cost; cacheReadCost prices cached prompt tokens.

For example, these illustrative per-million rates convert to per-token overrides. Check the official pricing page for the current rates for your model before using them.
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      inputCost: 0.000003 # $3.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.0000003 # $0.30 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000015 # $15.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      inputCost: 0.00000095 # $0.95 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      cacheReadCost: 0.00000016 # $0.16 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000
      outputCost: 0.000004 # $4.00 per 1M tokens divided by 1,000,000

Any other parameter supported by the OpenAI provider is forwarded as-is.

## Kimi thinking models

Thekimi-k3 and kimi-k2.x models are reasoning models and behave differently from the moonshot-v1 family:

- Fixed sampling parameters. Kimi pinstemperature (1.0 with thinking on), top_p, n, and the penalties to fixed values and returns a 400 ("invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model") for any other value. The provider therefore does not send promptfoo's default temperature/max_tokens for kimi-* models — leave them unset (recommended) or set temperature: 1. The moonshot-v1 models accept arbitrary sampling values.
- Reasoning output. Kimi returns a separatereasoning_content stream that promptfoo surfaces with a Thinking: … prefix. Set showThinking: false when you assert on structured output (for example is-json) so the reasoning doesn't contaminate the parsed result.
- Token budget. Reasoning tokens count against the output budget. When you leave the token limit unset the provider lets Moonshot apply its server default (32k for K2.x, 131k for K3); if you set one, leave generous headroom for the answer. Moonshot's canonical field ismax_completion_tokens (max_tokens is a deprecated alias) — the provider sends max_completion_tokens for kimi-* models whichever of the two you configure.
- Controlling thinking. The two generations use different, mutually exclusive controls:
- kimi-k3 is always thinking and accepts a top-level reasoning_effort field, which the provider forwards from config.reasoning_effort. Supported values are low, high, and max (the default). Do not send the K2.x thinking parameter to K3 — the API rejects it.
- kimi-k2.6 and kimi-k2.5 support thinking: { type: disabled } (pass it via config.passthrough); kimi-k2.7-code is always thinking. The thinking parameter is K2.x-only.
- Settingconfig.reasoning_effort on a non-K3 model is a configuration error and the provider fails fast with a clear message instead of sending it.

providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
    config:
      showThinking: false
      reasoning_effort: max # optional: low, high, or max (default)
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k2.6
    config:
      passthrough:
        thinking: { type: disabled } # K2.x only: turn reasoning off

See the Kimi K3 quickstart and Using Thinking Models for the full behavior matrix.

## Vision

The vision models (moonshot-v1-*-vision-preview) and the multimodal Kimi models (kimi-k3, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed) accept base64-encoded image input using the standard OpenAI image_url content format. Moonshot does not accept remote image URLs — embed images as data: URIs or reference files uploaded to the Kimi platform as ms://<file-id>. Video input is supported by kimi-k3, kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, and kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed, referenced the same way after uploading via the files API. See Use the Kimi Vision Model.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: moonshot:kimi-k3
  - id: openai:gpt-4o-mini

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

A runnable comparison lives in examples/provider-moonshot.

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 (global). China-mainland keys use https://api.moonshot.cn/v1 — point at it with apiBaseUrl, since the global and China platforms issue region-locked keys.
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions API.
- Full API documentation.

## See Also

- OpenAI Provider — compatible configuration options
- Kimi model list and pricing

Kimi.title: AI Subscriptions Hit a Wall as Smarter Models Burn Quotas Faster
Kimi.description: Moonshot’s Kimi is the clearest recent example: a stronger release ... Moonshot AI’s Kimi product has issued three formal apologies in about six months—the latest after Kimi K3.1 Pro burned through allowances within hours of launch and forced a company-wide 25% quota restoration.
Kimi.content:
## AI Subscriptions Hit a Wall as Smarter Models Burn Quotas Faster

2026.11.03 10:03

· 来自海外

· 1446阅读

全文4802字

Across the industry, frontier models are improving while fixed monthly plans feel smaller. Moonshot’s Kimi is the clearest recent example: a stronger release, angry subscribers, and another public apology. The tension is structural—capability is outrunning the economics of flat-fee access.

NextFin News — Consumer AI is caught between two clocks. On one clock, models keep posting better scores on code, long documents, and multi-step jobs. On the other, paying users hit rate limits sooner, meet peak-hour wait screens, and compare notes on which brand still “lasts a month.” Vendors answer with quota top-ups, limit resets, and apology posts. OpenAI has doubled some Pro and business caps after complaints.

In China, Moonshot AI’s Kimi product has issued three formal apologies in about six months—the latest after Kimi K3.1 Pro burned through allowances within hours of launch and forced a company-wide 25% quota restoration.

Kimi is not an outlier so much as a loud instance of a pattern. Anyone selling near-frontier intelligence for a fixed monthly price is discovering that “smarter” often means more tokens per finished task. Unit prices can fall while the cost of a real workflow rises.

Heavy users no longer treat chatbots as occasional toys. They wire them into review, drafting, and agent-style loops and notice burn rate the way they once noticed mobile data. Community comparisons are blunt: the same cash that stretches a month on one API or subscription may last a day on another. K3.1 Pro illustrated why. Independent evaluations placed it among the stronger global models, including as a leading open-weight entry, and Moonshot cut list API prices by roughly a third. Benchmarks also showed it emitting far more tokens than median peers to complete the same intelligence suite. Default “thinking” traces, long context, and sub-agent swarms turn a single prompt into many billed or capped steps. A subscriber who asks for an architecture review and watches five agents empty a multi-hour window is not misreading the marketing. They are meeting the true shape of modern inference.

Capacity compounds the insult. Restored quota means little when the service asks paid users to try again later or climb to a higher tier for speed. Labs that depend on rented or partner GPU pools—Moonshot has been linked in reporting to large external Nvidia-class clusters—face a hard allocation choice among training, API customers, and consumer generosity. After prior launches, new Kimi subscriptions were paused when silicon ran short. That is rationing, not a temporary bug.

The industry’s early consumer pitch was simple: pay once a month, use freely enough that the meter stays invisible. Frontier systems broke that fiction. Longer reasoning chains and tool-using agents raise quality and multiply runtime. Some teams now treat token efficiency as part of competitiveness, not only raw leaderboard rank. Others still ship capability first and repair trust with partial refunds of allowance. Memory and personalization features are being redesigned in the same light—coarser summaries instead of exhaustive stored instructions—because every retained detail can become another chargeable read.

None of this is unique to one Chinese lab. It is the subscription version of a problem cloud customers already know: the bill follows tokens, and better models can be greedier models unless engineering intervenes.

Under GPU constraint, companies reveal their real customer. DeepSeek has been described as earning almost entirely from API usage while leaving the consumer app free, with a reported annualized revenue run-rate above $1 billion and price increases that management said did not drive users away. Zhipu’s revenue mix has swung toward API and away from one-off local deployments as coding demand surged. MiniMax is spreading across API, consumer products, and enterprise media and agents. Moonshot, alongside consumer Kimi, has been reported in talks to distribute models through global clouds for a revenue share, and to use license terms that pull large hosting firms into paid deals. Wholesaling intelligence to platforms that already own chips and sales teams is a different business from promising unlimited-feeling chat to individuals.

Internet groups have a further option: fold models into office suites, messaging, and commerce they already monetize, so the model is a feature cost rather than the sole product. Pure-play labs without those surfaces must choose whether the paid consumer app is a profit center, a showcase, or a feedback instrument. Quota crises are what it looks like when the marketing still says “plan” and the P&L says “scarce resource.”

Leaderboards will keep moving. The quieter contest is who can deliver a finished task with fewer tokens, clearer limits, and infrastructure that does not punish the people who pay. Until that catches up, every jump in model strength risks another round of full meters and familiar apologies.

# Introducing India-based inference for Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock

Kimi K3 is a multi-modal, open-weight foundation model (FM) that provider Moonshot AI reported achieved frontier-level coding and general agentic intelligence at release.

In addition to global and US-based inference, Amazon Bedrock now supports in-country inference in India for Kimi K3: unblocking local workloads with strict data residency requirements. Customers like Ultrahuman are already seeing the benefits in production:

“Jade, an AI Health and Wellness assistant in the Ultrahuman app, answers questions in plain language using each person’s own Ring and glucose data, across more than 14,000 conversations a day. Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock let us add a leading open-weight model through the API we already use, with health data staying inside AWS and Mumbai as a fallback Region. With prompt caching, we’ve cut LLM costs by 80 percent and made multi-turn chats 85 percent faster.”

— Aditya Patawari, VP Engineering, Ultrahuman

In this post, we explain the different global and geographic inference options available, and share code for an example use case: optical character recognition (OCR) and understanding of Indic-language documents, with follow-up question answering in code-mixed Hinglish.

## Choose where inference can run

Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock is offered through cross-Region inference profiles. You can invoke the model from any of a wide range of AWS Regions (the “source”). Amazon Bedrock then securely processes your request in one of multiple possible “destination” Regions.

Cross-Region inference is fully managed by AWS: Data is encrypted in transit between Regions and remains on the AWS network, never traversing the public internet or requiring you to set up any multi-Region virtual private cloud (VPC) infrastructure.

The inference profile ID you invoke controls which destination Regions are eligible:

Profile | Model ID | When to choose it 
---|---|---
Global | global.moonshotai.kimi-k3 | Recommended for most use cases: lowest cost and most broadly available 
India geographic | in.moonshotai.kimi-k3 | Inference processing must stay within Mumbai and Hyderabad Regions 

See the Amazon Bedrock Kimi K3 model card for up-to-date information on available inference profiles, which AWS Regions they can be called from, and what destination Regions they can use for inference.

## Example walkthrough: Indic-language document understanding

Let’s consider an example use case: reading a scanned Hindi document, extracting structured data, and answering follow-up questions in mixed Hindi and English (Hinglish).

This need is common in Indian financial services and public sector workflows where know your customer (KYC) forms, utility bills, and similar documents must often be digitized. Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock can directly read and reason about images, including those containing multilingual text. It offers a potential solution with no separate OCR or translation service required.

### Prerequisites

The full source code for this example is available on GitHub.

To follow along, you need:

- An AWS account.
- Python 3.11 or later installed, with internet access to install the required PyPI packages.
- The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) installed, with credentials configured with sufficient AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to invoke the Kimi K3 model through the India inference profile.

For example, to use Kimi K3 through theap-south-1 Mumbai Region with India geographic inference, the following IAM policy grants sufficient access. Replace the {ACCOUNT_ID} placeholders with your AWS account ID:

For more information about permissions, see Prerequisites for running model inference in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. If your organization restricts AWS Regions, ask your administrator to review the geographic cross-Region inference IAM and SCP guidance. Keep the source Region permitted and allow routing to both India destinations, using a profile-scoped exception where appropriate. The Responses API guide also describes required default-project access.

### Get started with the inference APIs

As detailed on the model card, Amazon Bedrock supports multiple APIs for invoking Kimi K3, all under the Bedrock Runtime endpoint:

API | Request and response format 
---|---
Chat Completions | OpenAI-compatible messages input and assistant-message output. 
Responses | OpenAI-compatible input and structured output items. 
Converse | Standardized messages, content blocks, and inference parameters across supported models. 
InvokeModel | Model-specific JSON request and response bodies. 

Because the OpenAI-compatible APIs are recommended for this model, we use those in this example and connect through the openai Python Library.

Amazon Bedrock supports generating API keys for integrations that require them. However, AWS recommends using short-lived credentials instead where possible. The AWS token generator Python library derives a short-term API key-like token from the standard AWS CLI credential chain.

If you use a named profile for your AWS CLI, you might need to set theAWS_PROFILE environment variable first. After CLI credentials are set up, you can invoke the model with the following code:

Here,region (ap-south-1 Mumbai) specifies the source Region to which the request is made. The inference profile in.moonshotai.kimi-k3 ensures that inference is processed in Indian Regions only.

A broad range of features like streaming, tool calling, and structured outputs are supported across both the Chat Completions and Responses APIs. See the OpenAI Python API Reference for more examples.

### Analyze images

Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock supports images as well as PDFs and a range of other file types. You can send input files to the model directly by base64-encoding. For OCR or other use cases where small details are important, consider setting the imagedetail parameter to high. This improves accuracy, at the cost of more input tokens consumed per image.

In some cases, we’ve seen higher output quality for Kimi K3 when images are provided before text inputs. We suggest experimenting with request ordering. Consider the following example code:

To demonstrate, we generated an image of a synthetic electricity bill in Hindi.

Given this image input, the model can answer questions by pulling data directly from the document with no separate digitization step required. For example:

Q: Bill kitne ka hai aur last date kab hai? Late hua toh kitna dena padega?

A: Bill ka total ₹2,217.20 hai, aur last date 20/10/2026 hai. Late hua toh ₹2,261.54 dena padega.

### Build a structured extraction pipeline

Beyond general question-answering, you can create structured document processing workflows by using static prompts to extract a consistent set of expected fields across many documents.

To apply firm constraints on output structure (rather than best-effort prompt-guided generation), Kimi K3 supports structured output on Amazon Bedrock either through function calling or by providing a JSON Schema output format. These options are described in more detail in the OpenAI documentation (for OpenAI-compatible APIs) and the Amazon Bedrock User Guide (for native Converse/InvokeModel APIs).

In the full sample code repository, we’ve provided an end-to-end pipeline that:

- Transcribes the document in its original script (OCR).
- Extracts key fields as JSON using a configurable schema, with dates normalized to ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), Devanagari digits (for example २८८) converted to Western digits (288), and names transliterated into English.
- Writes a short English summary.
- Answers multi-turn follow-up questions in Hinglish (Hindi written in Latin script, mixed with English) about the same document.

Download the sample code from GitHub to explore further and try it out on your own images.

As with any automated extraction, you should verify the outputs are reliable for your specific use case before relying on them for important decisions. Consider adding post-validation logic or a human review step for critical workflows.

## Optimize price-performance, service tiers and caching

Tune your system prompts and schemas against example documents for reliable extractions. Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization (AdvPO) provides a fully managed option to optimize prompt templates based on reference examples.

Amazon Bedrock service tiers give you control over price-performance on a per-request basis. Kimi.content:
Call Moonshot AI’s Kimi models from Guild agents through AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, or Fireworks AI, with model policies on every workspace and agent.

Integrations · Moonshot AI

Guild agents call Moonshot AI’s Kimi models through task.llm, using a credential for AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter, or Fireworks AI. Guild holds the credential server-side, checks your model policies on every call, and attributes spend to the workspace, agent, and user that made it.

Kimi models reach Guild only through third-party inference providers. kimi-k3 is on Bedrock in all four supported US regions and on Fireworks AI. The default, kimi-k2.5, and the reasoning model kimi-k2-thinking are on Bedrock outside us-west-1. OpenRouter serves its moonshotai/ namespace.

Agents never hold the key. Guild stores the credential server-side and shows only a masked value, so you can rotate it without touching agent code or the model policies bound to it. Policies are an allowlist: a workspace, agent, or installed agent can call a Kimi model only if a rule allows it. Set a daily token limit to cap spend, and see each call by workspace, agent, and user in Usage.A raw API key in an agent’s environment reaches every model the key can. A policy reaches only the models you name.

Guild prices and recognizes these Moonshot AI model IDs. A policy or preference can also name any other model your credential can reach. Third-party providers route more models than this list, and their catalogs change; see each provider’s page for what it serves.

Guild has no managed key for Moonshot AI. To use Moonshot AI models, add a credential for a provider that serves them. Adding your first credential switches the whole account to bring your own key (BYOK).

1

Open Models & providers

Click Access & setup in the left nav, then Models & providers. In an organization, only admins can open it.

2

Add a credential

Click Add API key and choose an inference provider from the table above.

3

Enter the provider's secret

Give the credential a Name and paste your provider’s API key. AWS Bedrock asks for an IAM role and region instead.

4

Choose Moonshot AI

Under Models, check Moonshot AI. Keep kimi-k2.5 as its default model or enter another from the list above. Then click Add Key. On Fireworks AI, pick a model from its list, because the pre-filled default isn’t available there.

To control which workspaces and agents can use Moonshot AI models, add a model policy for the credential. For example, --models "kimi-*" limits a policy to matching models:

The first entry asks for kimi-k2-thinking. The second falls back to the default model of the matching policy. Preferences are strict: if no credential or policy allows any of them, the call fails rather than using another publisher. See LLM preferences.

The "moonshot" provider value needs @guildai/agents-sdk 0.7.6 or later.

xAI.content:
# xAI (Grok)

Thexai provider supports xAI's Grok models through an API interface compatible with OpenAI's format, including text, vision, image generation, video generation, and voice workflows.

## Setup

To use xAI's API, set theXAI_API_KEY environment variable or specify via apiKey in the configuration file.
export XAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here

When xAI is the selected fallback provider family, Promptfoo can use xAI defaults for grading, suggestions, synthesis, and web search. These automatic defaults currently usegrok-4.3 on the global endpoint; select grok-4.7, grok-4.6, or grok-4.5 explicitly where they are available. xAI does not currently expose a public embeddings or moderation API, so those defaults fall back to OpenAI when xAI is selected. Explicit provider IDs in your config still take precedence.

## Supported Models

The xAI provider includes support for the following model formats. xAI recommendsgrok-4.7 for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work; consult the public model catalog for current availability.

Legacy xAI model aliases

xAI periodically retires older model slugs and keeps them working through redirects. As of the May 15, 2026 (12:00 PM PT) retirement, requests to thegrok-4-1-fast, grok-4-fast, grok-4-0709, and grok-3 families redirect to grok-4.3 and use Grok 4.3 pricing. Requests to grok-code-fast-1 route to grok-build-0.1, while grok-imagine-image-pro routes to grok-imagine-image-quality. For new configs, use a current canonical model ID directly.

Regional model availability

xAI documents Grok 4.7 on its global and US regional endpoints, and announced Grok 4.5 availability in the EU API Console. Check your account before depending on Grok 4.7 in another region;grok-4.3 remains Promptfoo's automatic fallback.

### Grok 4.7 Models

- xai:grok-4.7 - Chat Completions; 500K context, text and image input, text output
- xai:responses:grok-4.7 - Responses API, including server-side tools and encrypted reasoning

Use the exactgrok-4.7 model ID. Grok 4.7 Fast is available in Cursor and Grok Build, but not on the public xAI API.

### Grok 4.6 Models

- xai:grok-4.6 - Previous flagship reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work (500K context, text and image input)

xAI does not publish any aliases for this model, so target the exactgrok-4.6 id. There is no grok-4.6-latest.

### Grok 4.5 Models

xAI.content:
# Grok Bot halves subscribers' quotas without warning

Over Halloween weekend, Grok Bot's weekly usage counter jumped on its own from 50 to 100% for some subscribers, without a single request being sent. For context, this in-house AI bot from Elon Musk comes with X's paid subscriptions, and the more expensive the plan, the bigger the quota.

One subscriber watched his counter shoot from 56 to 100% in an hour, even though he still had several days left before his cycle reset.

No announcement from xAI, not a single message, nothing. The quotas melted away while everyone was asleep. For some users, the limit was reportedly cut in half outright.

It took until November 1st and a big wave of angry messages for Elon Musk to confirm that the throttling was intentional, because according to him, running Grok Bot costs far too much compared to what it brings in.

Two weeks earlier, though, the very same Musk was telling everyone that Grok Bot was the fastest-growing product he'd ever seen in his entire life. The service reportedly passed 800,000 users, with plans billed up to $200 a month. Apparently, even at that price, every request is run at a loss.

So subscribers dug up a term borrowed from crypto: the rug pull, where the rug gets yanked out from under you once your money has been cashed in. Nobody ran off with the cash here, they're talking more about an indirect rug pull, a prepaid service that loses half its value overnight.

Musk gave no figures, neither on what Grok Bot actually costs, nor on the limits that will apply over the coming weeks. So subscribers are paying full price without knowing what they're buying anymore, which is pretty annoying for a service sold as premium.

But hey, Musk isn't the only one rationing. OpenAI tightened ChatGPT's limits at the same time, to the point that its users are talking about the end of an era, and the English-language press now describes a general rationing of AI as losses pile up. The whole industry sold near-unlimited AI below its real cost to attract people, and the bill is starting to arrive.

Personally, at that price, I'd at least expect an email before someone cuts off my supply in the middle of the night.

Source: TechCrunch

# Elon Musk: Grok Bot Costs Are ‘Unsustainable’ as Usage Limits Tighten

SpaceX is tightening Grok Bot usage limits as Elon Musk warns of unsustainable AI costs. Here’s what the changes mean for paying users and businesses.

Written By

Nov 3, 2026

Elon Musk's Grok Bot faces tighter usage limits as AI costs climb. Image: The White House.

We may earn from vendors via affiliate links or sponsorships. This might affect product placement on our site, but not the content of our reviews. See our Terms of Use for details.

Grok Bot users are running out of usage credits faster than expected, and Elon Musk says the rising cost of running AI agents is to blame.

SpaceX is tightening Grok Bot usage limits after Musk acknowledged that operating costs were “unsustainably high relative to revenue.” The move follows complaints from users on X who say they’re exhausting their allowances much faster than before, with some reporting that they reached their limits in a single night.

Grok Bot is one of many AI agents launched over the past few months that can be assigned long-running, repeatable tasks. What sets it apart from other bots is its integration with X, allowing it to search posts, timelines, mentions, and other information.

It is part of a push by SpaceX to compete more heavily in the enterprise AI market, where rivals Anthropic and OpenAI currently lead. Grok Bot has seen some early success, with SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell confirming 800,000 weekly paid users in October, although the throttling may see that usage drop. Grok Bot can also be used by individuals for consumer-related tasks, similar to Meta Muse, but it has not seen comparable success due to its lack of a free tier.

## SpaceX trying to keep out of the red

While private AI labs OpenAI and Anthropic have been more laissez-faire with spending, SpaceX has made greater efforts to reduce costs and increase revenue. It has rented out a significant portion of its data center capacity to rivals Anthropic, Google, and Reflection AI, reportedly generating over $2 billion in monthly revenue.

It has also explored potentially turning Grok Bot into a routing tool for AI models, similar to OpenRouter, which would reduce output costs. Its latest model launch, Grok 4.7, also introduced higher charges for heavy token usage to prevent power users from hurting its profitability.

## AI agents under more scrutiny

AI agents are currently under considerable scrutiny following several major security incidents involving rogue AI. OpenAI disclosed several incidents in which its AI escaped confinement and hacked into websites and applications, including Hugging Face, the Australian health system, and the US Education Department. Some of these disclosures came months after the incidents occurred.

The Federal Trade Commission has opened a probe into AI agents operated by Anthropic, OpenAI, and other firms, which appears to have been prepared before the Hugging Face disclosure. A European Commission office has also requested information on the security incidents, with an investigation by the bloc expected in the near future.

Advertisement

Given the level of autonomy these agents can have when granted permission, world leaders are scrambling to ensure that consumers and businesses are protected. At the same time, government online services have repeatedly been targeted, raising concerns that successful attacks could disrupt access to public sector resources for millions of people.

### More must-read AI coverage

## What Grok Bot’s restrictions mean for AI users

For businesses and individuals relying on AI agents, Grok Bot’s reported usage restrictions highlight an important concern: Paying for an AI subscription doesn’t necessarily guarantee consistent access to its capabilities.

Users who depend on agents for research, monitoring, or other recurring tasks could find their workflows interrupted if they unexpectedly exhaust their usage allowances. Businesses may face additional challenges when budgeting for AI tools, particularly if providers adjust their limits or pricing as operating costs rise.

Before committing to an AI agent, users should understand how usage is calculated, what happens when limits are reached, and whether additional credits are available.

As AI agents become more integrated into everyday work, reliability and predictable pricing could prove just as important as the capabilities themselves. For customers, the question is increasingly whether these tools can deliver enough consistent value to justify their cost.

For more on why autonomous AI workloads are becoming increasingly expensive, read TechRepublic’s AI Agent Cloud Costs Are Making Enterprise Budgets Harder to Predict, which explores the challenges businesses face in controlling AI spending.
