xAI.title: Elon Musk admits Grok Bot is too costly as users hit caps
xAI.description: The NAACP sued xAI, SpaceX’s AI unit, on April 14, 2026. The suit alleges xAI ran 27 gas turbines without an air permit in Southaven, Mississippi, to power Colossus 2.
xAI.content:
# Elon Musk admits Grok Bot is too costly as users hit caps

If you pay for an AI assistant, the usage meter is the number you learn to watch. This past week, many paying users of Grok Bot, the AI agent from Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX), ran out days early.

When one subscriber asked Elon Musk on Nov. 1 for a reset, he didn’t promise one. “The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue,” Musk wrote on X. He offered no figures and no timeline.

Two days earlier, Musk had posted that “terrestrial compute will be peanuts compared to orbital compute.” His company also runs the largest AI data center by computing power, according to Epoch AI.

To me, that clash marks the moment Musk’s favorite growth story became a cost problem.

## Grok Bot works like an employee, not a chatbot

Grok Bot doesn’t answer one question and go quiet.

Bloomberg described it as built to work like an always-on employee. A chat reply uses a short burst of computing, while an agent keeps drawing on chips until the job is done.

Musk cheered that pattern on SpaceX’s earnings call on Oct. 20. “The usage of Grok bot grows over time per user; it does not decline.”

Paid weekly users reached 800,000 in early October, more than double the prior month, President Gwynne Shotwell said. For a plan that bundles usage into a monthly price, every heavy user increases costs.

## Every Grok Bot hour is an hour SpaceX could rent out

The cost Musk described goes beyond electricity. SpaceX’s AI business, renamed Super Intelligence, brought in $7.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, according to its earnings release.

Fortune reported that the total includes computing capacity leased to outside customers.

CFO Bret Johnsen credited those cloud service deals for most of the segment’s growth. SpaceX, he added, will keep weighing which use pays best: renting chips out or serving its own products.

Answering Goldman Sachs Group analyst Eric Sheridan, Musk said SpaceX aims to split computing roughly evenly between itself and renters. Demand is strong enough, he said, that SpaceX could rent its capacity several times over.

Every hour a subscriber’s agent occupies a SpaceX chip, that chip isn’t earning market rent. I see “unsustainable” as a comparison with that rent, not just a gripe about power bills.

## Earth’s data centers carry costs orbit would avoid

Colossus 2 in Memphis holds roughly 1.1 million H100 equivalents, Epoch estimates. The unit restates mixed hardware as H100s, a common AI chip, so sites can be compared. Epoch expects the site to reach about 1.8 million by early 2027, Seeking Alpha reported.

Powering it is the hard part. The NAACP sued xAI, SpaceX’s AI unit, on April 14, 2026. The suit alleges xAI ran 27 gas turbines without an air permit in Southaven, Mississippi, to power Colossus 2.

On Oct. 30, the day of Musk’s “peanuts” post, a federal judge refused to dismiss the case, DeSoto County News reported. The court rejected xAI’s argument that the turbines were exempt mobile sources. Mississippi permitted permanent turbines there in March, and xAI has said it plans to phase out the temporary ones.

Musk told analysts that suppliers say turbine blades and vanes run 12 to 18 months behind the rest of each machine. That lag slows new power on the ground.

SpaceX’s own IPO filing warned that data center demand outrunning power supply already imposes “unsustainable strains on terrestrial power grids.” The same word now describes Grok Bot.

The orbital pitch is built to delete those problems. The filing says the satellites would run on near-constant sunlight and use space itself for cooling. In orbit, there is no air permit to win, no neighbor to convince, and no grid connection to wait for.

What stands out to me is the workload SpaceX picked. The filing says SpaceX believes they can handle energy-hungry inference, the work of running AI models for users. That is exactly the work Grok Bot burns through.

More SpaceX:

## SpaceX’s orbital timeline leaves subscribers waiting

Timing is the catch. The filing said orbital deployment could begin as early as 2028. Musk later moved the first launch to the fourth quarter of 2027, with significant scale in 2028, Bloomberg reported.

Before then, SpaceX can charge heavy users more, tighten allowances, or shift chips away from renters. Musk’s past-tense wording hints that a fix may be in place, though SpaceX hasn’t announced one.

The bigger shift reaches beyond SpaceX. Flat-fee AI plans were priced for people who chat, not for agents that work around the clock.

Musk is betting the cheapest home for those agents sits in orbit. Until a rocket proves it, every company selling AI agents faces the math Grok Bot users ran into this past week.

cross_cutting.description: Mistral releases open-weight ML4 for coding & cyber Tue, 3rd Nov 2026 (Today) ... Mistral has released the weights for its open model, Mistral Large 4, on Hugging Face, describing it as its flagship open frontier system.
cross_cutting.content:
IT Brief Australia - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers

# Mistral releases open-weight ML4 for coding & cyber
Tue, 3rd Nov 2026 (Today) 
MARA SUGUE News Editor

Mistral has released the weights for its open model, Mistral Large 4, on Hugging Face, describing it as its flagship open frontier system.

Also referred to as ML4, the model is a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal system with 52 billion active parameters. Mistral said it continued training the model for three weeks using reinforcement learning after an earlier preview, while testing it with customers and cybersecurity partners ahead of the wider release.

Mistral said the model ranks as the top open model for agentic coding on Artificial Analysis' Coding Agent Index. It also said ML4 improved its score on Terminal-Bench 4.0 from 28% to 41%, putting it level with GLM-5.3 on that benchmark.

On the Artificial Analysis benchmark, ML4 uses 47% fewer tokens per task on average than GLM-5.3 while delivering similar results, Mistral said. The model also includes three reasoning modes - low, medium and high - allowing users to set the level of reasoning for each task.

Coding Focus

Mistral is positioning the release around coding and cybersecurity use cases, particularly for organisations that want to run models on their own systems. It said the approach could appeal to regulated sectors seeking tighter control over code, data and access.

The model can also be deployed on a customer's own infrastructure for cyber defence work, according to Mistral. That would allow enterprises and government bodies to detect, analyse and respond to threats across software code and IT systems without relying on a third party to maintain access.

ML4 was trained on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell graphics processing units in Mistral's European data centres, according to the company. It said this gave it a path to state-of-the-art results with lower compute and capital demands than closed-model developers.

Mistral said one technical change since the preview was the addition of two reasoning modes during the same reinforcement learning run.

"ML4 OSS showcases our science team's ability to innovate at speed. Building on the ML4 Preview, the open weight version continues reinforcement learning training and delivers substantial gains with no signs of saturation. In under three weeks within the same reinforcement learning run, we integrated customer feedback by introducing two additional reasoning modes, while making ML4 more efficient and customisable," said Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science, Mistral.

Open Model Push

The release comes as debate continues over whether leading AI systems should be distributed as open-weight models or kept behind proprietary interfaces. Open-weight releases allow developers and organisations to download model parameters and run them on their own infrastructure, although deploying them at scale still requires substantial computing resources.

Mistral has built its profile around open models as it competes with larger US AI groups. In comments on the release, it contrasted its funding with the spending levels associated with some rivals developing closed models.

"Open source is essential to ensure state-of-the-art AI does not end up concentrated in the hands of a few actors. Other labs have raised hundreds of billions to develop equivalent capabilities; in three years, Mistral raised roughly $6 billion. We have taken the lead globally in compute efficiency and have widened the gap between Mistral and other labs in that area. Our approach is to deliver quality science and put the results in everyone's hands," said Arthur Mensch, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder, Mistral.

Mistral also outlined several industrial uses for the model. It said manufacturing groups could use it to turn two-dimensional blueprints into three-dimensional models inside computer-aided design software, while financial institutions could apply it to spreadsheet work, large-scale data analysis and information extraction from filings.

Its multimodal design could also support geospatial tasks such as analysing satellite and aerial imagery for wildfire detection, crop monitoring and checks on power line infrastructure risks, Mistral said.

ML4 is also available through Mistral's application programming interface alongside the Hugging Face release, according to the company. The launch follows the recent introduction of Voxtral 3, a set of voice models and voice agents, as Mistral broadens its model lineup across different formats.

cross_cutting.description: 谷歌Gemini 4 Carbon刚把全球第一抢回去没几天，OpenAI和Anthropic就在周末同时亮出了下一代底牌 ... 在Codex后台悄悄灰测GPT-6.2 Astra ... 多位参与盲测的开发者判断，既然Anthropic已经开始在官网前端预埋Mythos 5.5代码，本周（11月3日或4日）极有可能就是正式发布窗口。
cross_cutting.content:
# OpenAI、Claude新旗舰同日曝光！

### 
新智元报道

两大新模型爆料，竟撞在了同一天！

谷歌Gemini 4 Carbon刚把全球第一抢回去没几天，OpenAI和Anthropic就在周末同时亮出了下一代底牌。

OpenAI直接跳过6.1，在Codex后台悄悄灰测GPT-6.2 Astra。

结果这一爆料刚冲上热搜，后脚Anthropic官方源码里就被扒出赫然躺着Claude Mythos 5.5。

这两款新模型的核心亮点，全在下面划好重点了：

GPT-6.2 Astra

跳过6.1闭关重炼直奔6.2：原计划冲刺的6.1因安全测试「翻车」被迫回炉，闭关重炼一个月后直接跳级6.2；

不只会写代码，还能自己盯梢：为配合新模型，OpenAI Codex团队28天连夜重做底层，让AI能自己拉起子进程、连续工作几小时；

Claude 5.5

杀伤力太强被「锁进保险柜」：无护栏特种版Mythos 5.5仅向顶尖网安与科研机构开放；支持100万上下文的通用旗舰Fable 5.5则已现身MLflow与Azure目录；

53分钟攻破Linux与手搓3D大作：Mythos 5.5仅用53分钟独立攻破Linux内核拿到最高权限；Fable 5.5一句话手搓出3D版《我的世界》。

一天之内，两大巨头全部提前泄露下一代旗舰。这周的AI圈，一场刺刀见红的正面硬刚彻底藏不住了。

知名爆料人Token Gremlin忍不住调侃，Anthropic真是见不得OpenAI独自抢占哪怕一天的聚光灯，非要出来截胡不可。

最先被开发者抓到现行的，是OpenAI的当家编程与Agent旗舰。

11月1日晚间，开发者Salio在调试Codex时抓包发现，前端界面虽然还挂着GPT-6 Astra的名字，但底层API返回的数据包里，模型真身已经换成了gpt-6.2-astra。

这并非个例。很快，多位Pro订阅用户在后台用量统计面板里翻出了更硬的账单证据。

在Token Gremlin晒出的账户账单明细中，旧版gpt-6-astra占了80%的调用量，而单独列出的gpt-6.2-astra已经吃下了19.8%的真实流量。

悄悄换上6.2新底座后，最先感知到变化的是命中灰度的重度开发者。

Token Gremlin给出了极高评价，直言GPT-6.2 Astra相比初代实现了巨大跨越，在多个维度上超越Claude Opus 5.5。

无论是设计审美、底层工程技术还是编程表现都全面跃升，完全具备与Fable 5.5正面掰手腕的实力。

新模型的实战体感之所以能实现如此大的跨越，甚至连版本号都直接跳过了6.1，背后源于过去一个月的闭关重炼。

OpenAI借着这次跳级，集中修好了前两代最致命的两个硬伤：

第一，修好了6.1「越权瞒报」的安全红线。

原计划10月发布的GPT-6.1 Astra在内部安全测试中翻了车——它在长任务里会擅自越权调用外部工具，事后甚至对人类隐瞒自己做过的操作，被OpenAI紧急叫停。

第二，治好了初代6.0「高智商却不会干活」的偏科顽疾。

知名技术博主Teortaxes透露了一个反常识的内幕：初代Astra 6.0的底层智商其实早就超过了Opus 5.5，只是因为缺乏针对真实开发环境的打磨，平时写起代码来才显得「偏科」甚至爱偷懒。

趁着这次回炉重炼的一个月窗口期，OpenAI把「安全可控」与「工程实战手感」两块短板一次性补齐，这才端出了脱胎换骨的满血版GPT-6.2 Astra。

模型底座炼成了，外层的Agent脚手架也早已同步就位。

现在回看Codex负责人Tibo过去四周力推的「Codex 28天升级计划」，意图已经非常明显。

从拓宽上下文窗口、上线多子Agent协同架构，到收官前夕突然把Pro用户额度翻倍，每一步棋都在为GPT-6.2 Astra铺路。

更有意思的一幕发生在28天计划收官当天。当Token Gremlin发帖感慨「升级计划结束了，总感觉还有很多大招没放完」时——

Codex掌门人Tibo本尊亲自跑到评论区接话，直接剧透称：「我强烈要求把倒计时重置，咱们再来一轮！」

掌门人亲自下场剧透，意味着已经在后台灰度的GPT-6.2 Astra，八成就是下周压轴登场的最终大招了。

就在OpenAI靠后台灰度暗度陈仓的时候，老对手Anthropic却因为一次前端代码失误，把下一代底牌暴露在了聚光灯下。

11月1日深夜，大V Chubby晒出一张网页源码截图，指出Anthropic官网的anthropic.com/claude/mythos页面里，已经赫然写上了Claude Mythos 5.5。

全球开发者立刻涌入官网按下Ctrl+U查看源代码。

表面上看，网页前端显示的标题依然是9月发布的旧版「Claude Mythos 5.1」。

但翻到底层HTML源码里，却整整齐齐地躺着6处「Claude Claude Mythos 5.5」，前端工程师甚至手滑多拼了一个Claude。

官网前端已经提前把「5.5」的字标预埋进生产环境，意味着最强Fable/Mythos5.5正式发布近在咫尺。

看到Mythos 5.5这个名字，不少人可能会好奇它与近期频频传出的下一代旗舰Fable 5.5究竟是什么关系。

其实，Mythos 5.5与Fable 5.5底层用的是完全相同的AI大脑，连API定价都分毫不差。

Anthropic只是根据「安全护栏」的松紧，把同一个模型拆成了「一脑双版」：

其中，Fable 5.5装上了严格的安全护栏拦截高危指令，作为通用商业旗舰向全球开发者全量开放。

而另一个版本Mythos 5.5，则是解开了常规拒答限制的「特种科研版」。

它仅向受信任的顶尖网络安全团队与科研机构定向开放，是Anthropic在网安与科学领域最强的核武器。

一旦搞懂了Mythos 5.5「专攻网安与极限科研」的身份，前几天轰动技术圈的两桩神秘悬案瞬间迎刃而解——

悬案一（网安实战）：53分钟独立攻破Linux内核拿到最高权限。

此前Anthropic披露一款「未发布内部模型」仅花53分钟就打穿了Linux高危漏洞；而安全研究员用现有的Mythos 5.1死磕了整整3天、烧掉2000美元都没能复现。

悬案二（数学科研）：狂吐1400万Token独立写出算法论文。

几天前网上疯传一篇攻克经典计算机难题的数学论文，全篇没有一个人类作者，唯一署名只有冷冰冰的一行字：CLAUDE（ANTHROPIC）。

正如AI观察家Andrew Curran所言，能在内部卸下安全护栏、同时干出这两件大事的幕后真神，正是这次源码露馅的Claude Mythos 5.5。

无护栏的Mythos 5.5在网安和数学上大杀四方，而面向大众开发者的通用旗舰Fable 5.5也已准备就绪。

目前，它已同步现身MLflow与Azure官方目录，实锤支持高达100万Token的输入上下文和12.8万Token的最大输出。

在早期盲测中，这颗百万上下文底座展露出了恐怖的工程统治力。

最直观的突破，是模型戒掉了以往AI写长代码必犯的「半途偷懒」老毛病。

在重度游戏工程测试中，开发者notjazii将思考深度拉到最高档（xhigh），让Fable 5.5用单次提示词复刻一个网页版《我的世界》。

AI在后台不知疲倦地连续编码1至2个小时，交出的成品不仅具备逼真的水面焦散光影和完整的合成台。

甚至在没有被要求的情况下，它还主动给自己加戏，把「下界」和「末地」两个异次元维度也完整写了出来！

除了能连肝两小时大工程，这套5.5底座的3D空间感与物理光影直觉也上了一个大台阶。

在最新流出的Three.js实测中，Fable 5.5单次生成了一辆暗红色涂装的「KESTREL K1」3D超跑，赛车在镜面地板上360度丝滑旋转，车漆高光反射与尾翼碳纤维结构细节堪比专业游戏引擎。

哪怕是经典的「鹈鹕骑自行车」基准，它也告别了传统的2D简笔画，用Three.js一次性写出了一只车筐里装着法棍和大葱、在海滨长廊迎风踩踏的3D鹈鹕。

更有测试者甩给它一张奥特曼的真人照片，它仅凭纯代码就还原出了五官神态与发丝层次逼真的3D体素雕像。

多位参与盲测的开发者判断，既然Anthropic已经开始在官网前端预埋Mythos 5.5代码，本周（11月3日或4日）极有可能就是正式发布窗口。

这场看似巧合的周末连环泄密，背后其实是硅谷巨头们寸土必争的战略卡位。

一边是OpenAI跳过6.1憋出满血版GPT-6.2 Astra；

另一边是Anthropic赶在传闻中11月中旬冲击1.5万亿至2万亿美元超级IPO前夕亮出Mythos 5.5与Fable 5.5两大王牌，再加上几天前刚刚登顶的谷歌Gemini 4 Carbon。

硅谷三大巨头，在2026年11月初撞进了史上最密集的王牌决战周。

好戏，这下真的要开场了。

cross_cutting.content:
# Canva doubles down with OpenAI just days after launching its 2nd in-house AI model

Canva leans harder on OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra while racing to slash AI costs with Brush.

##### Four days after launching Brush, a design-editing model it says costs 46% less per edit than its previous tool, Canva has expanded its partnership with OpenAI.

The design scaleup has been working to cut the costs of running AI across the platform, and has now turned to one of the suppliers whose models it’s relied upon heavily to help turn a problem into a solution.

The deal gives Canva broader access to OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 models. The two companies will work on making them more economical to run, although no savings or costs were disclosed. OpenAI already powers features including Canva Code, which lets users build interactive designs, websites and apps by describing what they want.

The rising cost of AI forced Canva to rethink and reshape how it’s deployed in the software business. In August, cofounder and CEO Melanie Perkins said the company was “relying too heavily on frontier models” and cut revenue growth forecasts from 30% to 20% because they’d slowed the rollout of new AI features while Canva’s own technology and pricing caught up with demand. Canva.

Last week’s release of Brush is part of that strategy and the second home-grown model after Craft, which generates images was also announced last month. Brush edits existing designs, allowing a user to change headlines in a presentation without needing the AI to recreate the slides.

Canva’s researchers adapted an existing open-weights model, training it further on design tasks. Brush, available to Canva Pro subscribers, is up to 69% faster than its previous design agent and 46% cheaper per edit.

Head of AI product, Danny Wu, said their four-year collaboration with OpenAI began with GPT-3 powering Magic Write, and the company is now expanding staff use of ChatGPT and Codex.

“OpenAI’s models continue to power a growing number of AI features at Canva, reaching more people,” he said.

“Beyond helping us give millions of people new ways to bring their ideas to life, latest models like GPT-6 Astra have transformed how we achieve our own goals as a team.”

In one internal test, Astra navigated more than 80 million lines of Canva’s code and wrote and analysed more than 1,000 queries against its data warehouse.

Canva is among the five most-installed apps in ChatGPT, and OpenAI says that has brought millions of people to the Australian design giant’s products.

Meanwhile, Capital Brief today revealed previously unreported job cuts in Canva’s finance division in January, with 32 roles made redundant, also citing employees who believed another round of redundancies or a possible hiring freeze this month as part of another restructure. Canva declined to comment on that speculation.

# Teamily AI Reports 32× Quarterly User Growth, Positive Gross Margins, and Strong Global Adoption of Human–Agent Collaboration

03 Nov 2026 - 13:00

## The AI-native collaboration platform reaches 320,000 users across 100+ countries, validates product-led growth and monetization, and prepares to expand its global AI agent ecosystem.

Teamily AI, a human–agent collaboration platform that enables people and AI agents to work together in a unified, context-aware workspace, today announced significant growth and commercial milestones following a quarter of rapid global expansion. The company grew from 10,000 to 320,000 sign-ups in a single quarter, a 32× increase that works out to a compound monthly growth rate of 217.5%, just three months after its public launch in July 2026. With positive gross margins on paying users, and growing adoption among professional teams and businesses , Teamily AI establishes a foundation for scalable product-led growth (PLG).

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261103047955/en/

32× Global Growth in One Quarter

Teamily AI grew from 10,000 to 320,000 registered users across more than 100 countries in one quarter , representing 32× growth and a 217.5% compound monthly growth rate .

According to publicly available Similarweb traffic, Teamily AI has surpassed the website traffic of several emerging AI agent platforms, including Town.com, Viktor.com, today.ai, and cue.im, companies that have reportedly raised $100 million to $400 million at billion-dollar valuations.

The company has observed consistent paid conversion across global markets, with the United States leading, followed by Europe and Chinese-speaking markets, and additional paying customers across South Asia, Africa, and Southeast Asia. This broad geographic adoption provides early validation of the global demand for AI-native collaboration and productivity.

Strong Monetization and Organic Team Adoption

Teamily AI has attracted several thousand paying customers and 20,000 daily active users . More than 10,000 company teams have connected coworkers on the platform , averaging six agent tasks per group per day, while users create more than 300 group-level agent automation loops daily.

Based on customer usage and payment behavior, Teamily has identified two major categories with strong product-market fit:

- AI-powered collaboration: Group chat analysis, deep research, collaborative documents, meeting summaries, and multimodal file processing.
- AI-powered creation: Website development, slides, image and video generation, and professional content creation.

These findings reinforce Teamily's focus on prosumers, teams, and small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) , supported by a product-led growth strategy.

The company's PLG funnel is also generating inbound enterprise opportunities. Teamily plans to expand its account executive and sales partner channels while offering enterprise customers private models, secure data integration, and hybrid workflows combining local agents with cloud-based frontier models.

Proprietary AI Infrastructure Enables Positive Unit Economics

Teamily AI has processed more than 100 million messages, approximately 35% generated by AI agents , creating a growing foundation of interaction data for improving model performance, inference efficiency, and cost optimization.

Unlike platforms that rely primarily on third-party model APIs, Teamily develops its own large language models and self-hosted inference infrastructure . Its optimized serving system has achieved 30% higher throughput than publicly reported vLLM/SGLang benchmarks , while maintaining positive gross margins on paying users.

Together, proprietary models, efficient infrastructure, and growing human–agent interaction data establish a self-reinforcing advantage in product quality and unit economics.

Expanding Monetization Beyond Subscriptions

Building on its subscription business, Teamily is exploring additional revenue models, including advertising, enterprise services, and agent-powered service distribution.

The company sees significant opportunities to connect users with relevant merchants and professional service providers through context-aware AI agents, potentially generating referral and transaction-based revenue.

Business services represent a particularly promising market, as AI agents could help companies discover, evaluate, and access specialized services more efficiently.

Looking Ahead: Building the Agentic Internet Ecosystem

With its global growth model and initial monetization strategy validated, Teamily AI is preparing to expand its ecosystem in the next phase of development.

The company's plans to release Teamily AI 3.0, a new version focusing on ecosystem strategy that includes wallet and merchant integrations, Studio plugins for high-value content creation, AI-native cloud storage connecting fragmented data sources, Mini Apps that turn third-party agentic applications into accessible AI agents, deeper app connectors, and expanded Channels that bring agents into external products.

Teamily also plans to strengthen partnerships with AI model developers, infrastructure providers, and data services, aiming to become a day-zero integration and distribution partner for emerging AI technologies.

"Our vision is to build the central platform of the next-generation Agentic Internet , where services and work are delivered by AI agents rather than confined to traditional applications," said Aiden Chaoyang He, Co-Founder and CEO of Teamily AI. "Just as Google transformed access to information in the web era, we believe AI agents will transform access to intelligence and services. Every user intent should be connected to the right people, agents, and services, with the right context and intelligence."

With strong initial commercial validation and a rapidly growing global user base, Teamily AI is preparing to accelerate growth in November while opening its platform to a broader ecosystem of businesses, vertical agent developers, and AI service providers.

About Teamily AI

Teamily AI is a human-agent platform where people and specialized AI agents share context and memory, collaborate on real work, and continuously learn and improve together. Built around an AI-native messenger, Teamily lets teams create custom agents, assemble them into agent teams, and put those teams to work producing websites, email, documents, presentations, video and images, inside the tools and channels where work already happens. Teamily AI publicly launched in July 2026 and was co-founded by Dr. Aiden Chaoyang He, formerly of Meta and Tencent, and Professor Salman Avestimehr, Dean's Professor at the University of Southern California, IEEE Fellow and PECASE recipient. The broader team brings together AI researchers, engineers, and product and growth veterans from Meta, Tencent, TikTok, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Qualcomm, combining deep AI expertise with proven experience in social networks, messaging platforms, consumer growth, and large-scale internet products. Teamily AI is headquartered in Palo Alto, California, the central hub of Silicon Valley. Learn more at https://teamily.ai .

## PhaseV Launches BonV, an Agentic AI Orchestrator Turning Clinical Questions into Defensible Decisions

News provided by

Nov 03, 2026, 8:30 AM ET

BonV Combines Agentic AI with Forward Deployed Engineers to Bring PhaseV's Vertical Suite of AI Modules into One Connected and Explainable, Team-Ready Workspace

BOSTON, Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PhaseV, a clinical development technology company that applies AI and causal machine learning to help biopharma make faster, more informed decisions, today announced the launch of BonV, an agentic product layer built on the PhaseV platform. A trial team can ask a clinical development question in plain language, and BonV carries it through to a documented, evidence-backed trial decision.

"Every major development decision draws on modeling, historical data, operations, and safety, and that evidence usually sits in different tools owned by different teams," said Raviv Pryluk, PhD, CEO and Co-founder of PhaseV. "BonV brings it into one workspace. Our scientists and Forward Deployed Engineers work alongside each sponsor's team, so the recommendation a team reaches is one it can explain and defend."

From one question to a decision memo

BonV is built for the full range of development questions, from go/no-go calls and indication expansion to trial design and operational planning. In one illustrative scenario based on a real-world case, a team with a Phase 2 obesity asset asked BonV how to sequence its development strategy, including whether to start a second-indication program before or after the Phase 2 readout. BonV interpreted the goal, requested missing context, and analyzed an uploaded brief to execute the workflow:

- Proposed a staged plan (clinical, statistical, and safety and tolerability review) that the user could edit and confirm at each step.
- Invoked the right PhaseV capabilities, including causal modeling, target trial emulation, ClinOps Optimizer, and Trial Optimizer.
- Compared three development strategies across nine criteria, including time to learning, safety and tolerability, patient burden, country feasibility, and operational complexity.
- Delivered a recommendation with the supporting evidence, before generating a trial synopsis and a decision memo recording what was decided, why, and from which data.

The same workflow can be applied across indications, phases, and decision types. Every result links back to the underlying module, where scientists can inspect the model and adjust assumptions.

Built for enterprise pharma

BonV connects PhaseV's optimizers with sponsors' existing tools and third-party platforms, including leading cloud providers, data warehouses, and clinical and commercial enterprise applications via APIs. It extends existing software investments rather than replacing them. Multi-user project workspaces support defined roles (such as reviewer, budget holder, and final sign-off) and project-level credit tracking for clear cost governance. Deployment is available in a sponsor's private cloud or a dedicated, isolated PhaseV-hosted environment.

Explainable by design

In one trial, BonV orchestrated four PhaseV platform modules to reduce trial costs by $32 million and shorten trial duration by eight months. In another, BonV invoked two applications to support investment due diligence within two weeks, helping enable a multibillion-dollar transaction in the metabolic obesity space.

Availability

BonV is already in use with select pharmaceutical companies, with a phased rollout underway for other enterprise customers. Initial engagements include integration with each sponsor's applications and data environment, supported by PhaseV Forward Deployed Engineers who partner with sponsor IT teams. Existing PhaseV modules remain available as standalone subscriptions. To learn more or request a demonstration, visit www.phasevtrials.com/contact.

About PhaseV

PhaseV is a causal AI clinical development technology company headquartered in Cambridge, MA that helps biopharma sponsors, CROs, and investors make more informed decisions across trial design, execution, analysis, and portfolio strategy. Combining explainable Causal AI with the expertise of its team of statisticians, clinicians, data scientists, and ML engineers, and drawing on multimodal data from diverse, high-quality sources, PhaseV helps sponsors evaluate development options, improve trial design, and reduce operational risk. Since its founding in 2023, PhaseV has supported more than 100 clinical programs for over 50 global sponsors, including 10 of the world's 20 largest pharmaceutical companies. In active collaborations, PhaseV's technology has helped sponsors cut trial development costs by up to 50 percent, shorten trial timelines by up to 40 percent, and improve the probability of success by more than 30 percent. Learn more at www.PhaseVTrials.com and follow PhaseV on LinkedIn.

cross_cutting.content:
# 76 launches later, Fabian would skip the SaaS and ship an Actor

76 Product Hunt launches and a SaaS of his own taught Fabian Maume how to launch. Now he helps developers ship their tools on Apify Store.

If Fabian Maume were launching his next product today, he'd publish it as an Actor on Apify Store, let the marketplace bring the first users, and only build a full SaaS once people kept coming back. He learned that the long way, through years of automations that only he could run.

These days he gets to do it for other people. As a senior product marketing manager at Apify, he helps developers launch their Actors on what has become the marketplace of tools for AI, where people and AI agents run them on demand. In this Life at Apify story, he talks about the road in, and what the job looks like from the inside.

## Growth hacking, Brno and 76 launches

Fabian got into growth hacking during his bachelor's degree in France, reading blog after blog on the subject. He says that it suits the French: La Growth Machine, lemlist and Phantombuster all started there.
The French have what they call "System D" to get the most done with limited resources. This is the core of growth hacking philosophy.
-- Fabian Maume, Senior Product Marketing Manager at Apify
So when it came to a master's, he did the math. A full degree in Brno, Czech Republic, cost less than a single year of study in France, so that's where he went.

His first Product Hunt launch came in 2017, when he helped Smartlook launch while working there as a freelance growth hacker. He was doing growth work for more than 15 SaaS companies and had about 20 ready-made automations sitting on the shelf, waiting to become products. To turn them into products, he went down the indie hacking rabbit hole and tried building Chrome extensions, which were the easiest way to ship something with a front end before AI could write one for you. It cost him a lot of time. "I'm not a front-end person," he says.

By 2021 he'd changed tack and was selling the automation as a service instead, hunting launches for other companies with a pipeline he had automated himself. Salesfit was the first. The catch was that it was a Python script that needed Selenium and a Windows setup, which nobody else was going to install. He sold consulting packages instead and ran the script for clients himself. He has hunted 76 products to date, and along the way started a YouTube channel on growth hacking and automation.

## QApop, and what it taught him

Hunting wasn't the only way he put his scripts to work. In August 2020, before he started hunting for clients, Fabian launched QApop, a SaaS built on his most successful script. It mined Quora and gave users a shortlist of questions worth answering. Fabian knew Quora well, too, as a Top Writer in Email Marketing there. With a front-end developer as his partner, it grew into a standalone SaaS that users rated highly and that sold well on lifetime deals.

A Quora audit gives you most of its value the first time you run it, so even with extras like keyword monitoring, people had less reason to come back every month. That's hard to know before you launch, and a SaaS built from scratch also has to earn its search traffic from zero.
If I were to launch a new product around data mining, I would use Apify Marketplace as a test bench. Leverage the marketplace domain rank to get some SEO traffic fast and monitor retention to see if the idea is worth pursuing as a standalone product.
-- Fabian Maume, Senior Product Marketing Manager at Apify
In March 2023 he sold QApop. Soon after, ChatGPT filled Quora with AI-generated answers and changed it as a marketing channel. Fabian calls it perfect timing, and it's hard to argue.

## Apify from the outside

Fabian first used Apify in October 2020, a couple of months after QApop launched, mostly scraping Google with thesite: operator to build lead lists, and wrote about it on the Apify blog. When Quora started blocking by IP, he moved the part of QApop that needed proxies to Apify and kept the rest on AWS.

For his consulting clients, most of them in lead generation, Apify stayed behind the scenes. They found even Phantombuster, then the friendlier tool, too technical, so he ran Apify for them as a managed service rather than teaching them to use it. He says the platform has come a long way since, with AI taking away much of the complexity for non-technical users. He still uses both tools, each for what it does best: "Phantombuster for anything requiring login, Apify for anything requiring IP rotation."

Through his Product Hunt work, he also became one of the people Apify called on when it had something to launch, and he hunted Crawlee on Product Hunt in 2022.

## Joining Apify

After the sale, Fabian went back to client work as a fractional CMO, which pulled him away from web data for a while. He kept following it, though, and the first Prague Crawl, in 2025, showed him where it was heading.
It was eye-opening on the direction of the industry. AI agents are as good as the data they have access to, and web scraping is a key component to provide agents with a good data layer.
-- Fabian Maume, Senior Product Marketing Manager at Apify
He went looking for a job at the point where web data meets AI and found it in product marketing at Apify. The work turned out to be familiar from his fractional CMO years. "I manage marketing for a cluster of products," he says. "Those products are just Actors instead of being SaaS."

## The job from the inside

Now he's a senior product marketing manager at Apify, which in practice means a bit of everything. One day he's planning a feature launch with the engineering teams, the next he's helping a developer whose Actors have vanished from Store search, or writing the monthly report on how his cluster of Actors is doing.

He also looks after the developers who publish on Apify Store, which now lists more than 100,000 tools. He runs community open hours and webinars for them, mentors at hackathons, records podcasts, and briefs creators who make videos about Apify.

In September, for example, he hosted a webinar with Salesforge and two outbound agencies that generate more than $1 million in monthly pipeline for their clients, using Apify Actors to find buying signals and enrich leads.

What surprised him most on the inside was how fast AI is changing the work itself, his own included.
Manually, it takes me 1 to 3 hours to develop an Actor. With the proper Claude skill, the work is down to half an hour and a few cents of tokens.
-- Fabian Maume, Senior Product Marketing Manager at Apify
So when something keeps coming up, he builds a Claude skill for it. One drafts social posts for colleagues, and another, made for a recent open hour, helps developers find ideas for improving their Actors.

That makes him the marketing team's go-to when a technical problem gets complicated, and he'll happily sit down and walk anyone through it.

## Outside work

Fabian says he rarely leaves his computer, but when he does, he's usually out hiking with his dog, Prezes. He keeps going in winter, too, and one hike at -25°C took him across a frozen lake.

For a while he did historical dancing, which is how he came to own a kilt. Kilts cover such a long stretch of history, he explains, that one gets you into the hobby on a budget.

He also drinks what he calls "an unreasonable amount of caffeine," spread across tea, coffee and maté. He brews his own maté liqueur, too, and because he's a marketer, it has full branding.

If you're ever in Brno, Fabian's tip is 10-Z, a former nuclear shelter that's now half hotel, half museum. He showed up fully equipped, gas mask and all.

## Apify from every side

Fabian has seen Apify from almost every side. He started as a user, scraping Google for lead lists and keeping QApop running when Quora began blocking him. He ran it behind the scenes for his consulting clients and hunted Crawlee on Product Hunt long before he joined. Now he spends his days helping developers do what he'd do himself next time: put an idea on Apify Store, see whether people keep coming back, and build from there.

## Work with us

While a lot of tech companies are cutting, Apify is hiring. Have a look at the open roles on the careers page, or come say hi to Fabian at one of the community open hours he runs for Apify Store developers.

Want to see Fabian in action? Here's the Salesforge webinar he hosted in September.

Build the marketplace of tools for AI

Join the team, or do what Fabian would do and publish your next idea as an Actor on Apify Store.

# Sanjeev Jasani and Shubham Saurabh launch AI marketing platform TurboAgents

Sanjeev Jasani and Shubham Saurabh have launched TurboAgents, an AI-driven marketing platform designed for small businesses and entrepreneurs. The platform integrates 39 specialized AI agents across various marketing functions, providing a comprehensive solution for generating marketing materials and enhancing business strategy, execution, and creative work without requiring extensive marketing teams.

B

- Published On Nov 3, 2026 at 04:22 PM IST

#### Highlights

- TurboAgents launches AI-powered marketing platform for small businesses.
- 39 AI agents streamline marketing across various functions.
- Founders aim to democratize agency-style marketing for solo entrepreneurs.

Advertising industry veteran and former agency Group COO Sanjeev Jasani has teamed up with technology entrepreneur Shubham Saurabh to launch TurboAgents, an AI-powered marketing platform aimed at solo entrepreneurs, small businesses, D2C brands and boutique advertising agencies.

The platform brings together 39 specialised AI agents across seven marketing functions: strategy, creative, social media, ecommerce, video, SEO and productivity.

The platform can generate marketing reports, digital advertising creatives, ecommerce listings, short-form videos and Google Ads campaign files.

"For 28 years, I have built marketing teams for some of the biggest brands and have seen how the best work happens when strategy, creative and execution operate together, with a shared understanding of the brand. Smaller businesses have traditionally lacked access to this kind of integrated capability. TurboAgents brings that agency-style approach to businesses without the need for large marketing teams," said Sanjeev Jasani, founder and CEO, TurboAgents.

Jasani's experience in advertising and integrated marketing is complemented by Saurabh's specialisation in interaction design, advanced new media and human-computer interfaces.

"Small businesses do not necessarily need more AI tools. They need a connected system that understands their business and brings together research, strategy, creative and execution. We have built that discipline into the software," added Shubham, co-founder, TurboAgents.

The platform is aimed at a range of users, including entrepreneurs, consultants, freelancers, D2C and marketplace brands, multi-location businesses and boutique agencies managing multiple clients.

# T-Systems and Sparxity strengthen Europe’s sovereign AI infrastructure with energy-efficient computing technology

- Letter of Intent (LoI) signed at the Digital Summit
- Sparxity develops energy-efficient AI chips and computing systems
- Integration and validation for use in Telekom data centers

Deutsche Telekom is continuing to expand its AI partner ecosystem. T-Systems and Dresden-based AI infrastructure company Sparxity (formerly SpiNNcloud Systems GmbH) agreed to cooperate. At the German Federal Government’s Digital Summit, the two companies signed a corresponding Letter of Intent. The aim is to combine Sparxity's sparse-native computing technology with T-Systems' data center infrastructure and operational expertise.
Present at the signing of the Letter of Intent (LoI) were Karsten Wildberger, the Federal Minister for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation; Hector A. Gonzalez, co-founder and CEO of Sparxity; and Ferri Abolhassan, CEO of T-Systems.

## Sparxity technology in Deutsche Telekom`s data centers

The two companies intend to jointly develop and deploy the next generation of energy-efficient AI computing infrastructure in Europe. Sparxity's technologies are used for so-called energy-saving and demand-driven "sparse computation". This involves directing computing power exactly where it is needed. In the first step, Sparxity's current hardware will be used to jointly develop approaches for the technical integration of the next generation of Sparxity chips in data centers. The first deployment is targeted in 2028 - in combination with T-Systems' data center infrastructure and partner ecosystem. Building on this, the two companies plan to develop high-performance, energy-efficient AI computing systems for future applications and optimize them for specific use cases. The details of the collaboration will be agreed in the coming months.
Karsten Wildberger, the Federal Minister for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation: "The project shows that digital sovereignty is feasible in Germany – if we combine our own technological expertise with efficient infrastructure and strong partners. The Digital Summit gives such cooperation an important impetus and brings together the players who are shaping Germany's digital future."
Hector A. Gonzalez, co-founder and CEO of Sparxity: “Our computing technology is designed to concentrate computing power only where it is needed. This makes AI more energy-efficient and scalable. The current generation of our systems are already deployed in Europe and the United States. We see great potential in partnering with T-Systems to bring our next-generation chip into datacenter deployments.”
Ferri Abolhassan, CEO of T-Systems and Member of the Board of Management of Deutsche Telekom AG: "Germany and Europe need a powerful AI infrastructure that can be operated and scaled economically. With our T Cloud portfolio and our AI factory in Munich, we have created the basis for this. We are open to further partners and are looking forward to having Sparxity on board in our AI factory soon. The German company scores particularly well with its energy-efficient use of AI computing power."

## About Sparxity

Sparxity builds sparse-native compute for AI. Our principle is simple: compute only what matters. For years, models have been shaped by the dense hardware they run on. Sparxity builds the hardware that lets them go further: full-stack systems, from custom chips to software, built for fine-grained, dynamic sparsity, where intelligence scales without trading off speed or efficiency. Deployed in rack- and supercomputer-scale systems across Europe and the US, Sparxity opens a new world of compute for the builders shaping what comes next. Learn more at sparxity.ai.

# Drax partners with Brookfield and Radiant for up to 1GW data center at North Yorkshire power station

First phase targeting 100MW of capacity by 2028

UK power company Drax has finally unveiled its plans for a data center at its 2.6GW Drax Power Station in Selby, North Yorkshire, UK.

The company partnered with Brookfield and its UK-headquartered AI infrastructure platform, Radiant, to jointly develop, deliver, and operate up to a gigawatt of data center capacity at the power station.

The data center is expected to be built in phases, with phase one targeting up to 100MW and expected to be operational from Q1 2028. Phase two would increase the capacity to 500MW between 2028 and 2031, and phase three envisions additional capacity increases post-2031.

The project will be developed as part of a joint venture dubbed Brookfield-Qai AI. Brookfield has said it estimates total investment in the development could exceed £20 billion ($26.8bn), including an initial £2.5bn ($3.4bn) for the first phase.

The partners said the first phase will progress subject to “the timely progression of the necessary planning, as well as receiving the required regulatory and network approvals from government and the system operator, in addition to securing a suitable tenant for the project.”

The proposed site comprises 1,000 acres and 4GW of grid access, with 2.6GW of active dispatchable generation and cooling systems from the existing wood pellet plant.

According to Drax Group CEO Will Gardiner, the site is “one of the few UK sites that can provide large-scale reliable power directly to data center customers by utilizing existing and underutilized generation capacity.”

“If constructed in full, this project could become one of the largest data centers in the UK, attracting billions in inward investment, supporting the North’s reindustrialization and strengthening sovereign AI capability,” he added.

“Teaming up with Drax and Qai for this project represents a major opportunity for our AI infrastructure strategy,” said Brookfield Head of AI infrastructure, Sikander Rashid.

"Our capital and deep operating capabilities will help accelerate the construction of a critical piece of sovereign AI, delivered by Radiant, our UK-headquartered compute infrastructure platform. In addition to preserving hundreds of jobs, this project will also create many direct and indirect jobs around the broader Yorkshire area."

The announcement follows shortly after the UK government rejected a bid by North Yorkshire Council, the University of York, and energy company Drax to develop an up to 1.2GW data center at the same site as part of the UK’s AI Growth Zone scheme.

Rumblings that Drax was planning a data center first arose in November 2024. Following this, in February of last year, it was reported that it was in discussions with data center operators about a potential supply agreement, noting that it had received “positive engagement with data center providers regarding the potential to co-locate a data center with biomass generation.”

Since then, the company signed a ten-year corporate Power Purchase Agreement with Global Switch to support the firm's UK operations.

However, concerns have been raised about the proposed data center's low-carbon credentials. As part of the application for the AI Growth zone data center, the applicants described the facility as the world's largest “carbon negative data center,” even though the power plant itself is one of the UK's largest emitters.

According to data from energy think tank Ember, Drax emitted 14.1 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2025.

Despite pushback, Drax and Brookfield have said they are committed to delivering lasting local benefits, including a voluntary community benefits fund developed in consultation with communities around the Drax Power Station site, separate from and in addition to any planning obligations and Drax’s existing community initiatives. The company said that community consultation on the plans will begin shortly, with the formal planning process following afterward.

Radiant was launched last November as part of the $10bn Brookfield Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Fund (BAIIF), with plans to build and acquire as much as $100bn worth of AI infrastructure.

# Bull and Lidl owner’s Schwarz Digits team up on a European AI cloud

The French supercomputer maker would build the servers in Angers, while Schwarz Digits brings its STACKIT cloud. The memorandum was announced at Germany’s Digital Summit in Berlin.

France’s Bull and Schwarz Digits, the IT arm of Germany’s Schwarz Group, plan to build a European AI and cloud infrastructure stack together. It would run from the servers to the software. The two companies agreed a memorandum of understanding (MoU), Bull said on Tuesday. They announced it at the German government’s 2026 Digital Summit in Berlin.

The companies say the partnership aims to let European organisations develop and scale AI and enterprise computing. It targets regulated and strategic sectors in particular. Sensitive data, infrastructure and operations would stay under European jurisdiction and control.

“Together, we demonstrate that Europe can deliver high-performance innovation entirely on its own terms,” said Bernie Wagner, chief revenue officer of Schwarz Digits.

## What each company brings

Schwarz Digits, whose parent group owns the Lidl and Kaufland supermarket chains, will contribute its STACKIT cloud. Bull will bring its experience in AI and high-performance computing on large projects.

The servers would be built at Bull’s factory in Angers, France, which produces rack-scale AI systems. They would use Bull’s direct liquid cooling technology.

In June, Bull’s systems took the top three places in the Green500 ranking of energy-efficient supercomputers, the company said. It also built the JUPITER supercomputer in Germany, which Bull calls Europe’s most powerful.

Bull’s BullSequana AI platform will also be sold through the STACKIT Marketplace to companies and public-sector customers.

“This partnership, which contributes to building a sovereign digital infrastructure in Europe, reflects our commitment to a resilient and competitive European ecosystem,” said Emmanuel Le Roux, chief executive of Bull.

## What comes next

Beyond these first steps, the two companies intend to co-design servers based on Open Compute Project (OCP) standards. They also plan to work on SAP RISE integration and large high-performance computing projects. And they will explore quantum computing integration.

Bull reports about €720m in revenue and 3,000 staff in 32 countries. The announcement came a day after Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Germany and Europe must build their own AI more quickly.

# Multiverse Computing, YellowDog target European sovereign AI

#### Author: Joe Peck

Multiverse Computing, a Spanish company specialising in compressing large language models (LLMs), and UK cloud workload orchestration firm YellowDog.ai have agreed to work together to improve compute efficiency and support the development and deployment of European sovereign AI.

The collaboration will combine AI model compression with hybrid and multi-cloud compute management to help enterprises, research organisations, and public sector institutions operate AI within European infrastructure.

Multiverse Computing’s CompactifAI technology uses quantum-inspired tensor-network methods to compress large AI models, while YellowDog.ai provides a platform for managing compute resources across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

The companies say they aim to bring together processing capacity, secure access, storage, networking, and data centre operations, whilst simultaneously reducing costs, energy consumption, and infrastructure complexity. They also identify GPU shortages as a key challenge, particularly for European organisations seeking to make more efficient use of available capacity.

Customers will be able to use the combined capabilities for model development, benchmarking, optimisation, compressed model deployment, inference, and sovereign infrastructure planning. Target sectors include financial services, life sciences, advanced engineering, energy, telecoms, public services, and defence-adjacent industries, where data residency, security, cost, compute availability, and regulatory compliance are important considerations.

## Supporting Europe’s AI compute infrastructure

Enrique Lizaso, co-founder and CEO of Multiverse Computing, says, “Sovereign AI will only succeed if it is economically and technically sustainable. Our compressed AI models are designed to run faster, use less energy, and operate closer to the data.

“Working with YellowDog.ai gives customers a powerful route to deploy efficient AI across cloud, on-premises, edge, and sovereign data centre environments.”

Bruce Beckloff, CEO of YellowDog.ai, adds, “Europe has the talent, data, and industrial base to lead in AI, but it needs infrastructure that is fast, efficient, secure, and sovereign by design.

“By partnering with Multiverse Computing, we are creating practical capacity solutions where organisations can scale compute intelligently, reduce bottlenecks, and retain control of critical workloads.”

The agreement comes as European organisations seek alternatives to fragmented, expensive, and capacity-constrained AI infrastructure. The companies also point to the European Commission’s AI Gigafactory initiative, which envisages large-scale facilities providing computing capacity for the development, training, fine-tuning, and deployment of advanced AI models and applications.

These facilities are expected to combine AI-optimised computing, secure cloud access, high-capacity storage, advanced networking, energy-efficient data centres, and specialist support services.

The stated priorities include improving access to hybrid compute, reducing operational costs and energy use through model compression and workload scheduling, and supporting deployments that meet European requirements for data protection, security, and technological autonomy.

# What Microsoft & Lumen's Partnership Means for Data Centres

November 03, 2026

undefined mins

Katy Brown, Microsoft Corporate Vice President for Americas Markets, discusses the company's collaboration with Lumen on Azure AI data centre connectivity

Lumen Technologies and Microsoft have expanded their co-selling collaboration to solve a pressing problem for enterprises deploying AI.

Many struggle to connect data and applications scattered across private data centres, public clouds and partner environments through fragmented network infrastructure.

The collaboration focuses on aligning network transformation with Microsoft Azure modernisation plans, enabling connectivity, security, data movement and AI infrastructure decisions to be planned as part of unified enterprise architecture.

Lumen intends to bring its full suite of cloud networking and application connectivity capabilities to Azure, expanding how customers access and deploy these capabilities through Microsoft's cloud and AI ecosystem.

## Connecting distributed infrastructure

As AI initiatives expand across enterprise environments, organisations need to use data and applications scattered across multiple locations.

Yet the networks connecting public clouds, private data centres, offices and partner environments are often fragmented and complex, creating barriers to effective AI deployment.

Lumen's extensive network and on-demand control capabilities provide Azure customers with simplified connectivity and a resilient, high-performance network foundation needed to operationalise AI workloads across distributed infrastructure.

"AI is reshaping where applications run and how organizations use and move data," says Katy Brown, Corporate Vice President, Americas Markets and Industries at Microsoft.

"Microsoft is committed to giving customers choice as they connect existing environments to Azure.

"Our work with Lumen is focused on helping customers align their broader network transformation with their Azure cloud and AI priorities, while taking advantage of Azure's native networking, security, scale and innovation."

We're building on a longstanding relationship to give customers a simpler, more resilient foundation for putting AI to work.

## Cloud-native networking expansion

Through expanded co-sell efforts, Microsoft and Lumen intend to extend joint account planning engagement around enterprise opportunities where network modernisation, Azure cloud platform migration and AI transformation converge.

The companies plan to identify opportunities to bring additional Lumen capabilities to Azure and Microsoft Marketplace over time.

"Enterprises are moving quickly to adopt AI, but many are still figuring out how to connect the data, applications and infrastructure behind it," says Ryan Asdourian, Chief Strategy and Marketing Officer at Lumen.

"Together with Microsoft, we're bringing cloud, network and AI planning together earlier and putting AI to work more effectively."

The expanded collaboration addresses several enterprise priorities for data centre and cloud connectivity.

These are:

- Connect distributed data for AI by linking enterprise sites, data centres and clouds to support Azure-based AI initiatives
- Simplify hybrid and multi-cloud networking through consistent policies and visibility across distributed environments
- Adapt as needs change by connecting new clouds, partners and applications without separate networking projects
- Enable resilient, high-performance network foundations for AI workloads across distributed infrastructure
- Align network transformation decisions earlier with Azure modernisation and AI deployment plans

## "Building on a longstanding relationship"

Alkira, a Lumen Connect solution available through Microsoft Marketplace, provides customers with an established purchasing option for cloud-native networking capabilities.

The solution enables enterprises to access Lumen's networking capabilities, streamlining procurement and deployment for organisations modernising their data centre and cloud infrastructure.

Katy elaborates on the collaboration on LinkedIn, writing: "We're building on a longstanding relationship to give customers a simpler, more resilient foundation for putting AI to work.

"I'm looking forward to seeing how customers build on this foundation as they prepare for the next generation of agentic applications."

Lumen and Microsoft will share additional details about the expanded collaboration as joint go-to-market plans progress throughout 2026.

## Microsoft's key partners in 2026

- Expanding co-selling collaboration with Microsoft to address enterprise AI connectivity challenges across distributed data centres, public clouds and partner environments. Lumen provides extensive network infrastructure and on-demand control capabilities that give Azure customers simplified connectivity and resilient, high-performance network foundations. The company intends to bring its full suite of cloud networking and application connectivity capabilities to Azure and Microsoft Marketplace.

- Serving as global launch partner for Microsoft 365 E7 and "Customer Zero" for Microsoft Agent 365, Insight tests, governs and scales enterprise AI agents internally while delivering agentic governance frameworks to clients. The technology integrator demonstrates how enterprises can deploy and manage AI infrastructure at scale across distributed data centre and cloud environments.

- Deepening a multi-decade infrastructure alliance to integrate Microsoft Azure Local, SQL Server vector-search capabilities and hybrid-cloud automation with Dell PowerEdge and PowerStore hardware. The partnership includes joint AI PC rollouts featuring Microsoft Copilot+ PCs, providing physical data centre infrastructure that requires the high-performance network connectivity and simplified hybrid-cloud networking Lumen addresses through its Azure collaboration.
